items.statement: Organic revenue growth guided at 13-17% for FY26 with acceleration expected from Q2

items.statement: Exit EBITDA margin expected upward of 10% by end of FY26
items.quote: Yes, So, next year’s end, the exit margin should be upward of 10% for sure.

items.statement: Long-term EBITDA margin target of 10-12% and beyond as scale increases

items.statement: Order book stands at US$504 million, up US$39 million sequentially as of March 2025

items.statement: Record order wins of INR 1,550 crore in Q4, more than twice Q3 level

items.statement: Q4 FY25 EBITDA margin at 9.5%, up 130 bps YoY; PAT margin at 3.9%
items.quote: In Q4, revenue grew 4% year-over-year, while EBITDA and PAT increased 21% and 48% Y-o-Y respectively. This translated into all -time high margins, EBITDA at 9.5% and PAT at 3.9%.

items.statement: FY25 EBITDA margin expanded to 8.9% from 2.5% in FY19; PAT improved from loss of INR 79 crore to INR 205 crore
items.quote: Since then, we have executed a multi-year turnaround. EBITDA margin expanded from 2.5% in FY’19 to 8.9% in FY ‘25, while PAT improved from a loss of INR 79 crore in FY’19 to INR 205 crore in FY ‘25.

items.statement: Demand for digital transformation, user experience and AI-driven solutions remains non-discretionary; AI hyperscaler capex projected at $1.6 trillion through 2029
items.quote: The demand for digital transformation, improved user experience and AI -driven solutions remains non -discretionary. The investment climate in AI remains robust.

items.statement: 80-90% of pipeline from top 300-400 customers; focus on large deals >$5-20M with hyperscalers, healthcare, airports, education
items.quote: So, 80% of our business is from larger customers. Close to 80% to 90% of our pipeline remains with our larger top 300 customers. And as we move forward, I believe 90% of our pipeline will continue with our top 300 to top 400 customers.

items.statement: Committed additional INR 100 crore to double India business; expanding Bengaluru Center of Excellence
items.quote: We have committed an additional INR 100 crore to double our India business and are expanding our Bengaluru (Bangalore) Center of Excellence.

items.statement: Inaugurated security operations center and data networking lab in Sydney
items.quote: Notably, we secured a large INR 90 crores order from a consumer electronics firm in APAC and inaugurated a state-of-the-art security operations center and data networking lab in Sydney.

items.statement: No concrete acquisition to announce at this time; pipeline exists but nothing materialized
items.quote: So, as I said, we continue to look at assets, continue to have into pipeline, but there is nothing concrete for me to say at this time.

items.statement: Working capital investment led to higher debt in Q4 due to revenue skewness and proactive supplier engagement; ROE 27% for FY25
items.quote: During the quarter, working capital investment led to higher debt, primarily driven by revenue skewness within the quarter and proactive supplier engagement. Despite that, we delivered a robust ROE of 27% for FY '25.

items.statement: CRISIL upgraded long-term rating to BBB+/Stable in March 2025; committed to capital-light model
items.quote: In recognition of our financial progress, CRISIL upgraded our long-term rating to BBB+/ Stable in March of 2025. We remain committed to a capital light model with disciplined capital deployment.

items.statement: Board proposed final dividend of 50% of INR 1 per share (face value INR 2) subject to approval
items.quote: To reward our shareholders, the Board has proposed a final dividend of 50% of INR 1 rupee per share on face value of INR 2, subject to approval.

items.statement: Strengthened leadership team and sales force by hiring talent from global GSIs and industry players; verticalized go-to-market
items.quote: This included verticalizing our business to better align with client needs, strengthening our leadership team and sales force by hiring talent from global GSIs and other leading industry players.

items.statement: Managed services grew $61 million sequentially in Q4, improving revenue predictability and margin visibility
items.quote: Our managed and maintenance services business grew $61 million sequentially, which improves revenue predictability and enhances margin visibility going forward.

items.statement: Macro uncertainty and tariff dynamics may cause cautious client decision-making in near term; monitoring evolving economic impact
items.quote: Whatever the economy impact in terms of right now the evolving economical impact where the few industries will do good and few industries like the manufacturing will emerge in the U.S. and all those things, those all will be accretive logically to us. It may take some time to ascertain because people are right now holding off some of the decisions.

items.statement: India data center capacity only 1 GW vs 4x US population; structural supply-demand imbalance represents long-term opportunity
items.quote: India has four times the U.S. population, yet only 1 Gigawatt of data center capacity, a fraction of U.S. levels, despite being the world's highest data consumer.

items.statement: 75% of revenues from US; own product revenue ~$100M with $45M from US; tariff impact on own products nominal at overall scale
items.quote: 75% of our revenues are in US, and if you see our revenues, it has three components. One is our on-ground services, Second is we sell the OEM products and the third is our own products.

items.statement: Average project execution timeline 9-12 months; managed services contracts 3-5 years
items.quote: So, our average project execution timeline are between anything between six months to two years. Right. So, depending upon what kind of orders we get. So, at an average it is, say, if you draw out an average of about 9 to 12 months’ time.

items.statement: Management guided for double-digit revenue growth in FY26 while remaining cautiously optimistic due to global trade and geopolitical uncertainties.
items.quote: Going forward, we anticipate double -digit revenue growth in financial year 2025, '26, while remaining cautiously optimistic, given the uncertainty from changes in global tax and trade policies, along with the geopolitical issues, which we continue to monitor very closely.

items.statement: Management maintained double-digit revenue growth guidance for FY26 but declined to specify a narrower range citing global uncertainties and tariff impacts not fully baked in.
items.quote: Mohit, I will have to say that we are maintaining double -digit guidance. While we see demand in the local market, you will appreciate that there are uncertainties in the global markets and the impact of tariffs is not completely baked in yet.

items.statement: Management sees demand continuing across all segments including residential, commercial, infra, data centers, and emerging segments like quick commerce.
items.quote: We are seeing demand and this demand is continuing from the segment, all the segments that we serve. So there is demand in residential realty, commercial reality infra-related segments in data centers.

items.quote: Our endeavor is definitely to sustain or better these margins and our cost optimization efforts are ongoing. That's the best I can share at this point in time.

items.quote: In terms of electrification, the eAxles, which are the largest components in the eAxle business, will stay within Bosch Limited and that's how it is.

items.quote: Between the old hospital and the new hospital, we believe we have room to grow and we have capacity to grow into it as well. So, we're not capacity constrained and there is an opportunity to grow into it.

items.statement: Rajarhat, Kolkata Phase 1 (350 beds) construction started; commissioning expected in ~30 months (near FY28); total projected 1,100 beds.
items.quote: So, as we talk about phase 1, we've already given an indication that it will take us at least 30 months as we 31 speak, from now, for this commissioning to happen. So, mostly it will be functional somewhere near FY28 when it comes to Rajarhat at the first phase of around 350 beds

items.statement: Expansion is measured and focused on strong presence cities; land parcels acquired in HSR and Bannerghatta (Bangalore) where inorganic options unavailable; inorganic tie-ups in Banashankari and Chamarajpet.
items.quote: We are doing a mix of both. It's that there are parts of Bangalore where we want to be present, but there are no inorganic opportunities available for us. So, we have to make our own. And thus, in HSR and in Bannerghatta, we have to buy land.

items.statement: Project finance loans at 80% debt for 15-25 year tenor will continue; other debt calibrated prudently; management avoids excessive leverage.
items.quote: Project finance loans are for a bit long term. So, we can't take decisions of not taking those loans basis our temporary cash distribution. Because these are going to be 15-25 years loan, which we cannot say that we will not take just because we have got a very large cash corpus now. So those loans, we will continue with that 80% debt.

items.statement: Blended interest cost ~8% for India borrowings (declining with T-bill moves); ~6-6.25% for Cayman borrowings.
items.quote: You can assume my interest cost of around 8%, which is actually coming down because of the movements in the T-bill on our overall borrowing for India and for the Cayman, you can take a rate of around 6 to 6.25%.

items.statement: No equity preferential issue planned currently; may consider in distant future if needed.
items.quote: There's no need for it right now. But, should the need come, we would look at it, but that's much in the future.

items.statement: Dividend funded entirely from Cayman cash reserves in a tax-efficient manner; debt raised separately for expansion.
items.quote: So, the dividend is coming from Cayman. So, our dividend policy is linked entirely around being able to monetize the Cayman cash reserve and do it in a more tax efficient manner. Raising debt is for expansion.

items.statement: Technology team attrition is 7%, considered highly impressive given location in Bangalore's startup hub.
items.quote: Our attrition so far has been 7% for the Technology team, which is, I have been told, highly impressive.

items.statement: Senior and middle-level doctor attrition is negligible; unique engagement model and in-house nursing/paramedical training programs (largest in private sector) support retention for expansions.
items.quote: We are fairly very good with our doctor engagements and especially our senior and middle level doctor engagements. We hardly have any attritions at that level.

items.statement: International expansion criteria: stable rule of law, established insurance penetration, high GDP per capita, existing track record of private healthcare assets; no frontier markets.
items.quote: It has to be a stable market with stable rule of law, an established insurance penetration and a mechanism to pay. It has to have a high purchasing power, essentially high GDP per capita. We are not looking to go into a frontier country.

items.statement: No macro slowdown anticipated in healthcare demand; Bangladesh revenue may decline further but already anticipated.
items.quote: A more slowdown from Bangladesh, whatever little revenue we've been getting there may drop even further. This we had anticipated. Above and beyond that, if you're asking about macro slowdown, those are very hard to predict, and healthcare is one of those things that are really not discretionary.

items.statement: Digital platform investments eliminate paper, enable remote ICU rounds, and drive efficiency; AI adoption will follow once tools stabilize; no beds added since 2016 yet revenue grew with industry.
items.quote: We have eliminated nearly all paper from all the departments. We've made it so that our doctors can get data instantly and they can do the rounds of the ICU in their house.

items.statement: Formally clarified to regulators no intention to pursue or invest in Spire Healthcare (UK) after media reports.
items.quote: As soon as there was that information in the media, we issued a clarification to the regulators in both markets that we had no intention of pursuing or making any offer or investment in Spire Healthcare.

items.statement: Long-term vision: 40 self-owned hospitals in 10 years considered reasonable; expansion pace conservative due to focus on return on capital/equity and realization half of peers.
items.quote: 40 hospitals in 10 years seems reasonable. Now, if we have as much of the footprint as Apollo, that's hard to tell because Apollo is also not going to sit still.

items.statement: MTF book target not less than INR1,000 crores in next 3 years
items.quote: Next 3 years, our MTF book will not be less than INR1,000 crores.

items.statement: Retail client target 2 lakh to 2.5 lakh in next 3 years
items.quote: Retail clients so number, we are targeting 2 lakh to 2.5 lakh clients in next 3 years.

items.statement: Insurance distribution premium target 3-figure (INR100+ crores) this year, 30-35% YoY growth
items.quote: Our internal target is, we should touch 3-figure premium this year. So that is, again, 30% to 35% jump on year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Mutual fund AUM target at least 100% growth YoY this financial year
items.quote: Our aggressive target is on mutual fund AUM should at least grow by 100% this financial year on year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Prop trading bottom in Q4 FY25, sequential improvement expected from Q1 FY26
items.quote: We believe the fourth quarter should be the bottom for the prop numbers and from all the things that.

items.statement: Retail client base grew 30% YoY to 46,252; institutional clients up 250% to 137
items.quote: In retail clients, we have seen a jump of 30% on year-on-year basis. Last year, we were having 35,380 clients. And this year, we are having more than 46,252 clients.

items.statement: BSE options market share increased from 3.5% to 5.8%
items.quote: BSE options, we have seen a major growth like last year, our market share was 3.5%. This year, our market share is 5.8% in BSE options.

items.statement: MTF book grew 330% YoY from INR72 crores to INR239 crores
items.quote: Our book has increased by more than 330%. It was at INR72 crores at the end of financial year 2024, this year we've closed the book at INR239 crores.

items.statement: Prop trading returns dropped due to regulatory changes and fair value loss of INR42 crores in Q4
items.quote: Because of the market having a negative sentiment in the last quarter on our investment book that we had of all the equities in other companies that we hold, we had to book a fair value loss of INR42 crores.

items.statement: Strategy shifted from volume-based to margin-based due to higher margin regime
items.quote: Earlier, it was volume-based, now they are better margin based. So now we are not trading much, we are relying on better margins.

items.statement: Opened 3 new retail branches in Connaught Place Delhi, Kolkata, Ahmedabad in last 6 months
items.quote: Share India is also enhancing the visibility by opening the branches in the prominent locations at the different cities like we have recently opened a branch in Connaught Place in Delhi. It's a pure-play retail branch, and we opened a branch in the main land of Kolkata, Ahmedabad.

items.statement: NBFC branches increased from 61 to 80; client base reduced from 69,000 to 52,000
items.quote: As far as NBFC is concerned, we have increased branches from 61 to 80 branches now. Client base has a bit reduced from 69,000 to 52,000.

items.statement: NBFC book shifted to 50% secured SME loans from unsecured personal loans; book size flat at INR260 crores
items.quote: We have shifted our focus on -- more on secured SME loans rather than only doing unsecured personal loans. So, book size, we have maintained.

items.statement: AI-based retail trading product with uTrade to launch by end of Q3 FY26
items.quote: You will see AI is recommending the stocks, AI will be doing the technical charts. You can choose your stock through AI. So AI will play a major part in our product which we'll roll out in end of third quarter.

items.statement: Retail algo trading via open APIs from August 1; target 'think Algo, think Share India'
items.quote: SEBI has allowed retail for Algo, which from first of August, retail can also carpet in Algo. We want to make this Algo thing for Share India, like think Algo, think Share India.

items.statement: Silverleaf Securities (HFT firm) acquisition expected to complete this year; EPS accretive
items.quote: So it will be an EPS accretive acquisition. And as and when the acquisition happens, we can't disclose as where, but fiscal year, it would be an EPS accretive is what I can state officially right now.

items.statement: SEBI removed intraday position limits; end-of-day delta-based limit raised to INR1,500 crores; gross intraday monitoring INR10,000 crores each side
items.quote: Now Delta base will provide an additional advantage because it will be considered as a net position so that the limit would be much, much higher. And the limit of INR500 crores also will be revised to INR1,500 crores on delta based at end of the day.

items.statement: SEBI allowed 2 weekly expiries (Tue/Thu) for NSE and BSE; MSE must develop cash market first
items.quote: Yesterday, there was one more circular from SEBI that has clarified we will have 2 weekly expiry for multi exchanges, that is one expiry per exchange for weekly contracts.

items.statement: Fair value loss of INR42 crores in Q4 due to investment book markdown
items.quote: So fair value numbers, it is because of the investments in our book and because last quarter, the stock prices have gone down, so we have to book some fair value loss. That number is around INR42 crores.

items.statement: NBFC unsecured loan trouble in rural personal loans; shifting to secured SME loans to mitigate
items.quote: Client base has a bit reduced from 69,000 to 52,000 because even in NBFC, we have seen a trouble in 3 quarters for the -- especially for the personal loans in the villages and the side.

items.statement: Consolidated revenue INR1,449 crores, down 2.5% YoY; PAT INR328 crores, down 23% YoY
items.quote: Coming to the consolidated full financial year 2024, '25, total revenue from the operation was INR1,449 crores, showing a year-on-year decline of 2.5%. Profit before tax and profit after tax were INR431 crores and INR328 crores, respectively, representing approximately 23% decrease in both on year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Consolidated net worth exceeded INR2,300 crores
items.quote: Consolidated net worth for the year has jumped to INR2,300 crores-plus.

items.statement: No unrealized losses unaccounted as of March 31; conservative accounting maintained
items.quote: As of today, there are no unrealized losses that have not been accounted.

items.statement: NBFC book size maintained at INR260 crores with shift to secured lending
items.quote: Book size is broadly same because INR260 crores and INR260 crores.

items.statement: Insurance distribution premium INR75 crores in FY25, up 35-40% YoY
items.quote: Insurance is doing great last year, insurance rate, INR75 crores premium. This is like 35% to 40% jump on an year-over-year basis.

items.statement: Standalone EBITDA margin guidance of 14% plus for FY26
items.quote: as we said, it's going to be around 14% is the guidance stand-alone.

items.statement: Standalone revenue growth target of 20% YoY without new projects
items.quote: Standalone operation, 20% growth year -on-year without these 2 projects are a complete possibility.

items.statement: Total capex of INR 100-150 crores for FY26 including Khurdha and JV
items.quote: Roughly INR 100 crores to INR 150 crores will be the capex roughly for FY '26 in total?

items.statement: Khurdha project capex of INR 40-50 crores in FY26, rest in FY27
items.quote: Khurdha, we'll be spending around INR 40 crores to INR 50 crores this year, and the rest will be spent in the next year.

items.statement: Regular maintenance capex of INR 90 crores with INR 55 crores cash outflow in FY26
items.quote: we will take up a capex of close to INR 90 crores, which will spill into FY '27 also.

items.statement: Khurdha DBM brick plant commissioning by end of FY28, 35% utilization in year 1
items.quote: in FY '28, we are going to start the Khurdha plant, where almost from the same time, the same year, even though mid of the year we start, but we will be almost 35% of the capacity utiliz ation in the year 1

items.quote: FY '29, it starts delivering in FY '29. Harssh Shah: FY '29, the JV with Marvel? Arasu Shanmugam: Yes. I mean that means what? It will start somewhere in the FY’28. So the H2 of September

items.statement: Visakhapatnam magnesia carbon brick plant ramped up to 2,400 tonnes/month
items.quote: after August '24, we started supplying around 400 tonnes per month, something like that. So... Amit Agarwal: 2,400 tonne.

items.quote: casting flux, yes, they are just on the level of now only 400 tonne month level, but we have the potential to go up to 1,500 tonnes.

items.statement: Non-ferrous segment revenue of INR 8-10 crores in FY25, targeting INR 200 crores at full ramp-up
items.quote: FY '24, if you look at there was no sales from non -ferrous sector. And this year, we have close to INR 8 crores to INR 10 crores

items.statement: Cast house refractory (iron) targeting INR 25-30 crores revenue in 3 years
items.quote: we are anywhere looking at somewhere like INR 25 crores to INR 30 crores revenues through this product line.

items.statement: New non-ferrous/cement project expected to deliver 20%+ EBITDA margin, DBM bricks 29-30%
items.quote: the one project what we are talking about for non -ferrous, cement and other market is expected to deliver not less than 20% on EBITDA margin. But whereas on the D BM, it is even will go as high as 29% to 30%.

items.statement: Domestic standalone business grew 27% in Q4 and 20% for full year FY25
items.quote: Our domestic business recorded a robust 27% year -on-year growth in FY '25 quarter 4 and a 20% increase for the full year, reaching INR 721 crores.

items.statement: German foundry market remains difficult but April showed good month; hoping for infrastructure/military investment boost
items.quote: We had a good -- very good month in April. But obviously, that's for next year. But generally speaking, it's a fair statement that the competitor has made. It's a very difficult position in Foundry

items.statement: Fused magnesia power cost increases expected, planning to pass through to customers
items.quote: fused magnesia as far as is concerned, there are some power cost increase from the places where the source we are getting. So we are expecting that. But by that time, we are also expecting to cover it up with some kind of price increase from our customers

items.statement: Domestic revenue share increased to 72% in FY25 from 67% in FY24
items.quote: The domestic market now contributes 72% of our stand -alone revenue in FY '25, up from 67% in FY '24.

items.statement: Magnesia carbon brick customers increased from 9-10 sites to 17 sites
items.quote: we have acquired new customers where TTM. I mean earlier, it used to be 9, 10 sites, now it has become 17.

items.statement: DBM brick market highly concentrated with only 2-3 players including IFGL, enabling better pricing
items.quote: we are going to be in a market where a number of players are going to be maximum 3, and we become 1 among 3. So we will have a better negotiating abilities in this market.

items.statement: US tariff protections under Trump expected to benefit domestic steel and IFGL's US operations
items.quote: In recent policy direction from President Trump, emphasizing Make in America and proposing tariff protections, it is expected to be positive for the domestic manufacturing and improve the steel production landscape.

items.statement: Working capital increased due to strategic stock build-up at Vizag and early receipts at Rourkela, expected to normalize
items.quote: it's because of the some stock we have built up strategically and we have new operation added, Vizag operation. So there are some stock and some amount of stock, we say, we have received a bit early than expected.

items.statement: Consolidated debt INR 32.99 crores, cash INR 169.35 crores as of March 2025
items.quote: we had a debt of INR 32.99 crores with a strong balance sheet. Cash and cash equivalents stood at INR 169.35 crores on a consolidated basis as on March '25.

items.statement: Dividend of INR 7 per share (70% payout) and 1:1 bonus issue approved for FY25
items.quote: The Board of Directors has recommended a dividend of INR 7 per equity share, including a final dividend of INR 1 per equity share of face value INR 10, representing a 70% payout for FY 2024-25

items.statement: Bonus issue in ratio 1:1 approved subject to shareholder and regulatory approvals
items.quote: The proposed bonus is in the ratio of 1:1, meaning 1 bonus equity share of INR 10 each will be issued for every 1 fully paid equity share held.

items.statement: Mihir Bajoria appointed as Managing Director, replacing James McIntosh
items.quote: As Managing Director, Mihir Bajoria will perform the same function as I had during my tenure as Managing Director of the company.

items.statement: European foundry market remains very difficult; recovery dependent on government infrastructure/military spending
items.quote: the comments of the other competitors is absolutely true, and we also share that it's a very difficult situation.

items.statement: FY26 revenue growth expected to be double-digit across all three business verticals
items.quote: We expect all the three engines to fire. Some stronger, some weaker, but all the three engines would be on a double-digit growth.

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA margin expected in low 30s, mid-term target mid-30s
items.quote: We expect our EBITDA margins to be in the low 30s in FY '26. The midterm target remains in the mid- 30s with scale.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 revenue growth muted, growth weighted towards second half
items.quote: We expect Q1 FY '26 to be muted with the growth being way towards the second half due to the shipment timings and customer inventory adjustments.

items.statement: FY25 capex Rs 314 crore, FY26 capex expected around Rs 350 crore
items.quote: I think our sense is that it will still be in the range of around Rs. 350 crore as a total CAPEX for FY '26.

items.statement: Investing in NJ Bio bioconjugation expansion and Oligo CGMP facility validation by end Q3 FY26
items.quote: We have initiated capital expenditure in the U.S. t o expand NJ Bio's bioconjugation infrastructure in line with our growth aspirations, as we work to meet some of our customer requirements. During our last calls also, we did mention Oligo facility of CGMP is on track for validation by end of Q3 FY '25-'26

items.statement: Phase-3 pipeline expanded to 9 molecules from 2, one molecule with 4 intermediates entering commercial production
items.quote: Notably, our Phase-3 pipeline has been maintained at 9 active molecules. Four of our intermediate projects pertaining to one of the important molecules expected to enter into commercial production.

items.statement: RFQ pipeline expanding with balanced mix of existing and new customers including late-stage RFQs
items.quote: Our RFQ pipeline continues to expand, featuring a more balanced mix of existing and new customers as well as late stage RFQs, which adds visibility to our new integrated global pharma CDMO platforms identity.

items.statement: Pharma CDMO grew 18% YoY in FY25 driven by late-stage project expansion
items.quote: Our Pharma CDMO segment continued to be the key growth driver, growing 18% year-on-year, supported by expansion in late- stage projects.

items.statement: Specialty Chemicals recovery in H2 FY25, clear recovery trend into FY26
items.quote: We see a clear recovery trend heading into FY '26, although on a weak base, FY '26 is poised to deliver further growth as we move up in the value chain with existing customers and expand into new areas.

items.statement: ADC and oligonucleotide platforms seeing healthy RFQ expansion and cross-selling opportunities
items.quote: We continue to see healthy expansion in RFQs across all modalities, particularly in late phase and integrated ADC opportunities, including payload linker and bioconjugation.

items.statement: FY25 EBITDA margin 34%, Q4 FY25 adjusted EBITDA margin 31.3%
items.quote: For the full year FY '25, we ended the year with 9% year -on-year revenue growth and with an EBITDA margins of 34%, in line with what we had communicated earlier.

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA margin dip to low 30s due to business mix, operating leverage, NJ Bio integration, inventory de-stocking
items.quote: There is also an NJ Bio which we are integrating. And that is a fast growth acquisition for us. It does come with a lower EBITDA than the average EBITDA for the business. So, there are actually multiple aspects.

items.statement: High-tech fast-growing modalities contribution expected to double over next five years
items.quote: Contribution from high- tech fast - growing modalities is expected to double over the next five years.

items.statement: ADC dual payload capability (Camptothecin and Oristatin) with integrated linker, payload, conjugation via NJ Bio
items.quote: Our dual value proposition in both Camptothecin-based and Oristatin based creates a very rare payload depth among global CDMOs, the integration of linker synthesis, payload supplies and conjugation via NJ Bio further underscores Cohance's pivotal role in upcoming late phase and commercial ADC programs.

items.statement: Added R&D team of 500+ scientists, facilities in Genome Valley Hyderabad and Princeton New Jersey
items.quote: We have augmented R&D to expand to a team of 500 plus scientists and added the facility in Genome Valley in Hyderabad and in Princeton, New Jersey.

items.statement: USFDA inspection at Nacharam site successful with EIR VAI classification, Jaggaiahpet API Unit-I cleared EU inspection
items.quote: USFDA inspections at our Nacharam site concluded successfully and we received an EIR with VAI classification. Our Jaggaiahpet API Unit-I cleared EU inspection recently.

items.statement: Commercial molecules expanded to 16 from 10, multiple large global innovator customers added
items.quote: We have expanded the commercial molecules to 16 from 10. We have expanded the late Phase III molecules pipeline to 9 from 2. We have built pipelines with higher RFPs from a wider customer base, including large global innovative pharma companies.

items.statement: Large innovator partner of 30+ years shared ADC RFQ, growing interest from other large innovators in ADC and oligo platforms

items.statement: Generated Rs 3.6 billion free cash flow, net cash balance sheet with Rs 2.9 billion cash
items.quote: We generated Rs. 3.6 billion in free cash flow maintaining a net cash balance sheet with Rs. 2.9 billion in cash and bank balance.

items.statement: Net cash position maintained despite $8.1 billion strategic investments for Sapala and NJ Bio acquisitions
items.quote: This is despite the strategic investment of $8.1 billion for the acquisition of Sapala and NJ Bio.

items.statement: Acquired NJ Bio and Sapala Organics to expand ADC and oligonucleotide capabilities, programmatic M&A approach to scale niche capabilities

items.statement: Built high-quality leadership team, engaged strategic advisors from leading global CMOs, added 100+ scientists via NJ Bio acquisition
items.quote: With the acquisition of NJ Bio, not only we got a business, we got capability, but we also added about 100 plus scientists. And as a science driven company, we were really excited with what NJ Bio brings, and we will continue to invest in expanding there.

items.statement: Vision of $1 billion integrated technology-driven CDMO revenue by 2030
items.quote: We remain focused on our vision of $1 billion global revenue by 2030, which is primarily driven by a diversified growth strategy built on three key pillars.

items.statement: FY25 revenue $335 million with 34% EBITDA margin
items.quote: We have created a $335 million integrated technology-led platform revenue company, FY '25 performer with EBITDA margin of 34%, reflecting a very disciplined execution.

items.statement: Inventory de-stocking in some commercial molecules, customers pausing orders for FY26
items.quote: there is an inventory de- stocking that is there in the business as customers have come back and said that for a few commercial molecules they do hold the inventory, and they are looking at pausing for FY '26

items.statement: BD teams established internationally in US, EU, and Asia (primarily Japan)
items.quote: We have also found BD teams internationally in U.S., EU, and in Asia, primarily Japan.

items.statement: Named among World's Best Companies for Sustainable Growth 2025, received SBTi validation for GHG emission reduction targets
items.quote: We have been named among the "World's Best Companies for Sustainable Growth 2025" by Times and Statista magazine. And we received SBTi validation, which is the science-based target initiative validation for our GHG, which is greenhouse gas emission reduction targets.

items.statement: FY26 expected to be a year of acceleration with increased contribution from high-margin gaming business, further strengthening profitability
items.quote: As we look ahead into the coming year, FY '26 is poised to be a year of acceleration with increased contribution from high-margin gaming business, expecting to further strengthen our profitability.

items.statement: FY25 gaming EBITDA margin at 20%, Q4 FY25 gaming EBITDA margin at 21.4%
items.quote: Our gaming EBITDA margins stood at 20% as well as generated healthy operating cash, reinforcing our intent to focus on core gaming business going ahead.

items.quote: So I think this year, we are surely going to double down our capital investments towards that segment.

items.quote: The EBITDA loss that you actually see is predominantly because of our NH7 Pune cancellation and the Freaks4U EBITDA hits that are there.

items.quote: It would be very close to INR300 crores, between INR280 crores and INR300 crores. Yes.
