items.statement: 4 vessels on long-term contracts, 2 on spot market (Seamec III, Princess), 1 barge seasonal (7 months/year)
items.quote: 4 vessels are on long-term contracts, and will be running equally among all contracts, all quarters going forward. However, one caveat during the year, some of our vessels will go for dry dock.

items.statement: L&T PRP-VII contract $101 million consortium; Seamec share ~$30-31 million completed over two seasons; PRP-VIII extension signed
items.quote: we have won a contract of $101 million, but this was in consortium with Porsche, Subsea, Singapore. And our share out of this contract was somewhere around US$30 million US$31 million.

items.statement: Swordfish deployed to Aramco Saudi Arabia; opportunities in Middle East from Aramco and ADNOC but limited vessel availability
items.quote: Swordfish is now going to Ar amco which is the oil major for Saudi Arabia. And one of our vessels Seamec III has already made its entry in the KG Basin on the East Coast where we are right now working for Hardy oil.

items.statement: Targets minimum 50% EBITDA growth excluding ESOP cost for next year.
items.quote: A minimum growth of EBITDA of 50% excluding ESOP cost. That's the very, very first target.

items.statement: Aims for at least 300 bps EBITDA percentage improvement next year.
items.quote: We want to increase the quality of our revenues. With that, at least 300 basis points of EBITDA percentage improvement.

items.statement: Aerospace revenue target for FY26 is at least 35% growth.
items.quote: Starting by aerospace, I will say that our target for Fiscal Year '26 is at least 35% growth in revenues.

items.statement: Defense expects growth rate of about 75% moving forward.
items.quote: And right now we are on a very strong growth path. And we expect the growth to be at a rate of about 75% moving forward and also a similar focus on the bottom line also.

items.statement: Defense order book reaching about Rs. 1,800 crores.
items.quote: And our order books are now reaching about Rs. 1,800 crores.

items.statement: ESAI order book close to Rs. 600 crores plus.
items.quote: We are close to Rs. 600 crores plus of order books with us.

items.statement: ESAI is doing a growth of more than 60%.
items.quote: We are doing a growth of 60%, more than 60%.

items.statement: Aims to improve EBITDA margins by about 300 bps each year.
items.quote: We intend to improve our EBITDA margins by about 300 bps each year.

items.statement: Aims to achieve average 24% EBITDA in next 2 to 3 years.
items.quote: With effecti ve execution of product-led strategy, by FY ‘28, the Company aims to invert its current revenue mix of 80% service revenue and 20% product revenue, which will be the key driver for non -linear margin- led growth, with the aim and objective of achieving an average of 24% EBITDA in the next 2 to 3 years

items.statement: Phase-1 facility will cost Rs. 250 crores; Phase-1A Rs. 120 crores.
items.quote: This facility of Phase-1 would cost Rs. 250 crores. And the first Phase-1A of it would cost Rs. 120 crores, which would be mostly through internal funding.

items.statement: Phase-1A CAPEX including building and equipment Rs. 100 crores to Rs. 120 crores, mostly internal accruals.
items.quote: See, as Dr. SRN explained, what we have on the radar, and which is under development where the plan is at an approval stage is Phase-1A where the CAPEX including the building as well as the equipment is going to be anywhere between Rs. 100 crores to Rs. 120 crores. Of which most of it, our objective is that most of it should be through internal accruals.

items.statement: Defense production revenue expected to double in FY26 from Rs. 196 crores.
items.quote: This year FY ‘25 was around Rs. 196 crores. We are talking about probably doubling it in FY ‘26.

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA margin at least 17% average.
items.quote: But I am saying profit after adjusting to EBITDA because we have a huge cost on ESOPs, after adjusting our EBITDA still can be around 50% growth from the current level, and PAT will be proportional and EBITDA margin will be at least at 17% average.

items.statement: FY26 ESOP cost expected around Rs. 50 crores to Rs. 60 crores.
items.quote: Around Rs. 50 crores to Rs. 60 crores.

items.statement: Effective tax rate expected at 26% at Company level.
items.quote: So, 26% is effective tax rate we can expect at the Company level.

items.statement: Management expects to sustain current recruitment billing growth if economy grows at 6-6.5% and no major incidents occur
items.quote: If the economy continues to grow at 6-6.5% and if there's no major sort of incident or episode, then we will try and sustain this kind of growth rate at least.

items.statement: Jeevansathi aims to break even in FY26 while continuing 20-25% growth
items.quote: In Jeevansathi we'll try to break even this year as well. But at the same time, we would want to continue to grow at 20-25%.

items.statement: 99Acres will prioritize market share gains over near-term profitability if revenue growth lags
items.quote: Now if revenue growth is solid, then it's not as if we will lose money, we would want to make money. But if revenue growth lags by a couple of quarters, we'll still go for share.

items.statement: Standalone operating margin was 34% in Q4 FY25 and 37% for full year FY25
items.quote: Operating profits at a standalone level grew by 3% YOY to Rs. 231 crores and the operating margins stood at 34%.

items.statement: Recruitment operating margin was 54% in Q4 FY25 and 56% for full year FY25
items.quote: The operating profit improved by 8% YOY to Rs. 278 crores and the operating profit margin was 54%.

items.statement: 99Acres reduced operating losses by 31% to Rs. 48 crores in FY25
items.quote: Operating losses reduced by 31% to Rs. 48 crores in FY25 vs Rs. 69 crores in FY24.

items.statement: Jeevansathi reduced operating losses by 76% to Rs. 2 crores in Q4 FY25
items.quote: Operating losses reduced on a year-on-year basis by 76% to Rs. 2 crores.

items.statement: Shiksha operated at break-even level in Q4 FY25 and full year FY25
items.quote: The business was at a break-even level in terms of operating profit and generated cash from operations of Rs. 16 crores in Q4 of FY25.

items.statement: Standalone billings grew 19% YoY to Rs. 984 crores in Q4 FY25 and 15% to Rs. 2,882 crores in FY25
items.quote: For the full year FY25, in the standalone business, billings were Rs. 2,882 crores, a YOY growth of 15%.

items.statement: Recruitment billings grew 18% to Rs. 740 crores in Q4 FY25 and 15% to Rs. 2,158 crores in FY25
items.quote: For FY25 as a whole, in the recruitment business, billings grew by 15% to Rs. 2,158 crores.

items.statement: 99Acres billings grew 22% to Rs. 160 crores in Q4 FY25 and 17% to Rs. 451 crores in FY25
items.quote: For the full year, billing growth was 17% at Rs. 451 crore.

items.statement: Jeevansathi billings grew 24% to Rs. 32 crores in Q4 FY25 and 31% to Rs. 111 crores in FY25
items.quote: In full year FY25, billings grew by 31% to Rs. 111 crores.

items.statement: Shiksha billings grew 16% to Rs. 52 crores in Q4 FY25 and 14% to Rs. 162 crores in FY25
items.quote: In the full year, billing in Shiksha was Rs. 162 crores, a YOY growth of 14%.

items.statement: JobSpeak index showed muted movement in Q4 FY25 reflecting moderate hiring environment
items.quote: The JobSpeak index showed muted movement in Q4 FY25, reflecting a moderate hiring environment.

items.statement: Recruitment billing growth was broad-based across Tech/IT/BPM (17%), GCCs (19%), Other Sectors (19%), Recruitment Consultants (15%)
items.quote: The billing growth rate in Q4 was broad-based across all segments. Tech, IT services and BPM combined grew by 17%, GCCs by 19%, Other Sectors by 19% and the Recruitment Consultant segment by 15%.

items.statement: Niche businesses IIM Jobs, Naukri Gulf, Naukri Fast Forward grew billings 43%, 26%, 18% YoY in Q4 FY25
items.quote: Our niche and adjacent businesses such as IIM Jobs, Naukri Gulf and Naukri Fast Forward have all continued a good growth trajectory in Q4 FY25 as well, with year-on-year billings up by 43%, 26% and 18% respectively.

items.statement: Naukri served over 128,000 corporate customers in FY25
items.quote: On the recruiter side, the Naukri business served over 128,000 corporate customers in FY25.

items.statement: 99Acres broker/channel partner segment grew faster than developers; live new project listings up 11%, resale/rental listings up 27% in Q4
items.quote: The broker and channel partner segment grew faster than developers. The number of live new project listings on the platform grew 11% in Q4 and the live resale plus rental listings from brokers grew by 27% in Q4.

items.statement: GCCs contributed 16-17% of recruitment India B2B billings in FY25
items.quote: GCCs contributed around 16-17% of recruitment India B2B billings in FY25.

items.statement: Shiksha domestic education grew 26% YoY while study abroad declined 16% YoY in FY25
items.quote: Within the Shiksha business, the domestic education business grew by 26% year-on-year and the study abroad business declined by 16% year-on-year.

items.statement: Marketing spend increased in Q4 FY25 for both Naukri (IPL advertising) and 99Acres (share gain strategy)
items.quote: We upped our spend in both the recruitment business and in the real estate business in Q4.

items.statement: Employee cost increased 250 bps in Q4 FY25 due to higher variable payouts linked to billing growth and AI talent investments
items.quote: Part of the bump you see is because we met our targets in all our businesses. And therefore, the variable payout was a little higher than expected.

items.statement: AI investments driving server purchases and hiring of expensive AI/ML talent across businesses
items.quote: Because of AI investments, we need to buy more servers, we need to hire more people and these people are not cheap, they're expensive.

items.statement: Naukri platform hosts 106 million resumes with 22,000 daily additions in Q4 FY25
items.quote: On the job seeker side, our Naukri platform now hosts around 106 million resumes and added an average of 22,000 resumes daily in Q4 of FY25.

items.statement: AI-driven improvements delivered 15-20% YoY improvement in job seeker engagement and recruiter productivity metrics
items.quote: New AI models for job search and recommendations have driven a 15-20% year-on-year improvement in job seeker engagement.

items.statement: Investment portfolio 2019-20 vintage fund targets 18-19% post-carry IRR as decent, above 25% as excellent
items.quote: The post-carry, post-expense IRR for the 2019-20 vintage fund, anything above 18-19% would be decent, above 25% would be excellent.

items.statement: Board proposed final dividend of Rs. 18 pre-split (Rs. 3.6 post-split); total FY25 dividend Rs. 30 pre-split (Rs. 6 post-split), up 36% YoY
items.quote: The board has proposed a final dividend of Rs. 18 per share pre-split or Rs. 3.6 per share post-split. Along with the interim dividend, the total dividend of FY25 is Rs. 30 per share pre-split or Rs. 6 per share post-split, a 36% year-on-year increase in dividend payout.

items.statement: Shareholders approved new fund of ~Rs. 1,000 crores for strategic investments
items.quote: Recently, we got the shareholders' approval for another fund for about Rs. 1,000 crore rupees.

items.statement: Headcount stood at 6,065 as of March 2025; AI team grown 5-6x over 4-5 years to ~100 people
items.quote: The headcount of the company as of March 2025 was 6,065 people.

items.statement: Management highlights uncertainty from global tariffs and economic conditions; takes quarter-by-quarter approach
items.quote: There is a lot of uncertainty, as we all know, in the world around us. It's very hard to predict what's going to happen even next week, forget about what's going to happen, in the full year.

items.statement: Targets 30-35% sales growth in FY26, aiming for Rs 10,000 crore
items.quote: We expect to achieve at least a growth of 30% plus this year, which is in FY'26, which we aimed to do in FY'25 and move towards the goal of reaching the 5-digit sales number by FY'26.

items.statement: Plans to launch at least half of 18.56 msf pipeline in FY26, optimistic scenario crosses double-digit msf
items.quote: In this financial year alone, which is FY 26, if everything works well, we will be able to launch at least half of this pipeline. In a more optimistic scenario, we can cross the double digit in terms of million square feet launches.

items.statement: Expects 20% increase in project completions to 5.5 msf in FY26
items.quote: We expect to also increase this by at least 20% next year with 5.5 million square feet in FY '26.

items.statement: Contracts, manufacturing and retail revenue to grow at least 10% with enhanced profitability in FY26
items.quote: And we expect to grow at least 10% with enhanced profitability next year.

items.statement: Targets at least 10% operating cash flow growth in FY26
items.quote: We should aim to achieve at least 10% growth on our operating cash flow.

items.statement: Future inflow from sold plus unsold units is Rs 24,120 crore with cost to complete of Rs 13,580 crore, generating Rs 10,500 crore marginal cash flow
items.quote: As on 31st March, from all our completed and ongoing projects, we expect Rs. 24,120 crore of future inflow from all sold plus unsold units. Against that, our cost to complete is expected to be Rs. 13,580 crore, thereby generating marginal cash flow of Rs. 10,500 crore at project level.

items.statement: Forthcoming projects of 19.3 msf expected to generate additional Rs 7,200 crore marginal cash flow over next 6-8 quarters
items.quote: Along with this, our forthcoming projects of 19.3 million square feet expected to be launched over next 6 to 8 quarters, shall generate another Rs. 7,200 crore of marginal cash flow.

items.statement: Project-level EBITDA margin of 33% on Rs 15,873 crore balance revenue to recognize from sold units
items.quote: Our current balance revenue to recognize from already sold unit as on 31st March is Rs. 15,873 crore which is Sobha share, and we expect project level EBITDA margin of 33%.

items.statement: New project EBITDA margins expected closer to 40%
items.quote: Current sales, again EBITDA margin should be now in the new one should be closer to 40% is what our sense is.

items.statement: Corporate overheads (ex-sales & marketing) estimated at 7-8%, plus interest embedded in projects
items.quote: But otherwise if you take that out, then it should be reasonably constant that should be about 7% to 8%, but only the other overheads non sales and marketing and there would be a small percentage of interest also that would be embedded.

items.statement: Gross debt Rs 1,131 crore, cash balance Rs 1,761 crore, net debt negative for first time
items.quote: We ended the year with a gross debt of Rs. 1131 crore and a strong cash balance of Rs. 1761 crore. And first time in history we are right now net debt negative.

items.statement: Average borrowing cost reduced to 9.12% in Q4 FY25
items.quote: Our average borrowing cost has also started come down. It was 9.12% in Q4.

items.statement: Completed Rs 2,000 crore rights issue, received Rs 1,996 crore by March 31, balance Rs 4 crore received in April
items.quote: In FY '25, we have completed Rs. 2,000 crore size right issue successfully and received Rs. 1996 crore and balance Rs. 4 crore was outstanding as on 31st March. Part of that we have received in April.

items.statement: Spent Rs 945 crore on business development in FY25 vs Rs 382 crore in FY24, added ~10.5 msf developable area worth ~Rs 15,000 crore
items.quote: We have in this overall business development that we have done , we have added about close to 10.5 million square feet last year, which would have the overall value should be about Rs. 15000 crores.

items.statement: New business development focus on Bangalore, NCR, Hyderabad, Mumbai; opportunistic approach with no fixed deployment guidance
items.quote: The kind of opportunity that we can really pursue now is slightly wider. I do not have a clear guidance in terms of how much we could deploy, but the fact is that we are in a good position to capture any good opportunity that can come by.

items.statement: Launched 8.76 msf across 8 projects in 4 cities in FY25, highest ever
items.quote: In FY'25', we launched 8.76 million square feet over 8 projects in 4 cities. This is our highest are a of launches till date.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 launches: Greater Noida (0.7 msf), Marina One Bangalore (0.92 msf), another Bangalore project (0.6 msf); Q2: Gurgaon commercial, Bangalore (0.5 msf + 0.3 msf), Trivandrum (0.25 msf); total 3-3.5 msf in H1
items.quote: Both first 2 quarters together, I think we should be looking at about 3-3.5 million square feet.

items.statement: Full year FY26 launch guidance 8-9 msf with ~40% in NCR, 15% Bangalore, 10% Chennai, 5% Mumbai
items.quote: From a launches point of view, I think roughly about 40% plus will be in NCR, which is in Greater Noida and Gurgaon. And roughly about 15% is in Bangalore and about 10% is in Chennai, 5% in Mumbai and rest of the locations carry the remaining.

items.statement: Residential demand steady across Bangalore, NCR, Kerala; Bangalore end-user driven, NCR has investor component, Kerala NRI-driven
items.quote: The residential demand environment seems to be steady at the moment, despite witnessing certain global political and economic uncertainties that have hit us in the past few months in this year.

items.statement: Like-to-like price increases likely to be inflation-led going forward; Bangalore and NCR pricing stabilized, Kerala new launches at higher prices with good interest
items.quote: like- to-like pricing probably we might not increase the price as we had done in the last couple of years. S o hence we can see a steady pricing environment. So going forward probably in the next few years, we would probably see an inflation-led price increases

items.statement: Core product remains 2-4 bedroom apartments; large projects have good mix; pricing methodology protects margins and ensures sales completion ahead of project lifecycle
items.quote: Our core bread and butter business has always been a 3 -bedroom, 2, 3 and 4 bedroom apartments and that continues to be the case even in the future and particularly the large projects, we have good mix of products.

items.statement: Gurgaon sales strategy avoids short-term investor bookings to protect cash flow; premium pricing filters out speculative demand
items.quote: One of the things that we have seen is any short -term investor led bookings would might, there is a possibility that it might lead to cash flow issues in case of any steadiness or slowdown in the market, that we would definitely like to avoid.

items.statement: Real estate collections grew 10% YoY to Rs 6,184 crore operational cash flow in FY25; Q4 collections crossed Rs 1,500 crore, highest ever
items.quote: In FY '25 total operational cash flow was Rs. 6,184 crore. Real estate collection grew up by 10% as compared to last year, FY'24, and contributed 89% to overall operation cash flow. In Q4, real estate collection crossed Rs. 1,500 crore, which is highest ever.

items.statement: Average realization Rs 13,412/sq ft in FY25, up 23% YoY
items.quote: The average realization stood at 13,412 per square feet, which is higher by about 23% as compared to FY'24.

items.statement: FY25 total real estate sales Rs 6,277 crore (Sobha share Rs 4,961 crore, 79%); Q4 sales Rs 1,836 crore
items.quote: During FY'25, our total real estate sales stood at Rs. 6,277 crores with Bangalore contributing about 58%, 20% from Gurgaon, 13% from Kerala. Sobha share of the total sales is roughly about 79% of this at about Rs. 4,961 crores.

items.statement: Organizational restructuring and redesignation of key people to support scale-up in launches, approvals, sales and execution across multiple cities
items.quote: We have made conscious restructuring and redesignation of key people inside the organization and that I am hoping that we have initiated the changes that are required to address this challenge.

items.statement: Bangalore E-Khata approval delays improving but evolving; US policy uncertainty (H1B, repatriation tax) may impact NRI sentiment but currently small percentage of demand
items.quote: E-Khata is an evolving phenomena . As we progress with the time, the adaption to the new system is continuing to take place both for inside the government and for the end users or developers.

items.statement: Hosur (40 acres) and Hoskote land parcels in design/approval phase; target launch within next 12 months
items.quote: Hosur, one of the land parcels that we have in which we plan to monetize through a plotted development, the change of land use has already come. And hence, we are in the design and approval phase right now. That's about 40 acres. Remaining parcels of the land in Hosur , we have clearly identified that they will be monetized. In addition to that, the Hoskote line, also is in design and approvals ph

items.statement: FY25 demand was subdued across key end-user segments; April 2025 was normal but May demand hit by cyclonic rains and early monsoon
items.quote: The operating environment in FY '25 was marked by subdued demand across key end user segments, which pose challenges to growth.

items.statement: Non-asbestos product share rose from 22% in FY24 to 26% in FY25 of overall sales
items.quote: The share of our non-asbestos product portfolio grew from 22% in FY '24 to 26% in FY '25 of overall sales.

items.statement: FY25 EBITDA margin declined to 9.5% from 11.1% in FY24 due to pricing dynamics
items.quote: EBITDA margin stood at 9.5% compared to 11.1% in FY '24.

items.statement: Debt-to-equity ratio improved from 0.32 to 0.21 through repayment of borrowings
items.quote: We have also made significant improvement to our balance sheet as the debt equity reduced from debt to equity ratio reduced from 0.32 to 0.21.

items.statement: Overall capacity utilization for FY25 stood at 68%
items.quote: During the year, our overall capacity utilization stood at 68%.

items.statement: Palghar and Odisha expansions delayed due to land acquisition; Palghar targeted Q4 FY27, Odisha Q4 FY28
items.quote: This would be Q4 FY '27 and Q4 FY '28. Q4 '27 would be Palghar and Q4 FY '28 would be Odisha.

items.statement: Board recommended final dividend of INR1 per share (face value INR10) for FY25
items.quote: the Board of Directors has recommended a final dividend of INR1 per share of face value INR10 for FY '25, subject to shareholder approval.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 demand subdued; no material price hikes taken; hoping to match or exceed FY25 numbers
items.quote: Q1 so far, there is hardly any price increase because, as I said, demand is subdued. And now again, this cyclonic and this impact of the early monsoon, so it's early to say whether any increase would come or not.

items.statement: Southern units running at 45-60% utilization in first two months of FY26 vs ~30% last year
items.quote: Southern unit is around between 45% to 60%.

items.statement: Value-added products at 14% of revenue in FY25; targeting ~20% in FY26
items.quote: See the next year, we are looking around 20% the value-added product.

items.statement: Value-added products carry 10-15% higher margins than conventional products
items.quote: See, generally, it is 10% to 15% extra than the normal one.

items.statement: Exports remain a focus; natural hedging via export revenues offsets rupee depreciation up to INR85-86/USD
items.quote: We are not doing any hedging because it's an automatic hedging, natural hedging because export is there, so it's an automatic hedging naturally.

items.statement: Minimal price increases in Q4 FY25 (<1%) and none so far in Q1 FY26 due to subdued demand
items.quote: Q4, it's minimal. I would say this time, hardly any price increase, I would say. The reason is, there may be Rs 1 or Rs 2 increases that may be, in the percentage terms, not more than 1%.

items.statement: Fiber cost ~30-35% of material consumption; no significant raw material cost increase expected
items.quote: you can take fibre at 30%-35% average considering both the products.

items.statement: Market share stable year-on-year; industry peers on similar trajectory
items.quote: More or less the same. There is no any because if the sales would have increased, then the share would have increased.

items.statement: Normal annual capex ~INR15 crores; CWIP INR31 crores (Palghar INR28 crores)
items.quote: 15 crores is the normal capex is always in the plants.

items.statement: Total long-term debt INR10.3 crores (incl. vehicle loans); working capital debt INR45 crores as of Mar 31; term loan repayable over 3 years but may prepay
items.quote: Our total debt is around INR 9.2 crore. Niteen: INR 9.2 crores, okay. Tuljaram Maheshwari: Plus vehicle, the total is INR10.3 crore

items.statement: No new debt for expansions in FY26; Palghar debt already sanctioned; further borrowing decision in FY26 based on cash flows
items.quote: We are not raising this year any debt on those expansions because already I spent good amount, and land acquisition is going on. So somewhere in '26 only we will see how my cash flow is.

items.statement: Management expects FY26 revenue and profitability to be better than FY25 but cannot quantify
items.quote: I think it would be better than '24-'25. I cannot quantify today, but it will be better than '24-'25 in terms of the revenue as well as the profitability.

items.statement: Gross margin unlikely to return to 50% (FY21 level); gradual improvement possible but limited by raw material prices and lack of price hikes
items.quote: Unlikely. The reason is that raw material prices for that increase, it is descending at the same price. There's no any reduction. So there's no increase happening now.

items.statement: Western plant utilization ~90%; Eastern (Odisha) utilization 35-50% as late entrant
items.quote: In the western part, more or less 90%.

items.statement: Distributors holding minimal stock; ordering cautiously (2 vehicles sold, 2 ordered) due to early monsoon
items.quote: They don't have a lot of stock. Now, because they are cautious because of the early monsoon, if two vehicles are being sold, two vehicles are being ordered. Like that.

items.statement: Employee costs may reduce ~1% with volume growth as fixed top-heavy structure leverages
items.quote: I think the employee cost generally, so the top people will get reduced with the volume, which is generally the top is always heavy. So definitely, in totality, it may be more or less, maybe the reduction of around 1%.

items.statement: Monsoon timing critical: early onset hurt May demand; recovery depends on monsoon pattern in coming weeks
items.quote: However, we remain optimistic about recovery in the coming weeks.

items.statement: Management reiterates double-digit topline growth guidance for FY26, aiming to beat industry growth
items.quote: I will continue with my guidance of double digital growth only. We will beat the industry that is something I would say.

items.statement: Dahej plant expansion expected to contribute ~Rs 100 crore in FY26 with >50% CAGR over next 3-4 years
items.quote: this plant is going to contribute roughly about Rs. 100 crores this expansion with a CAGR of more than 50% in next 3 to 4 years

items.statement: Kaeros subsidiary expected to generate Rs 10-12 crore PAT in FY26 and Rs 100 crore revenue
items.quote: in this fiscal, we can expect a profit of around Rs. 10 crores-Rs. 12 cores from this Kaeros business

items.statement: EBITDA margin improvement of 200-300 bps expected over next 2-3 years from FY25 base
items.quote: in 2-3 years, definitely we will see 200 to 300 points change actually in the EBITDA levels

items.statement: Net profit margin of 10% targeted over 2-3 years
items.quote: I can say that this should be 2 to 3 years target.

items.statement: FY26 capex budget ~Rs 100 crore, majorly for Sotanala fully automatic plant in Rajasthan
items.quote: expansion budgets, which for this year we have kept at around Rs. 100 crores FY'26. A major investment is going to go to Sotanala, which is going to be a fully automatic plant.

items.statement: Dahej plant received in-principle approval, production to start in June after Rs 150 crore investment
items.quote: We had made an investment of about Rs. 150 crores in this plant. And now this plant has received the in-principle approval from the government, which means that in the month of June, we will start our production.

items.statement: Rs 50 crore already spent on Sotanala plant, additional Rs 100 crore planned in FY26
items.quote: we have spent about Rs. 50 crores odd there already and there will be additional investment of about Rs. 100 crores in the new projects which will be majorly attributed to Sotanala now

items.statement: Dahej plant to manufacture insecticides, fungicides, intermediates; old facility to enhance herbicide capacity
items.quote: the new plant will be used majorly for manufacturing of insecticide, fungicide and their intermediate and the old facility we are going to enhance our capacity and some new of herbicides and their intermediates

items.statement: Power connection enhancement at Dahej expected in 2 months to support full capacity
items.quote: enhancement in the power connection is a lso expected, which should come in another two months

items.statement: 6 new product launches planned for FY26 including Altair (Nissan), Centran SC, Brahmos, Victor Gold, Sparkle
items.quote: We are going to launch 6 products in FY'26 and all these are expected to launch soon. So the first product is going to be Altair

items.statement: 12 launches in FY25, 4 moved to Focused Maharatna taking total to 16
items.quote: The highest number of launches, almost 12 launches were done in the fiscal '25. Out of these 12 launches, 4 products I am able to shift to Focused Maharatna this year. The total number of Focused Maharatna till last year were 12, which has been increased to 16.

items.statement: Strong herbicide demand expected in June due to early monsoon and market shortages in rice/corn herbicides
items.quote: June should see a good demand for these herbicides better than usual. So now it depends how much we are able to place. We are in a good situation

items.statement: Inventory built up in March for aggressive FY26 launches, expected to liquidate by June-July
items.quote: We had very aggressive launches in the year '25 and we have very aggressive launches in '26. There were a lot of new brands which are to be introduced into our market. We have to build up the inventory in the month of March, which will finish very soon by June-July.

items.statement: FY25 gross margin improved 655 bps to 32% driven by premium mix, pricing strategy, new launches
items.quote: gross profit margin in FY'25 also stood at 32%, which is showing improvement of 655 bps over the last year. So, this is due to the better product mix sales, improved pricing strategy on which we are working and some new launches.

items.statement: FY25 EBITDA margin improved 281 bps to 11.1%; Q4 EBITDA margin 7.9% vs 3.2% YoY
items.quote: EBITDA margin also improved by 36% for the full year. So, from 8.3% it has come into the double-digit figure of around 11.1%. And EBITDA level for the quarter has also improved by 226%. From 3.2% it has come improved to 7.9%.

items.statement: FY25 PAT margin improved to 7% from 5%; Q4 PAT margin 3.9% vs 2.8% YoY
items.quote: full year PAT has also improved by 39%. From 5%, it has come to 7%. And during the quarter, it has improved by 85% from 2.8% to 3.9%.

items.statement: Raw material prices stable; 3-4 month inventory maintained; some price improvement in April-May, further revisions depend on monsoon
items.quote: Raw materials like you have to make an arrangement because it's a cyclic industry. That is one reason actually we have to plan four months in advance. So generally we will keep always the stock for 3 to 4 months.

items.statement: Herbicide prices seeing small increases due to shortages; regular 2-3 price revisions per year till August
items.quote: For the herbicide, there's a small window actually. So yes, there is some price rise internationally also in the domestic market also, but not very big.

items.statement: Working capital increase temporary due to strategic inventory buildup for season; improvement expected in FY26
items.quote: Yes, it's temporary because of the inventory buildup and you will see the improvement in the fiscal because we are very very fierce on this.

items.statement: Salary budget expected to grow ~15% CAGR; routine increments to cover new hires; Sotanala commissioning may add costs in FY26
items.quote: I think we should be able to maintain with 15% CAGR on our salary budgets.

items.statement: Senior leadership hiring in process; joinings expected during FY26
items.quote: There are things in process, so as they will happen, because you have to form a strategy, then you have to find the right type of people, and then people get free from their current assignments and join you.

items.statement: FY25 volume growth ~10% with 8% price decline yielding 2% revenue growth; Q4 volume growth ~40%
items.quote: in the full year, the volume growth has been roughly about 10%. The average price decline during the year is around 8%. So, the total growth in terms of numbers is showing about 2%.

items.statement: ROCE 18% and ROE 13% in FY25, both improved
items.quote: The return on capital employed and return on eq uity is also improved in FY'25. So, the ROCE is 18% and ROE is 13% respectively during the year

items.statement: Exports 5% of revenue; no major capex needed; 4 NABL labs including 1 GLP; 150+ R&D scientists; Mumbai office with 20 people
items.quote: At the moment my contribution from the international market is coming to roughly about 5%. That will grow slowly. There is not going to be any dramatic change.

items.statement: Manpower shortages post-war affecting production capacity in Q1; recovery taking time
items.quote: there is some shortage of manpower because when the war started, so people from Jammu fled actually and not only there, there was impact at other plants also

items.statement: OAT Agro JV first product (NCE with new mode of action) nearing India registration after 12 years, 60k+ molecules tested
items.quote: Yes, this is going to be the first product which will be commercialized by the JV. But there are series of products which are after this. And let me tell you that these are the real inventions, which are the new chemicals. We call it NCE, new chemical entities, with different modes of action.

items.statement: Launch pipeline of 13.5 million sq ft planned for FY26
items.quote: Puravankara is well-positioned to capitalize on these trends with a robust launch pipeline of over 13.5 million square feet, planned for Financial Year '25-'26, aiming at centering our presence amid a consolidating market.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 EBITDA margin 9%, full year loss Rs 186 crore due to approval delays
items.quote: EBITDA margins for the quarter was around 9% while we had a net loss of Rs. 88 crores. Given that, as you are aware that, we had delays in terms of getting the approvals, and hence, the handovers were actually delayed.

items.statement: Land investment of Rs 1,284 crore added 8 million sq ft with GDV Rs 13,000 crore in FY25
items.quote: We made significant progress during this financial year with land investment of approximately Rs. 1,284 crores, which added almost 8 million square feet of our development portfolio, representing a GDV value of Rs. 13,000 crores.

items.statement: 3.2 million sq ft commercial development underway, 2 million sq ft OC expected in FY26
items.quote: Currently we have 3.2 million square feet of development underway, with nearly 2 million square feet expected to receive OC during this particular year.

items.statement: Average realization Rs 9,031/sq ft in Q4 up 9% YoY, FY25 Rs 8,830 up 10%
items.quote: Average realization also witnessed healthy growth for Q4. Average realization stood at Rs. 9,031 per square feet, up 9% year -on-year. For the full year, it improved by 10%, up from Rs. 8,035 to Rs. 8,830 for this year versus last year.

items.statement: Customer collections Rs 3,937 crore in FY25 up 9% YoY, Q4 collections Rs 946 crore
items.quote: Customer collections for Q4 stood at Rs. 946 crores, and for the financial year, it grew by 9% to Rs. 3,937 crores from Rs. 3,609 crores, which is the last financial year.

items.statement: Net debt Rs 2,949 crore, net D/E 1.7x, cash Rs 732 crore as of March 2025
items.quote: As on 31st of March 2025, our net debt stood at Rs. 2,949 crores with a net debt equity ratio of 1.7x. We also had a cash balance of Rs. 732 crores, which reflects a strong liquidity position and gives us the comfort to manage operations smoothly.

items.statement: Exploring QIP or platform partnerships to balance capital structure and support growth
items.quote: We also are exploring funding options as we have been communicating with you, like QIP or platform level partnerships to keep our capital s tructure balanced and support our growth plans

items.statement: Operating cash flow Rs 4,342 crore in FY25 up 10% YoY
items.quote: Operating cash flows for Financial Year '24-'25 stood at Rs. 4,342 crores, up 10% Y -o-Y.

items.statement: Non-Bengaluru projects 54% of ongoing, 52% of planned pipeline; Mumbai+Pune 21% of planned
items.quote: It is important to highlight that non -Bengaluru projects now constitute 54% of our ongoing developments and 52% of our planned pipeline. Mumbai and Pune together account for about 21% of the planned projects, underscoring our focus on diversifying the portfolio across high-opportunity markets.

items.statement: Secured marquee redevelopment projects in Breach Candy, Pali Hill, Lokhandwala competing with top developers
items.quote: For example, the project that we have secured, most of the society redevelopment that we have secured, which is extremely prime, one being Breach Candy, the second one being Pali Hill in Bombay. If you are aware of the Bombay market, the third being Lokhandwala.

items.statement: NGT issue in Mumbai delaying Lokhandwala and Thane launches, resolution expected by September
items.quote: for example, Lokhandwala and I think, Thane, both are affected by NGT. Now, entire Bombay and those areas, all developers are affected by it. My sense is, and those are high value projects. My sense, what I am getting from CREDAI as well, is that there should be some sort of a resolution come September, right

items.statement: Organizational restructuring to regional CEOs (South, West) reporting to MD for operational efficiency
items.quote: in order to get more ope rational efficiency, cost efficiency, process efficiency, a regional structure, the organization will benefit a lot more from efficiency and cost as well, both. So therefore, the new structure is where we have a CEO for the South region, who manage the entire South business. We have a CEO for the West region, who manages the entire, and both then report into the MD

items.statement: Approval delays in Bangalore (e-Khata) and Mumbai (NGT) impacted handovers and launches in FY25
items.quote: On the handing over, Karnataka went into a very new method of actually giving the Khatas, which is called the e-Khata, which for millions of documents had to be redone and reconverted into an electronic format called e-Khata and that was put into a line. S o, we all were waiting in the line to get the Khatas because of which we could not register

items.statement: Residential demand strong with 88,000 units sold in Q4 FY25 across top 8 cities, 350,000 for full year
items.quote: The residential market continued its strong momentum with over 88,000 units sold during Q4 of Financial Year '25 across the top 8 cities and more than 350,000 units for the full year.

items.statement: Won marquee Mumbai redevelopment projects against top 1-2 city developers due to brand strength
items.quote: And each one of these cases, we were competing with the number one, number two in the city. Eventually, I think we were able to position the brand, and these customers are also highly discerning, right? So they understand real estate, they understand brands, the entire team, the SGBM team made a trip to Bangalore, saw the quality, saw the differentiation, or even the vision in the product that we

items.statement: Commercial projects Zentech and Aerocity in Bangalore expected to generate Rs 1,870 crore surplus
items.quote: We have two projects, one is Zentech and Aerocity. And they both are in Bangalore. And these two projects are exp ected to generate a surplus of Rs. 1,870 crores, making a significant value creation opportunity for the company

items.statement: JV with KVN for 25 acres in North Bengaluru, GDV Rs 3,300 crore, launch within 6 months
items.quote: In May, we basically have announced a JV with KVN, Property Holding Limited LLP for approximately 25 acres land parcel located in North Bengaluru with a potential GDV of Rs. 3,300 crores and a planned saleable area of approximately 3.5 million square feet. This development marks a key addition in our portfolio in a high growth micro market and is expected to launch within the next six months.

items.statement: Management targets 15% to 18% top-line growth for FY26.
items.quote: I think the whole plan is that on the top line we grow by 15% to 18% that is what we are aiming to do and let us hope for the best.

items.statement: Management aims for 15% to 18% annual growth over the next three to four years.
items.quote: the whole idea is that to continuously grow by 15% to 18% every year

items.statement: Management expects to sustain current EBITDA and PAT margins and hopes they improve.
items.quote: we feel that we will continue to maintain these numbers and we only hope that they will only get better in coming quarters.

items.statement: Management declines to speculate on achieving double-digit EBITDA margins.
items.quote: No, I do not want to speculate on these things that there will be two digit numbers.

items.statement: US tariff changes have not impacted India-US trade lane; enquiries have increased.
items.quote: overall there has not been any major impact on our business as far as the India-US trade lane is concerned. In fact, we are happy because globally people are at least, the US buyers are looking at India more seriously now.

items.statement: China-India trade lane seeing no major disruptions; relationship improving.
items.quote: the relationship with China is only getting better. We are not seeing any major disruptions on that route also.

items.statement: New ventures TiGreen, CUBOX LCL, and Freight Jar are showing results and will be scaled up.
items.quote: Our project "TiGreen", which is renewable energy that is also doing really very well. And I think overall it is showing in the numbers. We have launched CUBOX which is LCL product for us. That CUBOX is also doing very well

items.statement: CUBOX LCL product accepted positively in first three months; expected to contribute significantly.
items.quote: market has accepted the product in a very positive way and in coming quarters also this is going to contribute in a big way, in a good way to our whole revenue.

items.statement: Freight Jar 2.0 opening doors for new business despite slow digital adoption in industry.
items.quote: through freight jar we are able to open a lot of doors for new businesses. But yes, the acceptance on the digital, overall in the industry, in the businesses is very slow.

items.statement: Deliberate strategy to diversify customer base and reduce dependence on top clients.
items.quote: I think it is a concerted effort from our side, not to depend on few customers but to have a diverse portfolio of customers.

items.statement: PSU and government projects growing well; qualified for bigger shipments; expect 15% growth in this sector.
items.quote: I think we are expecting good numbers, good business from the PSU and government projects while continuing this upward trend, I think we will be growing by at least 15% in this sector also.

items.statement: Aspires to be among top five logistics companies in India in next three to four years.
items.quote: I would say in the next three to four years we want to be in the top five logistics company in India.

items.statement: Tariff war stabilized; no longer a threat for India-US business.
items.quote: we are seeing that the tariff war is more or less stabilized. It is no more a threat as such, I think we should not we worried about the tariff part on the India-US business is concerned.

items.statement: Operating leverage exists as verticals support each other (LCL supports other verticals, TiGreen and Freight Jar support imports).
items.quote: overall definitely this is there.

items.statement: Snowman Logistics FY26 capex guided at Rs 100-150 crore per year, 80% debt-funded
items.quote: Yes, we are still of the same opinion that we go with 80-20 model. 20 will be from our internal accruals, 80 will be funded through loans.

items.statement: Gateway Distriparks FY26 capex guided at Rs 30 crore per year excluding new terminals
items.quote: So, maybe around Rs. 30 crores, other than the new terminals.

items.statement: Gateway evaluating asset-light BTS model for new warehouses alongside own facilities like Lucknow
items.quote: we are also discussing BTS, where someone else builds a warehouse and we do a long-term lease for more locations. So, we will be growing on both asset light model as well as our own projects.

items.statement: Snowman warehousing margins fell to 11% due to Park 'n' Pay model (60,000 pallets) and Amazon exit
items.quote: So, some of it is contributed by the Park 'n' Pay model. This year we have grown 500 x in Park 'n' Pay model wherein close to 60,000 pallets were outsourced and built. So, wherein the margins are lower, thus the percentage margin is pulled down on the warehousing part.

items.statement: Snowman 5PL gross margin target revised to 6-8% from earlier 8-9% due to Unilever mix and product mix changes
items.quote: Yes, correct. That is changed, but it will remain in the range of 6% to 8% depending upon the product mix.

items.statement: Gateway Rail EBITDA per TEU ~Rs 9,500-9,600; CFS EBITDA per TEU ~Rs 1,300-1,400 in Q4 FY25
items.quote: Yes, so roughly it's about Rs. 9,500 - 9,600 for the rail side and say Rs. 1,300 - 1,400 for the CFS side.

items.statement: Snowman warehousing ex-Amazon grew ~5% YoY; temperature control flat; meat/seafood/poultry down 15% YoY
items.quote: If we remove Amazon business alone, from the Park 'n' Pay and the dry business, it's around 5% increase we can see in a warehousing business, which is exactly been compensated by loss of Amazon business in the topline, which is around Rs. 10-11 crores, works out to be.

items.statement: Snowman added Unilever (ice cream distribution in Northeast) and Kopi Kenangan (Indonesian coffee chain) as new 5PL customers
items.quote: So, this year we have added two new customers. One is Unilever and the other one is an Indonesian coffee chain by the name Kopi Kenangan.

items.statement: Snowman 5PL customer selection prioritizes payment ability and growth; contracts include safeguards against inventory risk
items.quote: We also select those customers who we are confident of their growth and their ability to make payments on time, because this business is very working capital intensive.

items.statement: Western DFC JNPT corridor expected completion by March 2026; Mundra congestion and double-stack restrictions hurt rail coefficients
items.quote: as per the site they are mentioning December, but as per our sources it might take another couple of months. So, it should happen by March. So, then only we will see 100% advantage.

items.statement: Jaipur land acquisition under Benami Property Act dispute; management confident of winning within 1-2 years
items.quote: We still believe we did it the right way. We have a good top legal firm also advising us, who believes that we have a strong case. We are hopeful within the next year or two, for whatever reason, this got caught in this legal case.

items.statement: Snowman trade receivables up with turnover; provision ~Rs 4 crore covering 180 days; majority from current year
items.quote: The increase in trad e receivables is a direct relation to our increase in turnover, we put it this way. And we carry a provision of approximately Rs. 4 crores, which is covering 180 days

items.statement: Gateway cash balance over Rs 100 crore; no immediate plans to increase Snowman stake or merge; surplus cash may fund dividends or capex
items.quote: Every year there will be certain CAPEX which is required in GDL. And we have a track record of paying dividend also. So, based on the cash flows, if and when there is any surplus, then we could consider it.

items.statement: Snowman contract renewals achieved 4-5% pricing increase; overall pricing drop due to mix change (less meat/seafood/poultry)
items.quote: about 4% to 5% pricing increase we have this year. 4%. But the mix changes. That's why on an overall pricing basis, you will see the drop, but contract basis with customers, we are able to get increases.

items.statement: Snowman consolidation added Rs 145 crore revenue, Rs 25 crore EBITDA, Rs 3 crore PBT, Rs 3.5 crore PAT for full year FY25
items.quote: for the full year, we have Rs. 145 crores of revenue, about Rs. 25 crores in EBITDA and PBT of Rs. 3 crores and Rs. PAT of 3.5 crores on account of consolidation.

items.statement: One-time stamp duty provision Rs 12.8 crore for past merger; goodwill impairment Rs 258 crore (non-cash, no tax impact) due to share price/DCF
items.quote: This is a provision we have taken on stamp duty amount payable for it, but since the amount was not ascertainable back when we did it three, four years ago, we have just taken it as a contingency right now.

items.statement: Goodwill impairment Rs 258 crore driven by share price drop from Rs 75 to ~Rs 50; DCF and share price in same range as of March 31
items.quote: Our last purchase was at about Rs. 75. So, we first took a gain at that value. Then this has come down from basically Rs. 75 minus close to Rs. 50. So, that Rs. 25-27 gap is the hit that we have had to take.

items.statement: CFS revenue accounting change: Rs 46 crore full-year impact from gross-to-net revenue adjustment for discounts
items.quote: for the full year, this figure is about Rs. 46 crores. So, if you add that back, then FY '25 revenue for CFS vertical would be higher than FY '24.

items.statement: Snowman transportation EBIT dropped 90% QoQ due to year-end provision and slight margin dip; business flat
items.quote: See, in Q4, as a year-end process, we have taken an additional provision as a cautious. Also, there is a slight dip in the margins in the current quarter. That itself is a reason. Otherwise, the revenue, I mean, otherwise the business itself is flat in the current quarter.

items.statement: Depreciation reassessed in Q4 only, impact Rs 3.5-4 crore lower for quarter; will continue as base for FY26
items.quote: We have only done it in Q4. We have not done it backdated from Q1. It's between Rs. 3.5 crores to Rs. 4 crores.

items.statement: Other income higher due to routine write-backs of discounts/incentives, interest income on Rs 100+ crore cash, and tax provision write-back from Vivad se Vishwas
items.quote: So, there are some routine write-backs of discounts and incentives payable. Then there is also interest income, as the company is sitting on over Rs. 100 crores in cash right now. And then also there was a write-back on account of a provision we made for tax last year.

items.statement: International combined ratio target 110-115% by year end FY26
items.quote: Yes, currently it is at 121 % something, and we still want to improve , if it can be around 110 % or 115% that will be an achievement by the year end.

items.statement: Overall combined ratio target 106-107% for FY26
items.quote: Yes, around 106%, 107% figure.

items.statement: Reinsurance business growth projected at 10% YoY for next three years
items.quote: On an overall basis, we project growth in our reinsurance business, which will be measured growth of about 10% year-on-year for the next three years.

items.statement: International Q4 growth driven by rating upgrade enabling new accounts in January renewals
items.quote: The 4th Quarter growth is mainly resulting from the rating upgrade of G IC wherein we got the rating upgrade in the month of November '24

items.statement: International market pricing soft except for loss-affected non-proportional treaties with 10-15% loadings
items.quote: Pricing international market what I saw in the 1st January renewal is quite soft, so far direct market is concerned.

items.statement: Health portfolio grew 66% in FY25 driven by retail health; future growth 5-10% due to commission demands
items.quote: And particularly, currently wherever we have participated, the participation on standalone retail part is substantial, and then the group health also.

items.statement: Crop portfolio declined 50-60% due to SSM model capping liability at 110-130%; Maharashtra adopted SSM model
items.quote: The SSM model which has been now in comparison to the previous model of PMAY scheme where the liability was 250%, whereas in this SSM model the cap is at 110% or 130%.

items.statement: Fire segment growth expected 10-20% as companies adhere to IRDA rates
items.quote: The pricing, as I said, we are seeing the growth, particularly the companies are following up the IRDA rates, which itself will help the market to grow by 10 % to 20% in the fire segment.

items.statement: FY25 combined ratio 108.8%; adjusted combined ratio 85.79% vs 86.24% prior year
items.quote: For FY '25, the combined ratio stood at 108.8%. This disciplined posture has not only fortified our financial position but has also deepened our understanding of market cycles and our own risk appetite.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 combined ratio 103.56% vs 89.26% prior year; income claim ratio 82.2% vs 68.9%
items.quote: Combined ratio for the quarter stood at 103.56% compared to 89.26% for the corresponding period in the previous year.

items.statement: Domestic Q4 combined ratio improved to 70.34% from 80% prior year; foreign loss ratio 68.60% vs 110.29% prior quarter
items.quote: If you look at domestic profit this quarter , the combined ratio has come down, non-life domestic has come down to 70.34% as against 80% of Q4 of last year.

items.statement: Domestic premium FY25 Rs 30,662.44 cr (75%, +18.8% YoY); International Rs 10,491.51 cr (25%, -7.8% YoY)
items.quote: Domestic premium for the year FY '25 is Rs. 30,662.44 crores and the international age Rs. 10,491.51 crores. The percentage split is domestic 75% and international 25%.

items.statement: CAT reserve building to Rs 5,000 cr corpus per Board policy; Rs 600 cr added in FY25; no drawdown planned until target reached
items.quote: So this reserve is being created in line with the CAT reserve policy as approved by the Board and we plan to build up this corpus to some thing like an amount of Rs. 5,000

items.statement: No official information from IRDA or Ministry on reducing obligatory cession from 4%
items.quote: We have no information or advice from either the regulator or the ministry.

items.statement: Companies adhering to IRDA-prescribed IIB rates from Jan 1, 2025; few aberrations noted
items.quote: They have been trying to adhere to the I RDA rates, particularly from 1st of January , '25, onwards

items.statement: Solvency ratio improved to 3.70 from 3.25; CAT reserves excluded from available assets for solvency
items.quote: The solvency ratio for the year end improved to 3.70 as compared to 3.25 for the previous year.

items.statement: Net worth excl. fair value change Rs 43,106.52 cr; incl. fair value change Rs 83,224.33 cr as of Mar 31, 2025
items.quote: Net worth excluding fair value change was Rs. 43,106.52 crores on 31 /3/25 as against Rs. 37,581.78 crores in the previous year end.

items.statement: Investment income FY25 Rs 11,204 cr: interest/dividend Rs 7,096 cr (+10% YoY), profit on sale Rs 4,108 cr
items.quote: The breakup is, for the full year investment income stands at Rs. 11,204 crores. The income excluding profit, that is your interest, dividend stands at Rs. 7,096 crores.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 investment income Rs 3,903 cr: ~Rs 1,500 cr profit on sale, balance interest/dividend
items.quote: For the quarter the breakup will be say around Rs. 1,500 crores from profit on sale and the balance will be interest income, so interest and dividend income.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 international losses driven by California fire, Taiwan typhoon, Dubai/Nepal floods, Israel/Turkey losses
items.quote: And the main dampener here is the foreign Q4 and that is mainly, as I said before, it is mainly because of the California fire and then Taiwan Typhoon.

items.statement: Life claims increased 2.5x due to higher paid claims (Rs 1,887 cr) and reserve strengthening (Rs 859 cr); expected to normalize
items.quote: So if you combine all those things , because of that your incurred claims have increased substantially compared to even last quarter and then the last year.

items.statement: Discontinued motor/cargo treaties from 2021 have waning tail; adequate reserves created
items.quote: I can only say that the contract that we cancelled by the end of 2021, the effect of it is waning. The tail continues. It has not come to an end, but it is certainly waning.

items.statement: Obligatory business ~30% of book; not necessarily more profitable; portfolio quality improving across non-obligatory business
items.quote: See, the point is that obligatory would constitute say something like 30% of our book. And there is always a risk return trade off, so it is not correct to say that this is more profitable.

items.statement: If obligatory cession removed, temporary top-line hit but greater portfolio control; plan to market additional quota share treaties
items.quote: But on the flip side , it gives us greater control on our portfolio. The entire risk selection is with our underwriting, will be based on our underwriting.

items.statement: Rating upgrade enabling re-entry into lost international markets and renewal of accounts
items.quote: Now we are trying to look into those territories where we can reenter them and to bring about or to renew those accounts , or to gain those accounts which are lost to us.

items.statement: CMD unavailable for call due to travel; Executive Director Hitesh Joshi led presentation
items.quote: Please note that CMD is not available for call today due to unavoidable travel plans.

items.statement: Expects ~25% YoY growth in Fluoropolymers in FY26 driven by new Fluoropolymers
items.quote: we expect to see almost 25% growth in Fluoropolymers from where we are today

items.statement: Expects revenue from EV Battery Materials business to start in H2 FY26 and ramp up in FY27
items.quote: We expect the revenue from EV business to trickle in towards the second half of this financial year

items.statement: Announced capex of INR1,600 crores for FY26 with INR1,200 crores for GFCL EV and INR400 crores for GFL
items.quote: We have announced capex of INR1,600 crores for FY '26 with INR1,200 crores earmarked for GFCL EV, largely towards increasing the current capacities with increased customer approvals and audits in pl ace and INR400 crores for GFL, largely earmarked for Fluoropolymers and refrigerant business

items.statement: R-32 plant capex around INR150 crores excluding HF; HF capex separate and not yet announced
items.quote: in the last quarter call, we had indicated a capex of around INR150 crores, okay? So we are still holding on to that capex

items.statement: LFP plant achieved mechanical completion; commissioning and trial production to begin next month
items.quote: Our LFP plant have achieved mechanical completion with commissioning and trial production set to begin next month

items.statement: Electrolyte and binder plants at advanced stage of customer validation with multiple successful global audits completed
items.quote: Our electrolyte and binder plants are also at advanced stage of customer validation with multiple successful global audits already completed

items.statement: Planning Phase 2 and Phase 3 capacity expansions for LiPF6 salt in FY26
items.quote: we are moving ahead with Phase 2 and Phase 3 capacity expansions planned in FY '26

items.statement: Targeting R-32 commercial sales by H2 FY26 via retrofitting; full run-rate target 20,000 tons
items.quote: our target is to bring the product by the second half of this year, this financial year

items.statement: Growing demand from automotive, semiconductors, EVs and Energy Storage systems for Fluoropolymers
items.quote: Growing demand from automotive, semiconductors, Electric Vehicles and Energy Storage system is opening significant opportunities for this sector

items.statement: Battery materials demand robust driven by EVs, ESS, renewable energy, green hydrogen and AI data centers
items.quote: Demand for our product is expected to be robust, driven not only by EVs, but also by the growing energy storage system markets, which is critical to renewable energy and green hydrogen transitions as well as rise of AI-powered data centers

items.statement: Q4 FY25 EBITDA margin improved to 25% from 21% YoY; consolidated PAT nearly doubled to INR191 crores
items.quote: Our EBITDA grew significantly by 28% to INR305 crores with margins improving from 25% -- to 25% from 21% in same time last year, which is quarter 4 FY '24. Our consolidated PAT nearly doubled, reaching INR191 crores in this quarter

items.statement: Fluoropolymer prices stable across domestic and global markets; FKM volumes rising with new project approvals
items.quote: Prices remained stable across domestic as well as global markets. FKM volumes are steadily rising as new project approvals are under progress

items.statement: R-22 prices improved in Q4; further increase expected as global production quotas reduce
items.quote: Within our Fluorochemicals business, we saw improvement in R -22 prices during the quarter and further increase is expected as global production quotas reduce

items.statement: MDC prices declined due to new capacity additions but expected to stabilize in coming quarters
items.quote: MDC prices declined due to new capacity additions, but are expected to stabilize in coming quarters

items.statement: Battery material prices stable for last 1-1.5 years; business plan accounts for current pricing with premium over China
items.quote: last 1.5 years or almost 1 year, they have been very, very stable, whether you look at the salt pricing or LFP or any of the battery materials pricing

items.statement: Fluoropolymer growth driven by higher value-added grades of new Fluoropolymers; PTFE portfolio churned toward higher value grades
items.quote: we are witnessing a continued growth in Fluoropolymers revenue and volumes due to our focus on higher value-added grades of new Fluoropolymers

items.statement: FKM and PFA approvals progressing; legacy player exit benefiting volumes
items.quote: approvals have started coming in and commercials have started. In PFA, we are into a regular business, which I also told last time that approvals have come even from some of the semiconductor applications

items.statement: Customer engagement increased significantly with technical visits and audits from prospective clients in US, EU, Korea, Japan and India

items.quote: working capital days have increased in anticipation of the growth in next few quarters. We have increased production of Fluoropolymers and Vacuum materials to build up the pipeline, and we expect this to normalize in next 1 to 2 quarters

items.statement: Net debt reduced to INR1,451 crores from INR1,769 crores YoY; net debt to equity improved from 0.3% to 0.2%
items.quote: Our net debt as on March 31, 2025 has come down to INR 1,451 crores as compared to INR 1,769 crores as on March 31, 2024, resulting an improvement of net debt to equity from 0.3% to 0.2%
