items.quote: We raised INR1,000 crores last year, which has funded the capex . We still have some cash out of that equity raise, which would be partly used for capex this year. Also, the new capex that Dr. Kapoor just mentioned would all be funded by the external sources without rel ying on the cash flow of

items.statement: No current HF bottleneck; HF capacity addition planned alongside R-22 to cater to future demand
items.quote: As of now, we don't have an issue with our HF. However, in order to cater to future demand, we have already announced that we'll be adding up HF capacity

items.statement: Captive power plant expected annual savings INR120-150 crores; benefits to trickle in partly in FY26
items.quote: the total saving will be in the tune of INR 120 crores to INR150 crores on an annualized basis, but that will trickle in partly this financial year

items.statement: Key risk for EV business is timing of market growth; fundamental demand from green climate agenda, renewables, EV and ESS seen as strong
items.quote: in terms of risk, if I see, in terms of timing, how these eventually grow. But fundamental that whether we will be able to reach, for example, in India, 300 gigawatt hours or not, I don't think we see that as a big risk at the moment

items.statement: Management expects volume-led growth in FY26 supported by early monsoon, stable commodity pricing, and new product launches; aims to increase margins above FY25 levels.
items.quote: Our focus will remain firmly on driving volume-led growth, scaling up recently launched products, and sustaining margins through tight cost controls and optimized operations.

items.statement: Management targets EBITDA margin above 20% and believes it can sustain or exceed current levels as low-margin products are phased out.
items.quote: we have already broken that ceiling and from the mindset point of view also, now we understand that since we are not focusing on the top line growth, since we are not focusing on some of the low margin product, naturally the margin profile will go beyond 20% and it may go beyond 20% if the trend continues like this.

items.statement: Board approved Rs 55 crore brownfield expansion at Bhavnagar to double capacity for a key SCC molecule, targeting completion by Q4 FY27.
items.quote: With the further investment of about INR 55 crore, and with this we are targeting to double the capacities. And it will also means this entire additional capacities can be used to expand our exports to our parent Company. This plant is expected to be completed by Q4 Financial Year 2026-27.

items.statement: Board approved under Rs 10 crore brownfield modification at Tarapur to manufacture newly launched patented product Excalia Max, targeting completion by Q4 FY27.
items.quote: The estimated CAPEX for this project is less than Rs. 10 crore. And the timelines are very similar to the first Brownfield project of Bhavnagar. So, the Tarapur Brownfield project is also expected to be completed by Financial Year '26-'27, Q4.

items.statement: Dahej greenfield expansion planned with initial Rs 300 crore investment for multiple SCC-innovated products, with production targeted between FY27-FY30.
items.quote: We plan to invest, as informed earlier, an initial investment of Rs. 300 crore to start with and we are prepared for more investment depending on the number of products we finalize and the time that will be required to put up each and every plant.

items.statement: Bhavnagar expansion will enable SCIL to meet 40-50% of global requirement for a key SCC molecule.
items.quote: This facility will enhance our ability to support the global requirement of very important SCC molecules and SCIL will be able to meet 40% to 50% of the global requirement.

items.statement: Tarapur facility will manufacture Excalia Max active ingredient within 12-15 months using existing plant with modifications.
items.quote: the technical or the active ingredient, as we call it, for this newly launched globally blockbuster product will also be made by us in India within next 12 to 15 months. This will be made in our existing Tarapur plant, and all the trials and technical evaluation have been completed.

items.statement: FY25 domestic branded volume grew 20% and export volume grew 30%+ year-on-year.
items.quote: In Financial Year '24-'25, our team delivered 20% volume growth in our branded business in Indian domestic market and 30% plus volume growth in exports over last year.

items.statement: FY25 EBITDA margin expanded 339 bps to 20.1% and PAT margin expanded 308 bps to 16.1%, both historic highs.
items.quote: EBITDA margin improved by 339 basis points year-on-year to 20.1%, while net profit margin expanded by 308 basis points to 16.1%.

items.statement: Gross margin expanded 337 bps to 41% in FY25 driven by favorable product mix, procurement efficiencies, and liquidation of high-cost inventory.
items.quote: Our full year gross margin expanded by 337 basis points year-on-year to 41%, underpinned by favorable product mix, procurement efficiencies, and proactive liquidation of high-cost inventories.

items.statement: Realizations declined ~10% in both domestic and export segments in FY25, offset by volume growth.
items.quote: Our revenue growth for the year was primarily volume-led, underscoring the strength of our domestic franchise, robust channel engagement, and timely execution of demand generation initiatives. This was complemented by sustained improvement in operational efficiencies and cost optimization measures, which enabled us to expand margins and deliver strong growth in profitability. We delivered 11% reve

items.statement: New products launched in last 3 years and premium portfolio drove volume growth and margin expansion; Excalia Max and Lentigo registrations received.
items.quote: In addition to several premium branded products in our existing portfolio, several products newly launched in the last three years or so contributed to this volume growth. We are extremely pleased with our team's performance to deliver such volume growth.

items.statement: Specialty portfolio revenue flat but mix upgraded to higher-margin products; low-margin products being phased out over next year.
items.quote: So, you are right that this process of maybe slowdown in some of the low margin products in specialty and focusing more on new products and high margin products, I believe this cycle will continue for some more time. So, in our portfolio, there are still some products in our specialty which are not yielding very good margins, and maybe there could be a slowdown of some of these products. So, that

items.statement: Every Day Farmer's Day campaign reached over 1 million farmers and thousands of channel partners, supporting domestic growth.
items.quote: Through which we reached over a million farmers and many thousands of channel partners across the seasons and across the country which helped us in robust growth.

items.statement: Export revenue grew 22% in FY25; South America up 78%, North America up 44%; Q4 exports declined to Rs 210-215 crore from Rs 260+ crore due to LATAM headwinds.
items.quote: Export revenue surged 22% year-on-year, supported by penetration into newer geographies despite Q4 headwinds. In FY '24-'25, sales to South America and North America increased by 78% and 44% respectively as compared to the same period last year.

items.statement: Excalia Max received fast-track approval under special window for new global launch products.
items.quote: We are also thankful to Indian regulatory authorities for granting fast-track approval of this product under a special window for new global launch products.

items.statement: Management emphasizes inventory control, receivables discipline, and working capital management as core priorities for FY26.
items.quote: Our efforts around inventory control, receivables discipline and working capital management will continue to be a core priority even as we prepare for the next phase of scale.

items.statement: Company holds strong cash balance of Rs 1,500-1,600 crore+ and generating more; CAPEX slowed in FY25 due to global agrochemical downturn.
items.quote: you are absolutely right, last one or two years, there was slowdown in CAPEX. But we feel that going forward, that situation should be behind us. And going forward, we should be having more confidence to be able to add capacities, both for our domestic requirement and also for the global requirement.

items.statement: Parent SCC evaluating entry into semiconductor chemicals in India; SCIL in discussions and hopeful to be considered for partnership.
items.quote: In our parent Company's strategic growth plan, they have announced that our ITCM sector, which deals with this kind of a chemicals and semi-conductor related chemicals, is looking to expand into India. And we are in discussions with them. And we are jointly evaluating the opportunities in India.

items.statement: LATAM export market sluggish in Q4 FY25; recovery expected in 1-2 quarters but uncertainty remains.
items.quote: Overall, you know, LATAM picked up early last year. First three quarters did well. In the Quarter 4, it did went a little bit sluggish. But based on our market information and all, it seems to be coming back on track. We need to wait for one or two more quarters to really see it to come back to normalcy. We are optimistic.

items.statement: Early monsoon onset, rising MSPs, and increasing acreage in cotton, corn, chili signal strong FY26 domestic demand.
items.quote: the monsoon has come little early, about a week or so early, the sentiments are positive. It looks to be very, very good season is upon us, and we are all fully geared up. There is definitely going to be a volume growth. I think, I just saw, I didn't read it. MSP prices have been announced just maybe half an hour back. I didn't read it yet. I am sure it has gone up at least 5% to 10% on key crops.

items.statement: Management sees no further price decline; prices stable and may inch up from current levels.
items.quote: And also we are not really seeing any further price drop because prices are quite stable. Whatever has happened has happened and I think if at all the price can only inch up from this level, that is what we feel.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 EBITDA margin was 3.64% due to higher raw material cost as percentage of sales
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter was around INR 4 crores with EBITDA margins at 3.64%

items.statement: FY25 EBITDA margin was 7.96%
items.quote: EBITDA was around INR 43 crores with EBITDA margins at 7.96%

items.statement: 22% additional custom duty on key raw material for dimer fatty acid imposed September 14, 2024 caused sharp cost escalation
items.quote: A key challenge since last 2 quarters is the 22% additional custom duty imposed on the key raw material used for manufacturing of our prime product dimer fatty acid, which came into effect on September 14, 2024.

items.statement: Could not pass on higher raw material cost to customers due to pricing pressure from Chinese competitors not subject to similar duties
items.quote: Unfortunately, the cost burden could not be passed on to customers due to pricing pressure from Chinese competitors who are not subjected to similar additi onal custom duties at their end

items.statement: Working on new raw material from vegetable oil byproduct to mitigate custom duty cost and reduce raw material cost
items.quote: It is not altogether, but it is one of the byproducts of one of the vegetable oils. So we are working on it, whereby we will be able to bring down our cost, nothing else.

items.statement: Isostearic acid export volumes expected to pick up in H1 FY26 and scale up in H2 FY26
items.quote: We anticipate a staggered increase in export volumes with the initial pickup expected in the first half of 25-26, followed by further scale up in second half.

items.statement: Confident of achieving higher capacity utilization by end of FY26
items.quote: Based on the current momentum, we are confident of achieving higher capacity utilization by end of this year.

items.statement: Isostearic acid expected to reach optimum utilization by FY27
items.quote: By next year, we should reach the optimum utilization.

items.statement: New product plant equipment ordered, expected to arrive by December, trials in January-March period
items.quote: We have ordered the equipment, which will take 6 months to come. because all these are specialty equipments. And so it will take around 6 months for us to receive the equipment and then before end of December, we should have all the equipment and we start trials in January, March period.

items.statement: Earmarked 40,000 tons of 120,000 tons installed capacity for new product family
items.quote: out of our installed capacity of 120,000 metric tons per annum in terms of throughput of raw material, we have already earmarked 1/3rd, that is 40,000 tons of capacity for this new product.

items.statement: Paint industry demand slightly down but not significant; expects revival in October-December quarter
items.quote: But a little bit of downside is there that I won't disagree with you. But it is there. I mean but no major downside is there. The way things are going on I don't think we should be bullish for the paint industry because this quarter is going to be the monsoon period. And typically, during monsoon period, paint activity is always on the lower side. So probably we can expect things to revive back in

items.statement: Isostearic acid faces global supply shortage due to biodegradable demand in developed countries
items.quote: As per our understanding, currently, there is a shortage of sup ply vis-a-vis demand because this is a biodegradable product and that is the demand in developed countries. So there is a supply shortage

items.statement: Q4 FY25 volumes increased >11% and value growth >6% quarter-on-quarter
items.quote: we have demonstrated soli d operational resilience whereby we have been able to increase our volumes in the Q4 by greater than 11% and value growth we have achieved of greater than 6% on a quarter -to-quarter basis

items.statement: Q4 FY25 revenue INR 121 crores, up 6.3% QoQ, down 25% YoY
items.quote: For the 4th Quarter under review, the revenue from operations stood at INR 121 crores, which increased by 6.3% on immediately preceding quarter and decreased 25% year-on-year.

items.statement: FY25 revenue INR 538 crores
items.quote: For the full financial year ended 2025, the revenue from operations stood at INR 538 crores

items.statement: Revenue target INR 1,000 crore for FY26 with EBITDA margin 18-20%
items.quote: Our revenue target for the next fiscal year is INR 1,000 crores with continued emphasis on maintaining or improving EBITDA margins.

items.statement: Projecting 15-20% revenue growth over next 2-3 years
items.quote: We are projecting 15% to 20% revenue growth in near next 2 to 3 years.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expected to improve from 16% to 18-20% in FY26
items.quote: We are expecting our EBITDA margins to improve from current 16% to between 18% and 20% as we are committed to increasing profitability.

items.statement: Capex of INR 116 crore planned for FY26 for IPL and Shalvis Specialities
items.quote: Capex of INR 116 crore has been planned for FY '26 for both India Pesticide and 100% subsidiary Shalvis Specialities Limited.

items.statement: Targeted capex of over INR 200 crore over 2 years with INR 52 crore at existing facility and INR 64 crore at Shalvis
items.quote: We have targeted a capex of over INR 200 crore over 2 years with planned capital expenditures of INR 52 crore at our existing facility and INR 64 crore at Shalvis Specialities Limited.

items.statement: Formulation facilities at 95% capacity utilization, technical segment utilization increased from 41% to 62%
items.quote: Our formulation production facilities have reached upward of 95% production capacity, prompting plans for expansion to further increase production capabilities. Additionally, our technical segment has experienced substantial growth with capacity utilizatio n increasing by approximately 50% from around 41% to about 62

items.statement: Sandila unit peak revenue potential INR 1,100 crore
items.quote: Peak revenue, it will be around, I think, INR 1,100 crore we can easily move from Sandila only.

items.statement: Pretilachlor capacity expansion to 8,500 tons by August, value potential over INR 300 crore
items.quote: 8,500 tons is the Pretilachlor if you take, sir, now that value here should be more than INR 300 crores.

items.statement: Pretilachlor sales over INR 100 crore in FY25, up from INR 70 crore in FY24
items.quote: It will be in excess of INR 100 crore of sales this molecule. But last year also, say, its contribution was INR 70 crore.

items.statement: Pretilachlor expected to grow 20% compounded over next 2-3 years
items.quote: We have increased capacity of this product significantly and in the process of further increasing this capacity. So, we see significant jumps at 20% compounded in next 2 to 3 years from this molecule.

items.statement: Domestic demand strong with early kharif sowing, favorable policy and positive monsoon forecast
items.quote: Domestically, our volume growth has been rigorous, supported by early kharif sowing activities, favorably government policy and a positive monsoon forecast.

items.statement: Export demand picking up as Chinese destocking tapers off, US tariff situation positive
items.quote: Export side demand is also picking up madam now. There has been -- in the last years, the oversupply was there from Chinese manufacturer, but now slowly it is getting reduced and the demand is increasing. And with this American tariff situation, we are slightly positively poised for U.S. markets.

items.statement: Raw material prices stabilized, no severe difference over short period
items.quote: And on the prices, on the raw material side, now raw material prices are getting stabilized and they are more or less stable now. There is no severe difference in the raw materials over the small period this time.

items.statement: Key product prices (Captan, Prosulfocarb, Folpet) stable with 10-15% demand growth
items.quote: Now pricing, price declined as now -- there is no price decline in this quarter. Price are very stable right now. And demand, we feel 10% to 15% demand growth in these molecules.

items.statement: Technical 65%, Formulations 35% of revenue in FY25
items.quote: 65% technical sir and 35% formulations.

items.statement: Formulations business growing >20% CAGR, bulk formulation exports increased from INR 10-12 crore to INR 50 crore
items.quote: Our Formulations business is growing, say, more than 20% compounded. In this current year, we have also exported bulk formulation, which was very small earlier. So, say, earlier, say, it was around INR 10 crore to INR 12 crore by '24, but it has increased to around INR 50 crore.

items.statement: MNC customers reducing order lead time from 6-9 months to 15 days-1 month, leading to higher inventory
items.quote: Our MNC or big customer, which used to give order for 6 to 9 months in advance, now giving orders only in 15 days to 1 month. So, we have decided to keep inventory at a slightly higher level so that we do not lose the seasonal demand of our big customers.

items.statement: Normalized working capital days expected around 220 days, down from 250 days in last quarter
items.quote: Last quarter, it was around 250 days. So, our normalized working capital should be around 220 days going forward.

items.statement: Total debt increased from INR 18 crore to INR 52 crore due to short-term borrowings, to be normalized soon
items.quote: Company's total debt increased from INR 18 crore in FY '24 to INR 52 crore in FY '25, primarily due to increase in short-term borrowings, which will be normalized soon.

items.statement: Antidumping duty on Pretilachlor recommended by Ministry of Commerce, pending notification by Ministry of Finance
items.quote: The antidumping has not been notified yet. It has been recommended by Ministry of Commerce, but it has not been notified yet.

items.statement: Received 4 technical and 19 formulation registrations from CIB India, 4 in EU/UK, 2 in USA, 2 in Australia in FY25
items.quote: During the year FY '25, we have received 4 registrations for technical products and 19 registrations for formulations from Central Insecticides Board of India and have also got our products registered across the world, 4 in European Union and United Kingdo m. And then we got 2 registrations in U.S.A. and two formulations registration in

items.statement: Export revenue INR 315 crore in FY25 (38% of total), Q4 exports INR 88 crore vs INR 38 crore YoY
items.quote: On geographical split, in FY '25, our revenue from export stood at INR 315 crore as compared to INR 269 crores in FY '24 and Domestic revenue stood at INR513 crores as compared to INR 410 crores in FY '24. During Q4, export has seen sharp recovery with turnover increasing to INR 88 crore versus INR 38 crore in same period last year.

items.statement: Export mix to remain ~38% of revenue, key markets Australia, Europe, USA, expanding to Africa and Middle East
items.quote: It will be approximately around that level only because now we are selecting products with a proper blend of domestic as well as export market. So, we don't want to depend entirely on domestic or entirely on export market.

items.statement: Revenue grew 21.3% YoY to INR 843 crore in FY25, EBITDA up 32% to INR 134 crore, PAT up 37% to INR 82 crore
items.quote: Our revenue grew significantly by 21.3% year-over-year, reaching INR 843 crore. This performance underscores our strategic clarity, effective execution and a strong differentiated product portfolio.

items.statement: Shalvis Specialities to start contributing from next quarter, built in small blocks
items.quote: It will start contributing from next quarter only. We will be building the Shalvis in small blocks and it starts with contributing step by step.

items.statement: Chinese destocking tapered off, inventory normalization underway, prices stabilized but not increasing significantly
items.quote: Chinese destocking is now tapering off. There is not much of the material now available with Chinese manufacturer. And even with the multinationals also who have bought -- overbought during the COVID period, now their inventory is also getting completely relatively over. So now the demand requirement is now coming to be little more steadier than what it was earlier.

items.statement: Industry demand showing early signs of recovery with rising customer inquiries and RFQs; broader revival expected in H2 FY26
items.quote: While overall volumes have yet to normalize, we are encouraged by the early signs of recovery reflected in a rise in customer inquiries and RFQs. These indicators strengthen our optimism for a broader industry revival in the second half of FY '26.

items.statement: Standalone revenue grew 13% in FY25; historically Tarsons has grown at 16-18% CAGR and expects similar levels in near future
items.quote: Historically, Tarsons has grown at a CAGR in the 16% to 18% category range. So I think we are still short by about 15-odd percent for further growth. So I believe that in the near future, we should see similar levels of CAGR growth for Tarsons, that is our expectation.

items.statement: Phase 1 commercial production at Panchla facility underway; Phase 2 on schedule for H2 FY26; cell culture revenue from Q4 FY26, full ramp-up FY27-28
items.quote: On the capex front, the Phase 1 of our commercial production at the new Panchla facility is already underway. And Phase 2 is on schedule to commence operations in the second half of the year. We anticipate that initial revenue contributions from the cell culture to begin in Q4 of this year and a full-scale revenue ramp-up in FY '27 and '28.

items.statement: Maintenance capex limited to INR 10-15 crores; commercial capex only for backed contracts; no further general capex planned
items.quote: So the plant maintenance and special order capex, it depends what kind of maintenance is required in each facility, but we don't foresee more than INR 10 crores to INR 15 crores of capex on maintenance. And regarding the commercial capex, it depends on what kind of orders will come from customer, what kind of commitment is there from the customer.

items.statement: Current capacity utilization 70-75%; new facilities add INR 350-400 crores incremental capacity; peak infrastructure capacity ~INR 800 crores without further capex
items.quote: Around 70% to 75%, based on our understanding of capacity utilization because we don't run dedicated equipment for all SKUs. So there are a lot of shared equipment -100, 200 SKUs running over 5 or 6 equipments, not 100, 200 SKUs running over 100, 200 equipment.

items.statement: New facility utilization: 50-60% in ~2 years, 80-90% in ~3.5-4 years
items.quote: So in the current scenario, I believe that 50% to 60% can be achieved in about 2 years and 80% to 90% in about 3.5 to 4 years.

items.statement: Standalone EBITDA margin 36.5% in FY25; expects 2-3% improvement at peak as volumes stabilize
items.quote: But for the stand-alone bit, I think we are around 36.5%, 37% is where we stand. There could be improvements by about 2% or 3% at peak as we are able to bring in the volumes and stabilize operational costs.

items.statement: Consumables, especially liquid handling, are best-selling; cell culture consumables line being commercialized for CDMO/CRO applications
items.quote: would be great. Aryan Sehgal: We just mentioned that we have produced [inaudible 0:37:22] consumables. So that's the entire line, which is used on [inaudible 0:37:29] as well as production laboratories for various cell culture applications

items.statement: CDMO segment demand encouraging; winning orders through weekly/monthly agreements; no contractual capex needed for most CDMO products
items.quote: Yes. So the business is not structured that way. You generally have contracts with them, which are not prewritten contracts, but there are agreements between these companies and Tarsons and various other suppliers of labware products. And orders are placed on a weekly, monthly basis by these companies based on whatever their ordering pattern is.

items.statement: Nerbe acquisition to serve as European hub; integration starting Q1 FY26, ramping through Q4; replacing third-party products with Tarsons manufactured offerings
items.quote: Yes. From this year, we will start the thing. So we will find initial transfer and integration starting from Q1, and it will ramp up gradually till Q4. And then over the next year, I think we would reach a full ramp-up of what Nerbe is today.

items.statement: Consolidated depreciation expected INR 80-85 crores in FY26; standalone depreciation higher due to Panchla capitalization
items.quote: I think, under a put-to-use kind of condition, we expect FY '26 depreciation will be in the range of INR 80 crores to INR 85 crores.

items.statement: International business expected to grow faster than domestic in FY26; Europe focus via Nerbe; US tariff situation uncertain with wait-and-watch approach from buyers
items.quote: We are expecting domestic to grow as well. But as the gentleman had asked in the previous question, at this time, it looks like the exports would have a better growth than the domestic.

items.statement: No cell culture approvals yet; commercial supply from Q4 FY26, approvals expected within same quarter
items.quote: Commercially, we would start supplying cell culture products by Q4 to customers, and we expect that by then, the quality level should be at par. And within that quarter, we should start receiving approvals.

items.statement: Radiation sterilization facility commissioned end July; warehouse operational June/July; in-sourcing to save costs as volumes scale
items.quote: The radiation plant we commercialized and commissioned in end of July, and we will start commercial radiation by August. The warehouse is ready. We are just getting the racking and other things done. So June end, first week of July, the warehouse starts and by July end, the radiation plant gets commissioned.

items.statement: Employee costs rising due to inflationary hires and new facility staffing; costs proportional to production ramp-up at Panchla
items.quote: But going forward, the additional employees, wha tever comes into the Panchla facility, that will only be on the basis of the production. So whatever minimum cost is required, that we have already done. But going forward, the employee cost, wages cost will be proportional and as per the production plan and as per the sales order for the Panchla facility

items.statement: US tariff policy changing daily; buyers adopting wait-and-watch approach despite India's relative tariff advantage over China
items.quote: I think at this point of time, the entire world is very unsure about the way this has been handled. It's not been very consistent, right? News is changing on daily basis. So people are also preferring a wait-and-watch approach because they don't know what's going to happen tomorrow.

items.statement: Asset turnover historically 0.7-0.8x (not 1.5-1.6x as per pre-Ind AS); peak revenue potential INR 750-800 crores by FY28-29
items.quote: Just wanted to clarify that when we got listed, at that point of time, we have converted from IND GAAP to Ind AS. At that point of time, our net asset has been transferred to Ind AS as a gross asset. So whatever financials you are seeing, you are always calculating on the basis of my brought forward fi gure. But actually, we always had the asset turn ratio in the range of 0.7 to 0.8

items.statement: Gross margin pressure offset by fixed cost leverage; highest ever quarterly sales drove EBITDA margin expansion despite gross margin drop
items.quote: The point is that if you see this quarter sales, this is the highest ever sales we reported in the stand-alone entity. That resulted into higher gross profit. And as our fixed cost, all the employee costs and other costs are fixed, that resulted into higher EBITDA margin.

items.statement: International market crowded with Asian exporters (India, Korea, China); Tarsons less established than in domestic market; scaling exports takes time to build trust
items.quote: There are various companies available to export from the Asian belt, which includes India, South Korea, China. And it is a crowded market where most of our business is focused on O EMs and in certain countries, it's focused on branded business. So we aren't as established and as strong a player as we are in the domestic market and hence, scaling up does take time as we get more and more acceptance

items.statement: Snowman Logistics capex of Rs. 100-150 crore per year, 80% debt-funded; Gateway Distriparks capex of Rs. 30 crore per year excluding new terminals
items.value: 100-150 crore per year (Snowman), 30 crore per year (Gateway)
items.quote: Rs. 100 crores to Rs. 150 crores per year. Even Gateway is Rs. 30 crores per year. So, say Rs. 60 crores for the next two years. This is basically some warehousing capacity and vehicles.

items.statement: Gateway Distriparks plans Rs. 30 crore annual capex excluding new ICD terminals; new terminal acquisitions will be announced separately
items.quote: So, maybe around Rs. 30 crores, other than the new terminals.

items.statement: Gateway Distriparks evaluating asset-light BTS model for new locations alongside own facility development like Lucknow model
items.quote: apart from the CAPEX which we are planning, which will be for buying land and building up our own facilities, similar to our Lucknow model, we are also discussing BTS, where someone else builds a warehouse and we do a long-term lease for more locations.

items.statement: Snowman warehousing margins declined to 11% due to Park 'n' Pay model growth (500x, 60,000 pallets) and Amazon business exit; 5PL margins now 6-8% vs previous 8-9% target
items.quote: So, some of it is contributed by the Park 'n' Pay model. This year we have grown 500 x in Park 'n' Pay model wherein close to 60,000 pallets were outsourced and built. So, wherein the margins are lower, thus the percentage margin is pulled down on the warehousing part.

items.statement: Gateway Rail EBITDA per TEU ~Rs. 9,500-9,600; CFS EBITDA per TEU ~Rs. 1,300-1,400 for Q4 FY25
items.quote: Yes, so roughly it's about Rs. 9,500 - 9,600 for the rail side and say Rs. 1,300 - 1,400 for the CFS side.

items.statement: Rail volumes settled at 92-93k TEUs/quarter; NCR and Ludhiana markets flat overall; growth from market share gains; Q1 FY26 expected better than low Q1 FY25
items.quote: For rail, if we see now last two, three quarters, we have kind of settled at this 92 -93,000 TEUs per quarter, and about Rs. 9,500-9,700 crore range for EBITDA per TEU. So, it's fairly sticky around this number.

items.statement: Snowman warehousing ex-Amazon grew ~5% YoY; temperature control business flat; meat/seafood/poultry segments down 15% YoY
items.quote: If we remove Amazon business alone, from the Park 'n' Pay and the dry business, it's around 5% increase we can see in a warehousing business, which is exactly been compensated by loss of Amazon business in the topline, which is around Rs. 10-11 crores, works out to be.

items.statement: Snowman added Unilever (ice cream distribution in Northeast from Guwahati) and Kopi Kenangan (Indonesian coffee chain, 2 outlets) as new 5PL customers
items.quote: So, this year we have added two new customers. One is Unilever and the other one is an Indonesian coffee chain by the name Kopi Kenangan. And that will start reflecting, I mean, it has already reflected in our books this year, and it will further increase the volumes in the coming years.

items.statement: Snowman 5PL customer selection emphasizes due diligence on growth plans, stability, global presence, and contract structures with safety guarantees; NDA prevents disclosing specific securities
items.quote: See, we have done our due diligence when we speak with a customer in terms of their plans in India, their stability, plus we see their global presence as well. So, at the pace Kopi is expanding globally and the way their contract is structured, it keeps us quite covered in all aspects and we try and put in our best effort in terms of doing a detailed due diligence, to ensure that the company's int

items.statement: Snowman remains pan-India cold storage capacity leader; regional competition exists; no current 5PL competition but expected as industry matures
items.quote: So, as of now, on a pan-India basis, we are still the leader by a large margin in terms of capacity. On a regional level, at every new location, there are some col d storages who we compete with. And on the 5PL side, we don't have any competition as of now. But the scen ario can change as the industry is maturing, and as more and more shift is happening from unorganized to organized

items.statement: Gateway Rail Q4 FY25 market share: NCR 17%, Ludhiana 27% (up from 23-24%), Kashipur 37%; Full year: NCR 17%, Ludhiana 25%, Kashipur 28%
items.quote: So, in Quarter 4, our market share at NCR has been steady at 17%. And at Ludhiana, so we have regained our market share to 27%, which last year it was as low as like 24%-25% (to be read as 23% -24%). In the Uttarakhand market at Kashipur, we have regained market share to 37%.

items.statement: Gateway Rail double-stacking at 41% in Q4 FY25 (up from 38%), targeting 42-43% going forward; Faridabad double-stacking driving gains
items.quote: In terms of the double stacking, after this double stacking which has happened at Faridabad, our double stacking percentage has increased to 41% in Q4. And if we split this further into different ICDs, so earlier we were in the range of 40% of Faridabad volum es, now it is gaining . So, overall, just wanted to tell you the overall 41% is there , and earlier it was around 38% . So, we Gateway Distr

items.statement: Snowman contract renewals achieving 4% pricing increase; overall pricing decline due to mix change (temperature-controlled products down)
items.quote: But on average, across most of our existing customers who we do renewals with, then about 4% to 5% pricing increase we have this year. 4%. But the mix changes. That's why on an overall pricing basis, you will see the drop, but contract basis with customers, we are able to get increases.

items.statement: Western DFC JNPT corridor completion expected by March 2026 (site says December 2025); Mundra congestion and double-stack restrictions hurt rail volumes; no commercial advantage from DFC yet
items.quote: So, hopefully once the JNPT Corridor is completed, which now they are saying is, as per the site they are mentioning December, but as per our sources it might take another couple of months. So, it should happen by March. So, then only we will see 100% advantage. Then there is a possibility of some shift from road to rail.

items.statement: Gateway payables variation due to business mix changes, primarily 5PL business; Snowman trade receivables up with turnover, Rs. 4 crore provision covering 180 days
items.quote: So, I think it's just a function of business. Depending on the business mix at that time, it varies, terms vary, customer to customer, whoever is growing at a different pace for the quarter. And this is primarily on account of the 5PL business.

items.statement: Snowman capex funding maintains 80% debt / 20% internal accruals model
items.quote: Yes, we are still of the same opinion that we go with 80-20 model. 20 will be from our internal accruals, 80 will be funded through loans.

items.statement: Gateway Distriparks holding Rs. 100+ crore cash; no immediate plans to increase Snowman stake or merge; surplus cash may fund dividends or future capex
items.quote: Every year there will be certain CAPEX which is required in GDL. And we have a track record of paying dividend also. So, based on the cash flows, if and when there is any surplus, then we could consider it. But as of now we have not announced any plans.

items.statement: Snowman trade receivables provision of Rs. 4 crore covers 180 days; majority receivables from current year
items.quote: And we carry a provision of approximately Rs. 4 crores, which is covering 180 days. But all the majority is from the current year itself.

items.statement: Gateway Jaipur land acquisition under Benami Property Act litigation; management confident of favorable tribunal outcome within 1-2 years; no settlement scheme available
items.quote: We still believe we did it the right way. We have a good top legal firm also advising us, who believes that we have a strong case. We are hopeful within the next year or two, for whate ver reason, this got caught in this legal case. But according to us, it's still fine

items.statement: Snowman became subsidiary in December 2024; full-year consolidation added Rs. 145 crore revenue, Rs. 25 crore EBITDA, Rs. 3 crore PBT, Rs. 3.5 crore PAT
items.quote: Then another big change is that in December, Snowman Logistics became a subsidiary. So, now it gets line by line consolidated. So, for the full year, we have Rs. 145 crores of revenue, about Rs. 25 crores in EBITDA and PBT of Rs. 3 crores and Rs. PAT of 3.5 cr ores on account of consolidation

items.statement: One-time stamp duty provision of Rs. 12.8 crore for past Gateway-Gateway Rail merger; non-cash goodwill impairment of Rs. 258 crore (net Rs. 131 crore gain for year) due to share price/DCF
items.quote: There was a big one-time hit on, it's a provision, it's not a cash payout yet, but of about Rs. 12.8 crores. This is on account of the merger that we did within the group between Gateway Distriparks and Gateway Rail at the time and one more group entity.

items.statement: CFS revenue accounting change: Rs. 46 crore full-year impact from gross to net revenue treatment for discounts; FY25 CFS revenue higher than FY24 after adjustment
items.quote: So, basically CFS revenue, it appears to be negative, but actually this is on account of change in accounting method between gross revenue, net revenue of some certain discount. So, for the full year, this figure is about Rs. 46 crores. So, if you add that back, then FY '25 revenue for CFS vertical would be higher than FY '24.

items.statement: Depreciation reassessment in Q4 FY25 reduced charge by Rs. 3.5-4 crore; will continue as base for FY26
items.quote: We have only done it in Q4. We have not done it backdated from Q1. It's between Rs. 3.5 crores to Rs. 4 crores.

items.statement: Aspires to achieve EBITDA margin of 17-19% within a year, factoring in 20-40 bps non-BIS inventory liquidation impact
items.quote: So, over a year's time for sure, like we should fall within the range of what we've guided.

items.statement: FY25 EBITDA margin expanded 120 bps to 16.1% driven by lower SG&A and normalized costs
items.quote: EBITDA margin expanded by 120 bps year on year to 16.1% in FY25 owing to lower SG&A, once again, the last year, numbers included one of provisions for inventory and receivables and hence the SG and A was higher last year, the current year SG&A numbers are more normalized

items.statement: Gross margin improved 20 bps to 52.3% in FY25 due to procurement and production efficiencies
items.quote: Our gross margins were at 52.3%, an improvement of 20 bps from last year driven by procurement and production efficiencies.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 revenue grew 11.5% YoY to INR 406 crores; distribution up 9.6%, online up 15.2%
items.quote: Our operational revenue grew by around 11.5% year on year to INR 406 crores in quarter 4, driven by higher distribution which has registered a growth of 9.6% and also, the online channel which has grown 15.2%.

items.statement: FY25 volume grew 12.3% to 24.9 million pairs; ASP declined 2% to INR 639 due to open footwear mix and accessories
items.quote: The company sold approximately 24.9 million pairs in FY25, up around 12.3% year on year. The average selling price stood at INR 639 per pair versus INR 652 last year, a drop of around 2%.

items.statement: Sneaker portfolio grew 150% YoY in FY25, reaching 8.5% volume contribution; expects continued expansion in FY26 with new Haridwar plant
items.quote: Our sneaker portfolio saw an impressive growth of 150% versus FY24, reaffirming our commitment to deliver stylish, high-quality footwear that remains accessible.

items.statement: Haridwar II facility for sneaker uppers commenced commercial production in March 2025; INR 21 crore investment amortized over 15 years
items.quote: We also commenced the commercial production from our Haridwar II facility for manufacturing high quality uppers for sneakers during March 2025.

items.statement: Added three leasehold assets in Q4: Kulana warehouse for online, Haridwar II facility, and raw material warehouse
items.quote: We took a warehouse in Kulana for our online business chief warehouse and also, we have taken this Haridwar II facility for the sneakers. So that is on a lease on premise and also, we took a raw material warehouse house, so we have added three leasehold assets in this quarter.

items.statement: Net working capital days improved from 92 in FY24 to 71 in FY25; targets 90-95 days as optimal level
items.quote: Notably, our net working capital days improved from 92 in FY24 to 71 in FY25, reflecting our focus on operational efficiency.

items.statement: Distributor inventory maintained at 100-110 days; primary sales mirror secondary on replenishment model
items.quote: We maintain around, I would say 100 to 110 days of inventory. It continues to be same and so fair reflection of that it's primarily working on a replenishment model, which means that whatever we are able to sell secondary, we are replenishing through primaries.

items.statement: Price hike taken on open footwear in Q4 FY25 vs last year; no further hikes planned for Q2-Q3 FY26 as NPD products priced accordingly
items.quote: Yes, we have taken actually just on the open category side on the open footwear versus last year quarter four, we've taken a price hike which has you know definitely helped us maintain the margin profile as well overall and I mean going forward, we generally do take a price hike at the end of the season, so now there is, you know, going to be a higher contribution of our NPD products, which anyway

items.statement: Open footwear mix increased from 14.2% to 15.2% in FY25; accessories introduced at INR 140 ASP diluting overall ASP
items.quote: As I mentioned, the open footwear mix increased from 14.2% last year to 15.2% this year. So, that's the kind of contribution it has on our business.

items.statement: Men's category 80% revenue share, women 13.3%, kids 6.7% in FY25; women's ASP premiumization driving mix improvement
items.quote: So, this category makes for men and women, Shraddha is pretty much similar to last year. It's 81% or rather, 80% has been the contribution for the entire year for men and about 13.3% for women and kids would be 6.7%.

items.statement: Active retail outlets reached 23,000 in Q4 FY25 vs 19,600 YoY; targets 1,500 counter additions annually
items.quote: By end of this quarter, I mean Q4, our reach was at around 23,000 odd outlets versus 19,600 outlets last year.

items.statement: Distributor count consolidated to 300-350 range; focus on outlet productivity and reach expansion
items.quote: The distributor count remains in the range of 300 to 350. Yes, we have consolidated certain geographies and hence the number of distributors have come down but the measurable output KPI is that how good we are expanding our reach.

items.statement: Chinese imports volume dropped significantly; BIS implementation extended to July 2026 slowing liquidation but finite inventory remains
items.quote: Yes, I mean the imports have certainly dried up, the overall volume has dropped from China. We do see some impact of that. But honestly to quantify that is still kind of early.

items.statement: Non-BIS inventory liquidation slower than expected; 20-40 bps margin impact expected in FY26 from residual stock
items.quote: We were expecting to liquidate a big portion of it by March end but there has it's been slightly slower than that, but it is all like, you know, under control and it's basically we're expecting you know in line with 20 to 40 bps of a margin, you know hit on in this specter of the non-BIS inventory in the coming year and nothing more than that.

items.statement: Company remains debt-free; ROCE 22.3%, ROE 17.2% as of March 31, 2025
items.quote: Our balance sheet continues to demonstrate strength and robust return ratios such as ROCE and ROE of 22.3% and 17.2% respectively as on 31st March 2025 and we continue to be a debt free company.

items.statement: SAP went live on April 4, 2025 to streamline operations, enhance inventory control and improve planning
items.quote: In parallel, we have gone live with SAP on the 4th of April 2025 to streamline operations, enhance inventory control and improve planning and forecasting, laying the foundation for scalable and agile growth.

items.statement: Metro and Tier-1 demand dipped in Q4 vs rural/Tier-2-3; South and Central regions flattish while North/East/West grew
items.quote: Metros and tier ones in quarter four, I would say has done, the saliency has slightly dropped so versus the rural and Tier 2 and Tier 3 counters so, versus you know year on year and so there has been some dip I think in terms of consumer demand in terms in metros and tier 1.

items.statement: Advertising spend at 8.4% of revenue (INR 135 crores) in FY25; plans to maintain 8.4-8.5% in FY26 funded by ASP increases
items.quote: So, I would say that you know we don't foresee this going down at this point, maybe in FY26 will continue to maintain this number at 8.4, 8.5%. Basically, a percent increase from what we spent in FY24, but you know this should be funded from the ASP increase also.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 PAT grew 7.3% to INR 35 crores; PAT margin 8.5% vs 8.9% due to higher depreciation from DIP line impairment
items.quote: PAT grew by 7.3% year on year to INR 35 crores during quarter 4 FY25 and PAT margins stood at 8.5% versus 8.9% last year. A slight depletion in PAT margin is primarily due to a higher depreciation owing to impairment of our dip lines.

items.statement: Board recommended final dividend of Rs 12 per share for FY25 subject to shareholder approval
items.quote: I would like to share that the Board has recommended a Final Dividend of Rs. 12 per share in its meeting held on 27th May, 2025, subject to shareholders approval.

items.statement: Individual new business premium grew 8.28% YoY to INR 62,495 crore, highest ever in LIC history
items.quote: The Individual New Business Premium Income for year ended March 31st, 2025 was INR 62,495 Crore which was INR 57,716 Crore for the corresponding year of last year thereby registering a growth of 8.28% on Year on Year basis.

items.statement: Group total premium decreased 1.28% YoY to INR 1,69,112 crore
items.quote: The Group Business total premium income for year ended March 31 st, 2025 was INR 1,69,112 Crore comprising of New Business Premium of INR 1,64,262 Crore

items.statement: Market share by first year premium income was 57.05% (individual 37.46%, group 71.19%) per IRDAI
items.quote: Our market share by First Year Premium Income for year ended March 31 st, 2025 was 57.05% (as per IRDAI) as compared to 58.87% for the similar period ended March 31 st, 2024

items.statement: Non-par share of individual APE rose to 27.69% from 18.32% YoY, non-par APE grew 50.28% to INR 10,581 crore
items.quote: Further, of the Individual APE, the Par business accounts for INR 27,636 Crore and Non Par amounts to INR 10,581 Crore. Therefore, our Non Par share of Individual APE is 27.69% and Par share of Individual APE is 72.31% for year ended March 31st, 2025.

items.statement: Individual segment VNB margin touched ~20.9%, up from 15.2% previously
items.quote: But I can -- just as an indicator, I can indicate to you, that VNB margins in non-participating products are the highest, followed by participating and other type of businesses or business being there. But as an indicator, what we can indicate that in the individual business segment, the VNB margin, we are almost touching 21% or so.

items.statement: AUM grew 6.45% YoY to INR 54,52,297 crore, an increase of INR 3,30,410 crore
items.quote: Assets Under Management (AUM) as on March 31st, 2025 was INR 54,52,297 Crore as compared to INR 51,21,887 Crore as on March 31st 2024. Therefore, our AUM has registered a growth of 6.45% on Year on Year basis.

items.statement: Indian Embedded Value grew 6.81% YoY to INR 7,76,876 crore, 3-year CAGR of 12.8%
items.quote: The Indian Embedded Value (IEV) as on March 31st, 2025 has been determined as INR 7,76,876 Crore as compared to INR 7,27,344 Crore as on March 31st, 2024. Therefore, IEV has registered an increase of 6.81% on Year on Year basis.

items.statement: Overall expense ratio decreased 315 bps YoY to 12.42%
items.quote: For the year ended March 31st, 2025, the overall expense ratio was 12.42% as compared to 15.57% for the same period last year. Therefore, there is a decrease of 315 basis points on Year on Year basis.

items.statement: Agent count grew 5.1% YoY to 14.87 lakh with net addition of 72,000+ agents
items.quote: As on March 31st, 2025, the total number of agents was 14,86,851 as compared to 14,14,743 as on March 31st 2024. We have made a net addition of more than 72,000 agents in the last one year.

items.statement: Bancassurance and alternate channel new business premium grew 57.96% YoY to INR 3,496.10 crore, share of individual NBP rose to 5.59%
items.quote: Bancassurance and Alternate Channel (including Micro Insurance) collected New Business Premium Income of INR 3,496.10 Crore for the year ended March 31st, 2025 which was INR 2,213.22 Crore for the year ended March 31st, 2024 registering a growth of 57.96% on a Year on Year basis.

items.statement: Launched 51 new products (33 individual, 12 group, 5 individual riders, 1 group rider) post IRDAI 2024 regulations effective Oct 1, 2024
items.quote: Post the implementation of the IRDAI (Insurance Products) Regulations, 2024, effective from October 1st, 2024, we have launched a comprehensive suite of 51 products till March 31st, 2025, which include 33 individual products, 12 group products, 5 individual riders and 1 group rider.

items.statement: Solvency ratio improved to 2.11 from 1.98 YoY
items.quote: The Solvency Ratio as on March 31st, 2025 improved to 2.11 as against 1.98 on March 31st, 2024.

items.statement: 13th month persistency on premium basis declined to 74.84% from 77.66% YoY; 61st month improved to 63.12% from 60.88%
items.quote: On premium basis, the persistency for 13th, 25th, 37th, 49th and 61st month upto the quarter ended March 31st, 2025 stands at 74.84%, 70.99%, 66.11%, 61.51% and 63.12%, respectively, as compared to 77.66%, 71%, 65.47%, 66.31% and 60.88%, respectively upto the quarter ended March 31st 2024.

items.statement: VNB sensitivity to interest rates higher due to non-par book backed by fixed securities; RFR fell 30-35 bps causing 280 bps negative margin impact
items.quote: Regarding the economic assumptions in the VNB walk, it's mainly due to the fall of RFR over the duration. We have observed that the RFR has fallen between 30 and 35 bps over the duration. And that is what has reflected in a negative 280 bps in the margin.

items.statement: Started hedging non-par book in March 2025, will increase pace in current year for larger coverage
items.quote: We have started in last March. This March, we have just started. In the current year also, we are going out at a greater pace – Dinesh Pant: And we continue to focus on this and possibly as well when the opportunities are there, we will continue to focus for larger coverage through hedging of our non-par portfolio

items.statement: Opposes open architecture; believes captive distribution channel takes time and cost to build, agents have social security benefits
items.quote: See open architecture, our stand is very clear. This is not a good idea, open architecture because to develop a captive distribution channel, not only for insurance, but for any distribution channel, it takes a lot of time, energy, cost, everything.

items.statement: Bima Sakhi Yojana appointed 1.49 lakh women who sold 4.71 lakh policies and procured INR 604.57 crore NBP between Dec 9, 2024 and Mar 31, 2025
items.quote: With great happiness I would like to inform you that till March 31st, 2025, 1.49 lakh women have been appointed as Bima Sakhis who have sold around 4.71 lakh policies and procured New Business Premium of INR 604.57 crore.

items.statement: Profit after tax grew 18.38% YoY to INR 48,151 crore
items.quote: The Profit after Tax (PAT) for the year ended March 31st, 2025 was INR 48,151 Crore as compared to INR 40,676 Crore for year ended March 31st 2024 registering a growth of 18.38% on Year on Year basis.

items.statement: ULIP share grew from ~2% to ~6% of individual APE due to customer demand, but not primary profitability driver
items.quote: ULIP has grown significantly, almost 2% share to almost 6%. We have grown significantly in ULIP because it has been the demand from the side of the customers, and that has been the flavour of the market.

items.statement: Wage expense lower due to one-time pension provision for wage revision in prior year not repeated
items.quote: In the last year, there was a wage revision that happened. And accordingly, based on the wage revision, we had to make a provision for the pension and other retirement liabilities that happened in the last year, which is not repeated in the current year.

items.statement: IEV negative investment variance of INR 30,000 crore driven 50% by RFR fall and 50% by MTM changes
items.quote: As regards to the -- in the negative investment variance, there are 2 parts to that. One is the RFR fall which is -- take about 50% of the fall. And the second is the MTM changes which have happened during the year. So these two totally contributed a negative variance of INR 30,000 crores.

items.statement: Guinness World Record for most life insurance policies sold in 24 hours: 5,88,107 policies by 4,52,839 agents on Jan 20, 2025
items.quote: LIC has achieved GUINNESS WORLD RECORDS Title for the “MOST LIFE INSURANCE POLICIES SOLD IN 24 HOURS” by selling 5,88,107 policies across India on 20 th January, 2025. Also, this feat was achieved by active participation of 4,52,839 agents on a single day on January 20th

items.statement: Death claims up 7.93% YoY to INR 24,420 crore; maturity claims up 14.02% to INR 2,37,313 crore
items.quote: On an amount basis during the year ended March 31st, 2025, the total maturity claims were INR 2,37,313 Crore and the total death claims were INR 24,420 Crores. On a comparable basis for the last year ended March 31st 2024, the maturity claims were INR 2,08,136 Crore and death claims were INR 22,625 Crore.

items.statement: Highest ever bonus to policyholders at INR 56,190.24 crore
items.quote: Highest ever bonus to policyholders at INR 56,190.24 Crore.

items.statement: Aim to cross Rs 1,000 crore revenue with focus on quality and margin, not just volume
items.quote: We aim to cross 1000 crores in revenue with strong focus in quality and margin, not just scheme.

items.statement: Target to double services revenue share within next 2-3 years
items.quote: We want to double our share of services in the revenue of our business within next two 2-3 years.

items.statement: Current order book stands at approximately Rs 38-40 crore
items.quote: With an order book of approximately 38 to 40 crores, a sharper services mix and a passionate team by our side, I truly believe our best days are ahead.

items.statement: Order book comprises cloud security, audio video solutions, and unified communication projects for large educational institutions
items.quote: It consists of couple of cases where we have something in UC which is unified communication and conversation. We are doing certain projects for large educational institutions, which is approximately 10 to 15 crore type, which is Phase 2 of what we had done earlier in Q4 so that's on hand, which is been on the verge of getting executed and everything is in place and another 15 to 20 crores we're wo

items.statement: Q4 gross margin decline to 7.8% due to one-time provision and dollar cost impact
items.quote: So, gross margin decline primarily in Q4 is for one-time provision which we have made. So that would have as an impact on the decline. Aditya Shah: OK. Chetankumar Timbadia: And also, the cost has been so with the dollar cost, a lot of factors which played into that so that also played into this, so it's not a single pointer, but a couple of factors which has looked into this

items.statement: AI and 5G driving more complex solutions with higher delivery expectations and security needs
items.quote: With 5G, AI, uh, the solutions and offerings are getting more I would call it more focused or more exactly to the point which a customer needs addressing that right problem or the need of that and also getting more and more complex in the nature plus the delivery, the expectancy is higher and with it also comes lot of risk which opens up and need to defend that is also opening up.

items.statement: Current revenue split is 81% product and 19% services (~Rs 100 crore services revenue)
items.quote: Segmental thing product to services 81 to 19% is what we are doing it and hopefully that with 19 percentage turns out to approximately 100 crore rupees in revenue.

items.statement: Plan to build customized services around each product to optimize customer deployment
items.quote: As per the plans is whatever the products which we are having, we are seeing and trying to build the model where we can add services to the customer in such a fashion, he is able to use the product or the solution to the optimum.

items.statement: Customer retention over 95% due to round-the-clock support and core infrastructure products with 3-5 year lifecycle
items.quote: Our customer retention is over 95% because of our round the clock support and strong service commitments including India's digital momentum isn't going to slow down.

items.statement: Supporting domestic MNC customers globally for their international operations
items.quote: We are also supporting our domestic couple of domestic customers globally also for their operations which are Indian MNCS spread across the globe.

items.statement: Planning expansion into Middle East and African markets to service existing customers
items.quote: As far as ourselves spreading the directly, yes, we plan to spread ourselves to Middle East and African markets, which is the need according to service our existing customer and as far as the faster growing market both ways.

items.statement: Open to acquiring niche capabilities in AI analytics and managed detection services
items.quote: We are open to acquiring niche capabilities, especially in AI analytics and managed detection services.

items.statement: Zscaler data security specialization places company among few allied partners in India with this skillset, alongside large integrators like Tata, Hitachi, PwC, Deloitte
items.quote: Yes, this kind of skill sets are there only with very large integrators like Tatas or the Hitachi's or entities of the world or maybe or PWC or Deloitte type of world. The mid-sized partner like ours, we are the only one of them who has the specific skillset to rule this out and support it.

items.statement: Cybersecurity market expected to reach nearly US $700 billion by 2032
items.quote: Cybersecurity is growing as a fast and it's expected to reach nearly US $700 billion by 2032.

items.statement: Addressable market focuses on large enterprise customers with complex networks across nation or globe
items.quote: We are addressing market where the solutions or the product or the technology or the offering, whatever you call it, we are looking at to serve the top corporates or enterprise customers who have large networks across the nation or across the globe.

items.statement: Recognitions help attract right talent and build stronger relationships with global technology leaders
items.quote: These milestones do more than just looking good on paper. To help us attract right talent, will trust faster and build stronger relationship with global technology leaders.

items.statement: ESG and sustainability not materially affecting software and electronics hardware solutions
items.quote: So, Sana, we are not into that kind of product and solution because we are more of a software and electronics is some hardware components. So ESG and sustainability doesn't affect or touch our solutions much.

items.statement: Dollar cost fluctuations impacted Q4 gross margins alongside one-time provision
items.quote: And also, the cost has been so with the dollar cost, a lot of factors which played into that so that also played into this, so it's not a single pointer, but a couple of factors which has looked into this.

items.statement: Actively considering AI-driven products and solutions for existing customer base, discussing partnerships for AI technologies
items.quote: In the AI portion also, we are actively considering certain products and solution which are more AI driven as an offering to our existing customer base, which will help them to make their infrastructure in terms of whatever they invested in IT and audio video so and AI per say now has penetrated every product and every technology, so whatever brands and offerings, current vendors, current partners

items.statement: Ranked 267th on Financial Times high-growth companies Asia-Pacific list for third consecutive year

items.statement: Expect repeat business from Nyati Engineering and A2 Green Energy if execution satisfactory; relationship works both ways.
items.quote: Absolutely. See, what happens is when you are -- when you get associated to somebody, you give them a good job, then you do expect a lot of return coming up.

items.statement: Building internal engineering and project management capacity to scale solar EPC; R&D and digital tools enhancement underway.
items.quote: We are now building the internal capacity, both in engineering and project management to scale up in this space.

items.statement: Solar EPC tenders expected in Rajasthan in Q2 FY26; PSUs directed to invest in solar; active participation in upcoming bids.
items.quote: In fact, a larger volume of tenders want to come out in Rajasthan, which has just been put on hold. So maybe probably we would see them in the quarter 2 or something.

items.statement: FY25 standalone net profit INR11.75 crores, up 99.58% YoY; EPS INR7.8, up 66.31%; consolidated net profit INR11.76 crores, up 99.44% YoY.
items.quote: FY '25 total income of INR171.28 crores, EBITDA at INR19.59 crores and a net profit of INR11.75 crores, up 99.58% year-on-year.

items.statement: Airport electrification opportunity: 11-12 major airports recently tendered; Udaipur won, Hisar in advanced talks; 7 airports in Maharashtra, regional connectivity expanding.
items.quote: There are almost major 11 or 12 airports that have been very recently floated and awarded about 6, 8 months back. Out of that, one was Udaipur, which we've already bagged.

items.statement: Company completed 50 years of operations in 2025; leveraging legacy to scale into EHV, solar, airport, and digital infrastructure segments.
items.quote: This year, we proudly marked a significant milestone, 50 years of excellence in delivering integrated power solutions.

items.statement: Expects positive EBITDA in die-casting by end of FY26
items.quote: We anticipate that this transition will lead us to positive EBITDA by end of financial year '26.

items.statement: Targets 15-20% growth in domestic India electronics, 12-13% export growth, 14-15% Lumel SA growth in FY26
items.quote: India business, Rishabh business, the expectation for domestic is about 20%, domestic I am saying, which is 50% of Rishabh's business. Export, I would say, about 12%, 13% because of what is going on in Europe, etcetera. And Lumel SA business, I would say, around 14%, 15%, again, based on what is going around.

items.statement: Targets INR 100 crore EBITDA from electronics businesses in FY26 if Alucast losses arrested
items.quote: For the next year, if we increase these two businesses, which we are damn sure for 15% to 20% on Lumel SA and this one with around 15% to 20% EBITDA. So we can generate about INR100 crores of EBITDA, this is quite achievable, possible.

items.statement: Capex of INR 70-80 crores over next 2 years for India buildings and Lumel SA SMT line
items.quote: So about INR 60 crores plus INR 20 crores, around INR 70 crores, INR 80 crores is the capex, which we can expect on the top line for the next 2 years.

items.statement: Two new buildings at Nashik adding 67,000 sq ft and 82,000 sq ft (6-story), 110% built-up area increase

items.statement: Standalone Rishabh India adjusted EBITDA margin 16.8% in FY25, Q4 21.8%
items.quote: On the EBITDA margin front, the adjusted EBITDA margins were 21.8% for Q4 FY '25 and 16.8% for the full year FY '25.

items.statement: Alucast reducing auto exposure from 40-45% to 20-25% of portfolio; negotiating price corrections and new non-auto projects
items.quote: Looking ahead, our strategy involves scaling d own the automotive segment from approximately 40%, 45%, which is currently to about 20%, 25% of our aluminum die-casting

items.statement: Electronics business 9% revenue growth with 15.5% EBITDA margin (post ESOP) in FY25; Alucast revenue down 2.7% due to conscious auto reduction
items.quote: The electronics business revenue at Rishabh India and Lumel SA grew at 9% with reported EBITDA margins of 15.5% post adjustment of ESOP costs for FY '25. The aluminum die cast showed a dip in revenues to the tune of 2.7%, primarily on account of a conscious effort to reduce the low-margin automotive business.

items.statement: Alucast targeting non-auto customers like Siemens, ABB, Endress+Hauser, Danfoss; new projects take 6-12 months to launch
items.quote: We have a big customer base, about 20 giant groups like we are talking about Siemens, ABB, Endress+Hauser, these are kind of -- Danfoss. These are our customers. So we're going to them and trying to -- where we are

items.statement: Lumel Alucast withholding tax assessment in Poland classified as one-off provision; outcome may be favorable per tax counsel
items.quote: Further in Lumel Alucast, we have withholding tax assessment or Polish tax authorities, in line with our conservative financial reporting practices, we have classified the associated provisions as one-off item in our financial statements. items.statement: US subsidiary revenue $2M in FY25, targeting similar growth to reach $5-6M; UK flat with slight negative EBITDA, expected improvement

items.statement: Acquired 100% of MICROSYS (Czech SCADA software) in August 2024 to offer complete automation solutions
items.quote: In order to offer more value add to our customers, we acquired 100% shares of MICROSYS, a Czech Republic based company. This is specialized in SCADA software development. This acquisition helps us to give our customers complete comprehensive solution along with our high-end products. And we acquired this company in August 2024.

items.statement: Consolidated net debt-free with INR 1,022 million net cash and INR 650 million operating cash flow as of March 31, 2025
items.quote: On the consolidated level, we remain net debt-free with a strong balance sheet. The net cash and cash equivalents as of 31st March 2025 stand at INR 1,022 million, a healthy cash flow from operations is INR 650 million.

items.statement: Commissioned 1.5 MW solar plant at Lumel Alucast to reduce energy costs; European energy costs up substantially in last 2 years
items.quote: Moreover, in line with our sustainability goals, we have commissioned a 1.5 -megawatt solar plant at our Lumel Alucast plant. So again, it shows in the last 2 years, the ener gy costs have gone up substantially in Europe and especially in Poland. And therefore, we have taken this initiative to put a 1.5-megawatt solar plant

items.statement: European auto OEMs cutting product lines, order volumes may persist for months; US tariff policy shifts adding supply chain volatility
items.quote: Several OEMs have instigated product line cuts leading to a reduction in order volumes, a trend that may persist for next few months. Adding to this uncertainty evolving on global trade environment, the recent policy shifts and potential tariff measures under the new U.S. administration. All these have introduced additional volatility and caution across global supply chain.

items.statement: Revenue growth target of more than 35% for FY26 with EBITDA margin at 7.5% plus and PAT maintained
items.quote: So, in terms of top line at EPACK, we are definitely looking to grow overall by more than 35%.

items.statement: Medium-term EBITDA margin target of around 8% plus/minus over next 2-3 years
items.quote: Overall, if you look at medium term for next 2 to 3 years, we are looking at an EBITDA margin of around 8% plus/minus.

items.statement: Capex guidance of INR 450-500 crores over next 12-18 months across parent, subsidiary and JVs
items.quote: We plan to invest approximately INR 450 crores to INR 500 crores over t he next 12 to 18 months to expand manufacturing capabilities and support our wholly owned subsidiary to cater to increasing market demand for FY '27 and onwards

items.statement: Capex funding: INR 230 crores from IPO proceeds, INR 100 crores new term loan, INR 100-150 crores internal accruals
items.value: INR 230 crores IPO + INR 100 crores debt + INR 100-150 crores internal

items.statement: Net debt INR 355 crores at FY25 end with 0.37x net debt to equity; average borrowing cost 7.9-8%
items.quote: We closed the financial year 2025 with a net debt of INR 355 crores representing a net debt to equity ratio of 0.37x.

items.statement: Term loan of INR 70-80 crores planned for FY26 capex
items.quote: And there might be some term loan, which is around INR70 crores to INR80 crores and balance amount will b e utilized through the internal accrual

items.statement: Hisense subsidiary production to start end of FY26 (Dec-Jan) for domestic and MEA export
items.quote: The production is scheduled to start from end of this year. So, December, January is when we are contemplating to start production.

items.statement: Washing machine capacity 30,000/month currently, ramping up from Q2 FY26 with full range by FY27
items.quote: So, the capacities we have currently created is close to 30,000 per month, and we are looking to further increase our portfolio for washing machines.

items.statement: Bhiwadi greenfield construction to complete by end Q1 FY26, new plant for cooling products diversification

items.statement: 55 established customers, targeting 70 by FY26 end; 2-3 new marquee RAC customers in advanced approval stage

items.statement: Strong business bookings and healthy pipeline in SDA and components; order book healthy despite Q1 slowdown

items.statement: Sri City plant utilization ramping up; optimal utilization expected in 2-3 quarters to improve margins
items.quote: So next 2 to 3 quarters, we believe that we'll be able to reach an optimal level of utilization in Sri City.

items.statement: Evaluating ECMS (component PLI) scheme participation; 2 months left to apply
items.quote: Yes. So currently, the company is evaluating the overall ECMS scheme. And since we have another 2 months to apply for it, we are evaluating for the possible components wherein EPACK can participate.

items.statement: Inventory days increased 12 days YoY (45 to 57) due to payable days reduction from QCO-driven domestic buying and supply chain disruptions; improvement expected in FY26

items.statement: Epavo JV BLDC motor capex INR 85-90 crores, INR 75 crores already committed/installed as CWIP
items.quote: So, the overall capex is close to INR85 crores to INR90 crores, which has been done in Epavo.
