items.statement: Two significant orders (one export, one domestic) in final stages, could finalize in next 1-2 months
items.quote: Actually, two of the opportunities are, you know, very much on the finalizing stage and it could get finalized in the next one or two months itself and both are comparatively quite significant value. That way, one is for export, and one is for domestic opportunity. Both our firm bids are already in place and any time in the next one month the customer could take a decision on.

items.statement: Employee expenses as percentage of revenue improved from 23.6% in FY21 to 9.2% in FY25
items.quote: Importantly, we have driven meaningful cost efficiencies with employee expenses as a percentage of revenue improving from 23.6% in FY21 to just 9.2% in FY25, illustrating disciplined cost management.

items.statement: ROCE 16.6% and ROE 8.6% in FY25, reflecting margin pressure despite scale growth
items.quote: Return on capital employed was 16.6% while the return on equity stood at 8.6%.

items.statement: Management targets 25% CAGR over the next three years.
items.quote: With the opportunities in the existing MICE setup and with the new developments in place, we are hopeful to clock a growth of 25% CAGR over next three years.

items.statement: Management expects to recover FY24 profitability ratios in FY26.
items.quote: But this year, we are hopeful that we will be able to achieve 2024 profitability ratios.

items.statement: Events organized increased 73% from 90 in FY24 to 156 in FY25.
items.quote: We are delighted to report a significant 73% increase in the number of events we organized this year from 90 events in FY '24 to 156 events FY '25.

items.statement: Acquired 21 new clients in FY25, including large cement and industry companies.
items.quote: We are proud to announce that we have acquired 21 new clients this year which is a significant milestone in itself.

items.statement: EBITDA margin declined to 9.31% in FY25 from 15.45% in FY24 due to aggressive pricing to win new clients and BFSI sector weakness.
items.quote: Our EBITDA stood at INR21.95 crores, with an EBITDA margin of 9.31% compared to last year of 15.45%.

items.statement: Margin compression in FY25 was driven by aggressive quoting in Q4 to acquire new clients and BFSI sector headwinds in Q3.
items.quote: Now, in acquiring the new clients, we have to be very aggressive while we are quoting the business. We are competing with the biggest and the best. And last quarter is everybody gets aggressive. Everybody has targets to achieve. Hence, we became a little more aggressive because we had to get into those corporates.

items.statement: Acquired pharma conference company has an order book of INR20 crores with visibility into 2026-2028.
items.quote: The company already has an order book of INR20 crores and the pharma business is a business which is kind of, closed, years before the event. While the company which we have acquired has 2026's business in hand, which is for the month of February, January and February ; they are pitching for various businesses as far as 2027 and 28 are also concerned.

items.statement: Approved acquisition of majority equity stake in Travexel Events and Travel Private Limited (medical conferences), turnover INR1.25 crores in FY25; deal to close in ~30 days.
items.quote: Recently we have approved the acquisition of a major equity stake in Travexel Events and Travel Private Limited. It is a young but promising company in the medical conference and travel segment. It has recorded a turnover of INR1.25 crores in FY '25.

items.statement: Board approved a loan facility of up to INR50 crores to the acquired subsidiary; management says it will be amended to tranche-based working capital as needed.
items.quote: The provision in the board meeting was just done to take one time approval. But I see that this is cause of concern and we've addressed this and I can assure you as soon as possible, we will amend it and the loan would be given to the company as a basis whenever it is needed.

items.statement: Appointed key distributor for Cordelia Cruises to offer luxury cruise itineraries and corporate incentive tours.
items.quote: I am also delighted to share a major milestone in our expansion strategy, our appointment as a key distributor for Cordelia Cruises, India's premier luxury cruise line.

items.statement: Launching corporate travel desk (B2B OTA) powered by TBO technology; also building B2C OTA platform with IATA/GDS integration for flights, hotels, cruises, visas.
items.quote: Looking ahead, we are excited to announce the launch of a new strategic initiative under our Digital Transformation Roadmap, a corporate travel desk , the comprehensive digital implant tailored for corporate clients. This platform will streamline and fulfill all day -to-day travel requirements for our enterprise customers, including flights, hotels, taxis, visas and more, and all this through a si

items.statement: B2C expansion will use existing technology partnerships (TBO) and modest team (10-12 people); no major capex or marketing burn planned.
items.quote: We are now creating a vertical, perhaps getting into a little bigger office, having a corner dedicated to 10 people, 12 people who would be into this business. Now, in terms of technology, we have thought about getting associated with established names since we are already dealing with them. So, we are not looking at any expensive proposition.

items.statement: Of INR47 crores receivables, INR25-27 crores already collected; balance expected soon from blue-chip clients.
items.quote: No, the good news is that out of the INR47 crores, INR25 crores to 27 crores we 've already received as we speak and the balance we would be getting soon.

items.statement: IPO proceeds eliminated interest cost; company is debt-free on a net basis.
items.quote: Now, with the money coming in from the IPO, we do not have an interest cost. We are saving a lot of money towards the cost of money.

items.statement: Board recommended dividend of INR1 per equity share (10% of face value INR10) for FY25.
items.quote: In line with our commitment to shareholder returns, the Board of Directors has recommended a dividend of INR1 rupee per equity share, representing a 10% payout on the face value of INR10 rupee per share for the year ended March 31st, 2025.

items.statement: Hired senior talent including former EaseMyTrip Head of Strategy & Acquisitions Varun Mehta to drive M&A.
items.quote: I can state to you that we have Mr. Varun Mehta and his team who were Head- Strategy and Acquisition in EaseMyTrip, who joined us about a month back and we would now slowly penetrate deeper into the acquisition field.

items.statement: B2C travel portal brand name under trademark dispute in court; product development continues in parallel.
items.quote: the dispute which is there regarding the trademark of our B2C portal is right now currently in the court. Mach Conferences & I will not like to comment upon it. We are pushing for the same name. Nevertheless, we are not wasting time. We are parallelly creating our product, the tool, which would help us to get into this business

items.statement: Related party transactions for promoter family wedding (one-off); historical RPTs for funding have stopped post-IPO.
items.quote: That related party transaction which you are referring to is a small little business. I can happily state in this forum, my son is getting married this year. So, this is his wedding expense which we have taken approval and we took the permission from the bo ard. And we have ensured that nothing is done which is unlawful. And this is one -off

items.statement: Revenue seasonality: 30-40% in H1, 60-70% in H2; pattern expected to continue.
items.quote: That should remain this way. That should remain this way this year also.

items.statement: B2C strategy targets local travel agents and FIT sellers, not large OTAs; leverages captive base of ~1 lakh travelers.
items.quote: We do not aspire to become, in current scenario, we do not want to, compete with the biggest and the best which would be there in your cell phone currently. That is not the audience, because we understand that we cannot compete with them. We want to compete with people like there are local travel companies, there are FIT selling companies and plus we have captive audience.

items.statement: Religious tourism pilot (Mahakumbh, Do Dham, Char Dham) saw strong demand; premium packages sold out, pricing surged from INR15k to INR1 lakh.
items.quote: We had got phenomenal response from the market. Our captive audience was initially not too excited. But at a later stage, we were under a lot of pressure from them for the inventory. We were unable to get the inventory or the sector was unorganized because, of the reasons told to you, somebody was selling a camp for 15,000. They took it upto one lakh because the demand had risen.

items.statement: Kumbh pilot revenue ~INR20 lakhs with 18-19% margin; limited by unorganized supply chain.
items.quote: Now, the Kumbh event, the revenue was not too much, I think about 20 lakhs or something with the profitability of surprisingly 18% to 19%.

items.statement: B2C verticals (corporate travel desk, religious, cruises) not expected to contribute significant revenue in FY26; ramp-up over 6-8 months.
items.quote: Overall, we understand that there will not be much significant business coming from the B2C verticals because everybody would need some time to penetrate and get the business onto the table. So, we are not too excited about that business in current year. In the following year, yes, it would take six to eight months for that business to establish.

items.statement: Cruise tourism growth supported by government Cruise Bharat Mission, Mumbai International Cruise Terminal (INR556 crore), simplified e-visa, reduced port charges.

items.statement: BFSI sector weakness in Q3 FY25 impacted revenue; entire sector affected, not a single client.
items.quote: No, no, no. Because you mean not the first quarter, you mean the third quarter. Yes, the entire BFSI sector, it had gone down. There are numbers which you could relate to. I do not have the numbers handy, but we have seen that. And that is the reason. But it happened with the entire BFSI sector.

items.statement: Management considering quarterly updates/investor communications; will seek advice and act on feedback.
items.quote: We had thought about it. We are still contemplating. We would seek advice and, you know, this is the foundation of the company in terms of the IPO listing. We are in the 9th month, 10th month. So, we are accepting a lot of suggestions. So, we are currently working on this.

items.statement: FY26 revenue growth guidance of 35-40% with EBITDA margins of 22-24%
items.quote: Looking ahead, we aim to sustain our growth trajectory with an expected annual growth rate of 35% to 40%, while maintaining healthy EBITDA margins in the range of 22% to 24%.

items.quote: As of 31st March 2025, our order book remains strong and healthy, standing at around INR 1,185 crores, comprising 22 diverse projects across multiple states. Our operation and maintenance order book adds another INR 806 crores.

items.statement: New orders worth INR 200 crores secured in FY26 so far
items.quote: Further, in financial year 2026, we have secured additional new orders worth INR 200 crores, indicating a strong start to the year and continued confidence from our clients.

items.quote: Even if we go by a conservative number of somewhere around 20% to 25%, even at that level, we can expect that an order inflow of INR 1,000 to INR 1,250 crores that should accrue to the Company from the bids that we have already submitted.

items.statement: FY25 EBITDA margin 25%, PAT margin 16%; guided FY26 EBITDA margin 22-24%
items.quote: The EBITDA margin for Q4 FY25 was 25%. While the PAT grew by 30% to INR 74 crores with the margin at 18%. items.quote: Notably, we aim to increase the scale of our projects from 50 to 200 MLD for sewage treatment plants and from 20 to 50 MLD for common effluent treatment plants.

items.quote: In terms of cash flow, I am happy to share that we have achieved a significant turnaround. items.quote: It can be both ways. It can be either IPP projects or PPA projects means or EPC. We always intend to go asset light. We will always have a right mix of EPC and PPA projects. So, we will be quite careful while choosing any of the assets which we can build up in tha

items.quote: Presently, in three of our existing wastewater treatment projects, which are predominantly sewage treatment plants, we are putting up this gas generation and CBG plants. items.statement: O&M revenue expected to grow from ~INR 30 crores to INR 70-75 crores in 2 years; FY26 increase of INR 10-15 crores
items.quote: If I talk 2 years down the line, we foresee that O&M revenue can shoot up to an extent of somewhere around INR 70 crores to INR 75 crores.

items.statement: Average project execution cycle 18-24 months (28 months for water supply schemes)
items.quote: The time period in general is in the range of 18 months to 24 months, apart from some water supply schemes, which we are having wherein the order, this timeline is around 28 months. So, in general, a timeline of around 24 months can be taken to be an average timeline for the execution of the projects.

items.statement: Maintaining 75:25 EPC to HAM mix for better margins; HAM drives higher margins but limited exposure
items.quote: HAM project drives better margins in comparison to EPC projects, but we cannot be, go very heavy on HAM. So, we will always be having a right mix between EPC and HAM. So, we understand that a mix of around 75 to 25 for EPC to HAM, I think that will be the right mix and right ratio going forward as well. So, we will try to maintain that level.

items.statement: Evaluating international markets (Middle East, Southeast Asia); will study before entering; may use local contractors for civil work
items.quote: regarding this question on the international, same ways we are having some inquiries now from the international market as well. So, it would be that student exercise that we study that market carefully and then we enter. We will ta ke our own time with the study, but one thing that is for sure is we will definitely be inclined to enter into the international market even when the opportunity is ava

items.statement: Unbilled revenue INR 265 crores (91 days) included in FY25 revenue of INR 1,066 crores
items.quote: Unbilled revenue is the sales valuation in INR 1,066 crores. So, in the current financial year, it will not be the part of the revenue. It has already been the part of revenue of FY25. The figure is INR 265 crores, not 256. It is 265. And if we see it in number of days, it comes out to 91 days. So, in 90 days, this unbilled revenue cycle seems to be okay.

items.statement: No JJM bids in current INR 5,000 crores pipeline; focusing on WWTP EPC/HAM projects
items.quote: Right now under JJM the projects which we were having and which we were executing, we are in the final stages of the execution of those projects. Since we were not having our comfort zone going further for the JJM projects, so we backed out and we didn't bid any of our bids which have been submitted out of this INR 5,000 odd crores. So, none of the project is from JJM.

items.statement: In-house design and execution control drives cost competitiveness and 35-40% historical bid success ratio
items.quote: Rahul, that gets transpired from the design and execution capabilities, which are in-house. So, we have control on the costings. So, that control on the costings as well as giving the economical and viable solutions. So, we always remain a bit competitive in comparison to our competitors and that translates into better success ratio in comparison to our peers.

items.statement: Expect renewable revenue in FY26 but small; meaningful visibility from FY27-28
items.quote: We do expect to generate revenues from this company in FY26 as well, but comparatively we expect it to be a bit smaller right now.

items.statement: JJM payment delay was one-time issue; worst over; funds expected by June 2025; no issues in AMRUT/Namami Gange
items.quote: This problem, this is one of the one problem which anybody has faced in the last 10 years and to our understanding the worst is over and the funds are there on the verge of being released in JJM. Apart from JJM, I have not faced any of the challenges in either AMRUT 2 projects or Namami Ganga projects. The flow of funds there have been quite smooth, which definitely have helped us in our execution

items.statement: Expects next couple of quarters softer, momentum to pick up in H2 FY26.
items.quote: Given the current landscape, we are expecting business in the next couple of quarters to be on the softer side, with momentum likely to pick up pace in the second half of FY '26.

items.statement: New facility at Adinarayanahosahalli to be commissioned by end of Q2 FY26, revenue from H2 FY26.
items.quote: Speaking on our ongoing capex, we have a new facility coming up at Adinarayanahosahalli, very close to our SLCM plant, which we expect to commission towards the end of the second quarter of FY '26. Revenue from the same will start coming in from H2 FY '26.

items.statement: Plans to offset CEV-5 material cost increase through price adjustments and operational efficiencies.
items.quote: The transition to CEV-5 standards has led to an increase in the material cost. We plan to offset the same through price adjustments and continued focus on operational efficiencies.

items.statement: Expects gross margin impact in FY26, not able to pass entire cost increase, relying on operational efficiencies.
items.quote: As far as FY '26 is concerned, I think we have been consistent that we would [inaudible] move completely at one go. There will be an impact on the gross margin. At the same time, we are relying on the operational efficiencies to be more in the range.

items.statement: Pricing increase from all market participants expected to trickle in from Q2.
items.quote: So it will happen most probably from Q2 onwards that the pricing increase from all the market participants should trickle in.

items.statement: Sees sluggishness in infrastructure project execution, reflected in cement volume growth.
items.quote: We have been seeing some sluggishness in the pace of on-ground execution of infrastructure projects. This trend is also reflected in the recent volume growth of cement players, which has hovered around the mid-single-digit range.

items.statement: One-third of Q4 FY25 sales came from CEV-5 machines.
items.quote: A key highlight that I would like to point out here is that despite a lot of attention on the CEV-4 machines, close to one-third of our sales during Q4 FY '25 came from CEV-5 machines.

items.statement: Working capital days at 30 in March 25 vs 24 in March 24, no secular increase expected.
items.quote: If you look at the working capital number of days as at March 25, we are again 30 versus the March 24, 2024. So that gives you a good indication that from an inventory buildup and the inventory liquidation, how it has panned out for AJAX, both for the CEV-4 inventory.

items.statement: No forward-looking guidance for FY26 revenue growth.
items.quote: So we don't make forward-looking statements at this point in time. We can only say that the business outlook and growth as has been stated in my earlier conversation when I was speaking about the way we see the business going forward.

items.statement: One-off expenses of about Rs. 60 million in FY25, not expected to recur at 30% growth.
items.quote: Yes, that's what I said, that it would be about Rs. 60 million.

items.statement: Exports grew from Rs. 36 crores in FY22 to Rs. 74 crores in FY25, no specific FY26 guidance.
items.quote: We were about 36 odd crores in FY '22 and reached about Rs. 74-75 crores in FY '25. That itself suggests that there is a very clear path.

items.statement: New facility will initially produce pumps, may also produce transit mixers.
items.quote: In the new facility, I think pumps will, of course, be a product which will have an immediate, let's say, traction there. And as Shubho mentioned that, in the pumps from '22 to '25, depending on the type of pumps, we have moved from 18% to 57% growth. So that's clearly an area which will come up in Hosahalli to start off with.

items.statement: No secular increase in receivables expected, most March receivables already liquidated.
items.quote: I can also say that for all the receivables which were accrued, let's say at March, most of it is already liquidated. So we do not envisage any secular increase in receivables.

items.statement: Employee cost increased to 5.3% of revenue in FY25 from 5% in FY24 due to hiring.
items.quote: So the 20 basis points, you would appreciate that the employee cost as a percentage of revenue in FY '24 is 5%, and employee cost as a percentage of revenue for FY '25 is about 5.3, the 30 basis points increase.

items.statement: No specific FY26 margin guidance, but expects gross margin impact and operational efficiencies.
items.quote: I will not speculate that whether you can break up about 100 or 150 basis points decline on EBITDA and all. That you can run through the models based on our commentary and come to your own view.

items.quote: FY '26 in Q1, we've continued with this strong performance of global iconic brands being launched on Nykaa. Some of them are mentioned here such as Chanel, which is one of the most iconic luxury beauty brands in the world, Armani Beauty as well, Aestura, Supergoop, Nexus and Lovetc etc.

items.statement: Beauty GMV grew 31% YoY in Q4 FY25 to INR3,058 crores, full year 30% to INR11,775 crores
items.quote: For Q4, the growth was at 31% year-over-year at INR3,058 crores of GMV. On an annual -- on a full year basis, it's INR11,775 crores at a 30% growth year-over-year.

items.statement: Fashion GMV grew 18% YoY in Q4 FY25 to INR1,000+ crores, full year 12% to INR3,804 crores

items.quote: In the Beauty business, the improvement stands at 90 basis points, and this is also aided by strong performance of our own brands. In Fashion, higher service and marketing income contributed to gross margin expansion of 419 basis points.

items.statement: eB2B contribution margin improved ~500 bps YoY in FY25 driven by gross margin +200 bps, lower fulfillment and selling costs
items.quote: And no wonder, you will see across all the different metrics of operating margin, we are actually improving quite significantly. We improved gross margin by almost 200 bps on the back of mix and higher ad income.

items.quote: There's a significant improvement in working capital with reduc tion in both inventory days, receivable days as well as improvement in payable days. So this is reflected in the form of working capital days coming down to 34 from 42 a year back

items.quote: So the operating cash flow now stands at INR467 crores. And what I would like to also point out is after lease payments as well as capex, there is still a significant amount of surplus cash.

items.quote: We would like to update all of you that in May 2025, we received NCLT approval for both the schemes, which is a merger of LBB into Fashion. LBB was already 100% subsidiary of the Fashion business. The other one is a demerger of our Superstore business into Nykaa E

items.statement: Own brands 40% sold through non-Nykaa channels (GT, DTC, Amazon); Dot & Key INR530 crores top line (14x in 4 years), Nykaa Cosmetics INR350 crores, Kay Beauty INR240 crores
items.quote: On the right-hand side, you can see how this GMV is split across our own channels. So the pinks are the Nykaa online and the Nykaa stores. But also there is about 40% of this business, which comes from other channels.

items.statement: Content-to-commerce flywheel: 28,000+ affiliates, 500k+ content pieces/year; Nykaa Play 4M+ live views, 15k shoppable videos; 17M social followers
items.quote: Today, there's over 28,000 affiliates and influencers who are registered and are creating content on behalf of the platform. They are creating over 500,000 pieces of content in the year alone.

items.statement: Fashion fulfillment expenses improved 136 bps YoY via lower leakages; marketing up 350 bps, SG&A down 40 bps, contribution margin +160 bps
items.quote: We have improved fulfillment expenses by 136 bps in large measure because of lower leakages. Leakages are a structural problem in the online fashion industry, but the team has taken multiple initiatives to reduce leakages in the fashion business.

items.statement: Beauty growing ~30% vs industry mid 20-25% CAGR; Fashion Q4 18% vs industry ~10-11%
items.quote: We believe this is significantly ahead of the rest of the industry, the rest of the India online BPC ecosystem, which we believe is growing roughly mid 23% to 25% CAGR over the past several years.

items.statement: Fashion industry still muted; leakages structural problem in online fashion; marketing investments continued ahead of curve
items.quote: The fashion growth revival is against a muted performance still in the industry; however, it is reflected through both growth in fashion.com vertical as well as the LBB, which is part of now the fashion vertical, and that momentum is likely to continue.

items.statement: Nuvama Wealth MPIS net new money INR6,500 crore for FY25, Q4 INR1,350-1,400 crore
items.quote: And if you see the flows, they're quite heartening. I think even this year, we were able to achieve about INR6,500 crores of net new money. And within that, quarter 4 saw about INR1,400 crores in a tough environment, which was nice.

items.statement: FY26 net new money target INR23,000-24,000 crore across Wealth, Private, Asset Management
items.quote: So, if I add all this together, we come back to some INR23,000 - 24,000 crores at the bare minimum is what we target.

items.statement: FY26 cost-to-income ratio target 100 bps improvement for Nuvama Wealth full year
items.quote: For FY '26, I think we are actually looking at 100 basis points down.

items.statement: FY26 opex growth expected around 10% year-on-year
items.quote: I think we will be in the similar ZIP code in terms of opex growth year-on-year. So close to 10% seems reasonable, and that's our expectation.

items.statement: Nuvama Wealth C/I 67% Q4 FY25, Private C/I 66% Q4 FY25, consolidated C/I 56% Q4 FY25
items.quote: With that, our overall C/I is at 56% compared to 60% of Q4 last year, which is an improvement of 4%.

items.statement: Added 350 RMs over last 18 months, plan 10-15% RM count growth
items.quote: the fixed cost has gone up because we have added around 350 odd RMs over the last 18 months.

items.statement: MPIS flows 70% managed products, Private ARR revenue 60% of total, Asset Management 92% fee-paying AUM
items.quote: And now almost 70% of these flows actually comprise of managed products, which in a sense is building some annuity for the future.

items.statement: Clearing business yield ~2% currently, new normal 1.8-1.9% assuming FD yield decline
items.quote: So actually, clearing business, I think the new normal should be closer to maybe 1.8-1.9%. I am assuming some decline in the FD yields coming in maybe Q3-Q4. And already, we are sitting at 2%.

items.statement: ROE improved from 23.6% to 31.5% FY25, Q4 ROE ~31%
items.quote: and the ROE substantially improved from about 23.6% to 31.5%.

items.statement: Q4 market tough but Feb onwards trend change, liquidity injection, rate cuts, primary supply dried up, FPI buying returned
items.quote: So therefore, Feb onwards, you see that there was a change in trend. And hopefully, we'll see that momentum continue and go on thro ugh the first half of this year

items.statement: Private families 4,250, added 575 in FY25, RM count 135; Wealth RMs 1,200+, ~500 under 1 year tenure
items.quote: In terms of number of families, we are at 4,250. We added around 575 new families during the year, and RM count stands at 135.

items.statement: Wealth RM attrition 25-30% vs banks 45-50%, Private regret attrition 0% Q4, top bucket lost 3-4 RMs
items.quote: In our Nuvama Wealth, we categorize RMs in different buckets. So, at the top end, we call the big league, there the attrition would be order of magnitude. About 300-350 people come in our big league out of our 1,200, we would have lost 3-4 people there.

items.statement: H1 interim dividend INR63/share, H2 dividend INR69/share approved, payout ~48-49% of PAT last 2 years
items.quote: In the yesterday Board meeting, the Board has approved INR69 dividend for the balance year. With this, we are within the range of our dividend distribution guidance. And on an average, 48%-49% of the last 2 financial years, we have paid it as dividend to the shareholders.

items.statement: Open to inorganic if strategic fit or asset class expertise, valuations high; global collaboration via external asset manager model possible
items.quote: In terms of inorganic, one always keeps looking for an opportunity, but it has to be some real addition, right? It can't just be going and buying some other wealth management firm because right now, the valuations are through the roof.

items.statement: F&O regulation uncertainty removed, peak margin monitoring changed, limits increased to INR1,500-10,000 crore, delta-adjusted open interest basis
items.quote: Now with the new rules which is now as a discussion paper and maybe will get finalized where the limits have been increased to INR1,500 - 10,000 crores, and limit will be monitored on a delta-adjusted open interest basis.

items.statement: PAG exit rumors only in news articles, no development to report to exchange
items.quote: I have also read the same news article, Sanketh. If there is anything which has to be reported, we will report to the exchange. There is no such development which has happened.

items.statement: Market hiring madness, compensation race to death, many will get decimated when cycle turns
items.quote: I mean, I think in a sense, there's some sort of madness happening in the market right now, the way people are building out teams and the way compensation has been dea lt, I don't know, it looks like a race to

items.statement: Asset Management FY26 net flow targets: CRE INR2,000-2,300 crore, public market INR3,000-4,000 crore, private market INR800-1,000 crore
items.quote: If I see FY26, at least INR2,000 crores -INR2,300 crores will come in commercial real estate. INR3,000 crores to INR4,000 crores bare minimum we'll target in the public market and say about INR800 crores to INR1,000 crores in the private market.

items.statement: Private ARR net new money FY26 target INR10,000-11,000 crore (25-30% on INR44,000 crore base)
items.quote: If we are able to do anywhere between 25-30% on that, so you are again looking at INR10,000 crores to INR11,000 crores coming from there is what we will target.

items.statement: Wealth MPIS net new money FY26 target INR7,000-8,000 crore (25-30% on INR30,000 crore base)
items.quote: Similarly, on the Wealth side, now our MPIS book would be around maybe INR30,000 crores, again, a 25-30%, so maybe INR7,000 - 8,000 crores there.

items.statement: Tech modernization of key systems, APIs, applications completed in Q4, GenAI integration into MARS platform next
items.quote: we were in the process of modernizing few of our key systems, APIs, applications on the tech side, this was more of an upgrade. Most of it has already been done, and that's why the cost is sitting in Q4.

items.statement: Management targets 14% operating margin, up from ~13% currently, driven by tubular plant startup, lead recycling, and throughput gains.
items.quote: while 13% kind of a margin is what we have seen earlier, our internal target is definitely to reach our originally stated position of 14% margin.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 margins negatively impacted by ~1.5-2% due to higher antimony alloy costs, power cost adjustments, solar settlement delays, higher trading revenue, and additional warranty/employee provisions.
items.quote: together between the material cost as well as the power cost and also considering the fact that the trading revenue is also higher during the current quarter, the overall margins got ne gatively impacted by roughly around 1.5% to 2

items.statement: A 2% price increase was implemented in April 2025 to mitigate cost pressures; further hikes depend on competitive dynamics and cost trajectory.
items.quote: We have taken a price increase in the month of April to mitigate some of these cost numbers.

items.statement: Antimony alloy prices have risen due to Chinese export restrictions; no supply constraint but higher costs persist into Q1 FY26.
items.quote: No, there is no supply constraint per se, but definitely, the prices have gone up. We are able to source the material that is required for our production, but the prices have definitely have gone

items.statement: Power costs increased due to fuel purchase cost adjustments and regulatory delays in settling solar power generation; costs may persist for a couple of quarters.
items.quote: there is also a delay in settlement of power by the government for the power that we have generated in our ground-mounted solar plant because of certain regulatory changes.

items.statement: FY25 consolidated capex ~INR1,200 cr: ~INR400 cr tubular reinstatement, ~INR500 cr other lead acid, INR200-300 cr New Energy (qualification plant, R&D lab, gigafactory land).
items.quote: As far as the capex spend on a consolidated basis this year is close to about INR1200 crores of that significant portion has gone into lead acid business, including the tubular battery reinstatement.

items.statement: FY26 capex similar to FY25 (~INR1,200 cr), bulk towards New Energy (~INR1,000 cr) for three projects under construction; cash flow timing may vary 15-20%.
items.quote: For FY '26, we may have to spend a capex of a similar amount as what we have spent during the current year. But this year, the bulk of capex will go towards the New Energy Business in terms of completing the balance three projects that are currently under construction.

items.statement: Lead recycling plant started commercial operations in Q4 FY25 with 50,000 MT/yr capacity, scaling to 100,000 MT/yr; refining operational, battery breaking in Q2/Q3 FY26.
items.quote: Our recycling unit has come online in Q4. We have a starting capacity of about 50,000 metric tons per annum, scaling to 100,000.

items.statement: Tubular battery plant reinstatement underway, commercial production starting June 2025, reducing trading mix and improving margins.
items.quote: The tubular battery plant reinstatement is underway with commercial production starting in June, allowing us to put our own manufactured products into the market with less reliance on trading.

items.statement: Throughput enhancement added ~6 million battery capacity without significant capex via Industry 4.0 initiatives.
items.quote: we are almost able to add 6 million battery capacity over and above our existing capacities without adding much of a capex.

items.statement: New Energy: two pack facilities (Tirupati, Hyderabad) with eventual 7 GWh cumulative capacity for telecom, UPS, light EV; R&D facility and customer qualification plant on track for end of CY2025.
items.quote: we currently operate two pack facilities that will have a cumulative eventual capacity of 7 gigawatt hours combined.

items.statement: First gigafactory broke ground, capacity coming online H1 2027 (~20 GWh ultimate); further capacity tied to firm offtake agreements.
items.quote: We broke ground earlier this year on our first gigafactory that should see capacity coming online around in the first half of 2027.

items.statement: Q4 FY25: 4W domestic aftermarket +9% YoY, OEM +15% YoY; 2W volumes +13% YoY; home inverter +17% YoY; exports -10% YoY (Western & APAC slowdown); telecom -15% YoY.
items.quote: The 4 - wheeler domestic aftermarket volumes grew by about 9% on a year -on-year basis during the current quarter, and the OEM volumes have shown a strong growth of about 15% d uring the current quarter

items.statement: FY26 outlook: 4W OEM volumes flattish in Q1, uptick expected in Q2; 2W OEM volumes down in Q1, recovery expected in Q2; export aftermarket facing tariff-related uncertainty.
items.quote: we see that the 4-wheeler growth is kind of flattish. Because - our market share in the 4-wheeler is about 35%, 36% on the OEM segment. We are seeing the volume projections to be a bit flattish, but we expect that during Q2, there could be some uptick in the volumes.

items.statement: New Energy: two sizable DC fast charger orders from private charge point operators under execution; grid-scale BESS orders won, first external deployments this year.
items.quote: recently, we have a two sizable orders from private charge point operators that is under execution right now.

items.statement: Trading revenue ~15% of Q4 revenue; will decline as tubular plant ramps, but some vendor sourcing will continue due to capacity gap.
items.quote: About 15% of the revenue is from trading.

items.statement: Lubricants business contributed INR40 cr revenue in Q4 FY25, adding significantly to bottom line.
items.quote: for the first time, the lube business has also seen a INR40 crores revenue for this current quarter.

items.statement: Lead acid market projected to grow from $4.6B to $5.8B over 5 years (~5% CAGR); management considers estimate conservative due to storage migration to other chemistries.
items.quote: considering the higher base, that is on the overall lead acid market. So you know that we are already seeing migration of some of the storage segment batteries to other chemistries, right?

items.statement: Target inventory days (DOH) 55-57 days; Q4 seasonally higher due to summer inverter stock build.
items.quote: Our idea is that our DOH levels cannot go beyond 56 or 57 days. There could be some seasonal impact of it because of the tubular factory, generally, we create higher inventories towards the end of the year to meet the upcoming season in the summer.

items.statement: New Energy first phase requires INR2,000-2,500 cr, funded by lead acid cash flows and some holding company leverage; further expansion funding to be decided after gigafactory stabilization.
items.quote: we believe the first phase would require in the New Energy Business close to INR2,000 crores to INR2,500 crores, which we believe we can easily meet with our existing lead acid business cash flow generation, maybe some bit of leverage that we have to take on the balance sheet of the holding company.

items.statement: Chinese LFP cell prices observed at $50-55/kWh (sub-$50 in one-off cases), NMC ~$60/kWh; prices on downward trajectory last 2-3 quarters; Indian cell manufacturing faces 15-20% cost penalty initially.
items.quote: I think LFP, we have seen the best price in some cases was seen around $50 per kilowatt hour, but it is still around that $55. But we have also seen based on the import data, one-off case where there was even sub-$50 level as well.

items.statement: Export markets in flux due to potential tariff differentials; US customers in wait-and-watch mode; competitive intensity may shift if India gets lower duties vs Southeast Asia.
items.quote: we are seeing some changes in the order flow from some of our U.S. customers. But the larger impact possibly could be if countries have differential duties, I mean, if for example, if India were to have a lower duty structure as against, let's say, some country in Southeast Asia, then obviously, their capacities in order to fill, they may start looking at elsewhere market.

items.statement: Power cost headwinds from solar settlement delay and fuel adjustments may persist for at least a couple of quarters; regulatory relief uncertain until commission decision next year.
items.quote: those costs are going to persist even in the next year.

items.statement: New Energy capex payback uncertain until 8-10 GWh capacity achieved; EBITDA of $4-5/kWh possible only if conversion margin reaches $20-25/kWh.
items.quote: It may still need about 8 to 10 gigawatt hour of capacity for us to achieve those kind of numbers.

items.statement: New Energy revenue flat in FY25 due to lower OEM demand and delayed ESS pickup; 35% revenue growth in Q4 FY25 driven by ESS and EV battery packs; 3W EV volumes muted.
items.quote: When we look at the entire revenue growth of this business, including the chargers as well as battery packs to both EV and ESS segments, 35% kind of a revenue growth is what we have seen in this current quarter.

items.statement: Management targets covering about 300 ZBM stores by December end, representing 45-50% of retail turnover
items.quote: my sense is that we should be covering about, ideally, my best guess is about 300-odd stores by [December] end. And that should cover us -- my sense is about 50% or 45% of our turnover on retail.

items.statement: Store additions expected to be slightly higher next year with 80-20 franchise to COCO ratio maintained
items.quote: It should be a little higher going forward, Videesha, right now as we look at it, right? Obviously, as I mentioned, we would want to continue. And we've largely retained, which is about an 80-20 ratio between franchise and COCO.

items.statement: Second consecutive quarter of broad-based volume growth in mid-single digits despite muted demand environment
items.quote: the second quarter that we've seen reasonably broad-based volume growth in the mid-single digits would be the best.

items.statement: Gross margin contracted 230 bps YoY due to channel mix shift and conscious value proposition pricing while resetting cost structure
items.quote: But also, the fact that we have been consciously providing value proposition, while we are parallelly working towards resetting the cost structure for some of our lead products like the kind of example that I mentioned, Sameer, in my presentation.

items.statement: Reported EBITDA margin 25.5%, down 14 bps YoY; like-to-like EBITDA margin would be 23.5% excluding license brand accounting change
items.quote: EBITDA margin reported is at about 25.5%. The change versus last year is about 14 bps lower. Now in the EBITDA margin, there is a change in accounting for one of the licensed brands based on the Ind AS. Like-to-like EBITDA margin versus last year would have been about 23.5%.

items.statement: Floatz brand revenue run rate expected to reach INR200 crores this year if momentum continues, up from over INR100 crores last year
items.quote: At the run rate, in fact, it costs out by a handsome margin. I'm assuming $1 billion is INR100 crores, right? So, it plotted by a handsome margin last year. And this year, my sense is if this continues momentum, right, we should be in the range of about INR200 crores.

items.statement: Zero Base Merchandising expanded to 146 stores from less than 40 last quarter; lines per store down 40%, inventory down 25%, availability up 300 bps, retrieval time 45 seconds vs 1.5 minutes
items.quote: We are now to about 146 stores. So, it's obviously a very large expansion from less than 40 or so last quarter. The pace has obviously gone up as we have learned to do this much faster.

items.statement: Value proposition rolled out across network with core price point INR799 in ~800 stores; Power Move+ collection launched at attractive price points with China partners
items.quote: So, let's say, for example, the core price point of INR799, Videesha, right, would be a core in, let's say, for example, about 800 stores, what is the opening price point for the balance 600 stores.

items.statement: Hush Puppies and Power are second and third largest brands after Bata, each in strong double digits around 20% revenue contribution
items.quote: I would say that the second and the third largest brand after Bata, which is the largest by far, is Hush Puppies and Power. They would be in the strong double digits in the range of about 20%.

items.statement: Channel mix for FY25: COCO retail ~70%, franchise ~7.5%, e-commerce ~10%, industrial/distribution ~12-13%
items.quote: Retail would be about 70% COCO. You will have franchise at about 7.5%, e-commerce at about 10%. And you will have IND at about 12% to 13%.

items.statement: Total inventory down 16% YoY over 5 quarters; aged inventory down 30-35%; inventory turns improving with further reduction potential
items.quote: The inventory is a significant drop at 16%. This is over a continuing drop over the last almost now 5 quarters that we have managed to do. That has shown up in terms of turns also.

items.statement: Largest ever backend capex installed at Batanagar for PUDIP machine backing IMEVA commercialization; strategy focuses on automated, technology-intensive, IPR-driven manufacturing
items.quote: We installed our largest ever capex in the back end in Batanagar in the PUDIP machine. This backs our commercialization of the IMEVA machine that we did last year.

items.statement: 100% BIS compliant with seamless transition; BIS imports were <5% of market now eliminated; viewing BIS as export opportunity for local manufacturing
items.quote: We had a seamless changeover, and we had almost no hiccups, except for maybe a few niche licensed brands, which also have now been sorted now. So, in fact, we are looking at this as an opportunity from an export's perspective.

items.statement: NPS at all-time high of 85; franchise stores at 625; key retail outlets (MBO activation) expanded to ~1,400
items.quote: Overall, NPS stands at a high of 85. Efficiency parameters on the stores have gone up. We are also, in our distribution business, expanding our key retail outlets, which are our activation program for the MBOs to now almost about 1,400 outlets.

items.statement: Licensed brand accounting change creates non-comparable quarters until Q4 FY26; one-time employee cost increase of ~100 bps this quarter
items.quote: Yes, yes. It will be recurring. So, we will have 3 more quarters where there will be numbers may not be comparable with reference to the previous year. Once we reach quarter 4 of '26 financial year, then number starts becoming like-to-like.

items.statement: Long-term vision: volume-driven revenue growth trajectory with aggressive inventory agility, operating leverage, and profitable growth over 2-5 years
items.quote: The second theme that's there is that we want, over the next not only 2 years, but also 5 years, to make sure that we -- it's a volume-driven growth trajectory overall, right? There might be some quarters up and down, but we want to make sure it's a volume-driven revenue growth trajectory.

items.statement: Distillery capacity utilization expected at 90-95% in FY26
items.quote: We are currently running at about 90% plus capacity utilization. We expect that to continue, and our endeavor is to move the needle substantially up because the benefit is there in utilizing our assets efficiently, and we have an opportunity unlike the sugar business. So 90% to 95% is the kind of capacity utilization we are looking at.

items.statement: Distillery capacity is 582 KLPD, yielding ~18 crore liters annually
items.quote: Our distillery capacity is about 582 KLPD. So that will give you about 18 crores liters or so, okay?

items.statement: Consumer products business targeting growth above 12% industry rate
items.quote: Branded packaged food business in India is growing at about 12% annually. We will be trying to beat that estimate in terms of our growth rates, and we will continue to keep focused on building the brand and driving the distribution.

items.statement: Consumer products currently only in South India, will expand as demand picks up
items.quote: So right now, we are present in the South of India. And as the market demand picks up, we will be expanding across to other geographies. Right now, we are present in the South of India.

items.statement: No ethanol price hike in ~3 years despite 8% FRP increase last year
items.quote: The last time and Venkat, correct me if I'm wrong, we saw an increase on ethanol offtake prices in late 2022. So we're almost going to be 3 years without any increase in molasses-based ethanol prices, barring some marginal increases on the C-heavy price. It is not very material.

items.statement: US ethanol import curbs may be lifted in trade talks, industry has objected
items.quote: We are also concerned, I will say, by the fact that there are conversations as part of a broader U.S.-India trade discussions that the lifting of curbs on import of U.S. ethanol is being considered. We don't know the outcome yet, but I think the industry body has officially also expressed their concern on this matter to policymakers across the board.

items.statement: US ethanol landed price in early 40s per liter, below Indian subsidized price
items.quote: I think if you look at the U.S. -- current export prices of U.S. ethanol, I think it equates to about, I would say, the early 40s. I did check this earlier this week. So of course, ethanol is subsidized in India. And I think U.S. prices are currently much lower. So that obviously impacts the economics.

items.statement: Sugar MSP needs to reach early 40s per kg for viability vs current INR37-38
items.quote: I would say something into the early 40s would only be near meaningful. However, it still continues to be a deliberation with them on the MSP. So, we'll have to wait and watch if anything is considered at all.

items.statement: Ethanol volumes dynamically allocated between OMC commitment and ENA based on profitability
items.quote: As far as the composition of ethanol and ENA is concerned, we'll be dynamically deciding it, which is more lucrative, okay? As far as the ethanol is concerned, to the extent of the OMC commitment, we'll be honoring it. So, balance, we will be diverting into the ENA.

items.statement: India sugar production 25.7 MMT as of Apr 30, ISMA estimates 30.3 MMT full year
items.quote: ISMA, the Indian Sugar Mills and Bio-energy Association has maintained its full season estimate of 30.3 million metric tons, contingent on an additional 4.5 million to 5 million metric tons from the May operations and the special season, which goes from June to September.

items.statement: India sugar closing stocks estimated at 5.5 MMT for SY24-25
items.quote: On the back of this, closing stocks estimated at 5.5 million metric tons for the sugar year '24-'25.

items.statement: Ethanol blending at 18%, auto industry ready for 20%, beyond 20% uncertain
items.quote: In terms of the blend, I think we're up to about 18% right now. And the auto industry also is seemingly prepared for up to a 20% blend. So whether this blend will move up beyond 20%, again, that's something which is on a concrete basis yet to be determined.

items.statement: Sugar business: INR850 cr short-term, INR205 cr long-term debt
items.value: INR850 crores short-term, INR205 crores long-term
items.quote: As far as the sugar business is concerned, we have about INR850 crores as a short-term debt, about INR205 crores is the long-term debt.

items.statement: Refinery business: INR590 cr short-term external debt, INR200 cr long-term ICD from EID Parry
items.value: INR590 crores short-term, INR200 crores long-term
items.quote: So as far as the refinery business is concerned, about INR590 crores is the short-term debt, and the INR200 crores will be the long-term debt. So long-term debt is basically from the ICD, which is given by EID Parry.

items.statement: INR427 cr impairment and INR350 cr infusion in Parry Sugar Refinery in FY25
items.quote: The impairment has been done on account of poor financial performance. I think that was looked at, and I think we were required to take that impairment. In terms of the infusion, it is to strengthen the net worth of the company and also bring about some debt reduction. This is the reason for the infusion.

items.statement: Sugar Control Order extended to raw sugar declaration and larger jaggery units, refinery unaffected as export-oriented
items.quote: In the Sugar (Control) Order, they have brought in some amount of control in declaring the raw sugar with manufacturers. And also they have brought units larger than, I think, 500 TCD for Jaggery crushing, kandasari into the ambit. We believe both are welcome to make the sugar balance numbers, and create a level playing field amongst various players.

items.statement: Higher sugar production next year risks price decline; exports needed in Q4 FY26/Q1 FY27 to support pricing
items.quote: Yes, with more sugar coming into the balance and with these kinds of release quotas and sugarcane ethanol not being given as much of an impetus, there is certainly a risk of downward sliding of prices. Now which is why perhaps into Q4 of F '26 and Q1 of F '27 Q2 F '27, having an export program will certainly be something I hope the policymakers will consider strongly to ensure that pricing remains

items.statement: No plans to enter organic/chemical-free staples; supply chain not optimized for farm-level sourcing
items.quote: As of now, we are present in the conventional staples business, and we don't have any plans right now to enter the organic or chemical-free staples at this point in time. Maybe in at some future situation, we'll consider it. We haven't yet optimized the supply chain to the extent of going up to the farmers.

items.statement: Grain ethanol capacity 3.5-4 crore liters at AP multi-feed distillery; output depends on cane availability and grain ethanol pricing
items.quote: As far as the grain is concerned, you are aware of it because we have only 1 facility in AP, where about 3.5 to 4 crores liters we can produce. That also depends on whether it is a syrup or the grain, or something. It's a multifed distillery. We can't comment on '25- '26, what could be the grain ethanol exactly depends on the availability of the cane and the government outlook on the price increas

items.statement: Positive cane outlook for FY26 with good monsoon in Karnataka/TN; neutral outlook with positive base
items.quote: Current timely monsoons in Karnataka and Tamil Nadu is giving us a lot of comfort. We are still in the stage of planting. Probably by the end of next quarter, we'll have a good view of any upsides that could be there. Currently, we are holding a neutral outlook with a positive base.

items.statement: Refinery white premiums recovering in FY26 from FY25 lows; run rate to improve
items.quote: However, as Muthu explained in his commentary, there is a tightening of the supply that's happening as far as refined sugar is concerned. Most refineries took break because of the low white premium situation. So there is a correction as far as the supply side is concerned. So we are seeing the white premiums going back, may not be up to the levels that what we witnessed in FY '24, but definitely m

items.statement: Sugar closing stock 1.9 lakh MT valued at INR37.50-38 per kg
items.quote: We carry closing stock of about 1.9 lakh metric tons valued at INR37.50 to INR38.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 sugar average selling price INR39.37/kg vs INR37.50/kg YoY
items.quote: Average selling price was about INR39.37 excluding the consumer pack against the INR37.50 for the previous period.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 distillery realization INR66.98/ltr vs INR64.49/ltr YoY; revenue INR268 cr vs INR224 cr
items.quote: The current quarter realization is about INR66.98 / INR67, against the previous year's realization of about INR64.49. So though there is no increase in ethanol prices, the average sales prices have increased. So, mainly the contribution has come from the price increase in ethanol in Tamil Nadu and Karnataka. As far as the revenue is concerned, it was INR268 crores as against INR224 crores of the c

items.statement: Q4 FY25 sugar revenue INR408 cr vs INR415 cr YoY (-2%) on lower release quota
items.quote: So as far as the revenue is concerned, from sugar operations, we've done about INR408 crores against the INR415 crores of the corresponding previous quarter, registering a degrowth of about 2%. This was mainly on account of reduced release quota.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 consolidated EBITDA negative INR38.12 cr vs positive INR56.21 cr YoY
items.quote: So as far as EBITDA is concerned, for the current quarter, it's a negative before exceptional item of about INR38.12 crores, against the corresponding previous period of INR56.21 crores profit.

items.statement: E-beam products expected to generate INR 500-600 crore annual revenue at full capacity
items.quote: We expect the pl an to generate revenue when it is in full steam of about INR 500 crores to INR600 crores per year from these 2 products

items.statement: FY25 capex spend was INR 236 crore; remaining INR 500 crore plan to be completed in FY26 plus INR 40-50 crore maintenance capex
items.quote: '24, '25, our capex has been about -- actual spend has been INR 236 crores. We had announced a INR 500 crores plan 2 years ago. Out of which about INR 160 crores was spent in '23, '24. 235 -- INR236 crores was spent in the last fiscal. The remaining part will be spent in the current year.

items.statement: BharatNet consortium bids unsuccessful but discussing supply to winners; procurement started March-April with 3-year build timeline
items.quote: However, many of the winners across the 16 circles, have used our manufacturers authorization to place their bids so we are in discussion with many of those winners, and we are hopeful of a decent level of business in the current and the next years.

items.statement: Project sales share increased 8-10% over 3 years vs retail, pressuring margins due to discounting
items.quote: That would have changed maybe between -- about the 8% to 10%, that would be a shift.

items.statement: 12 price revisions in FY25 on wires (6 up, 6 down); net cost increase 12.5-13%; 3% price hike effective yesterday
items.quote: So net impact, I think costs would have gone up about 12.5% to 13%.

items.statement: Wire demand revival expected from H2 FY26 driven by construction activity completion; FY27 growth likely
items.quote: I think with the kind of construction activity that is going on, it wouldn't be far-fetched to say that the current fiscal from the second half, you should see a revival in demand.

items.statement: Margin pressures largely behind; gradual improvement expected from current levels
items.quote: I do believe that most of the margin pressure related issues are behind us. We have addressed them as best as we can. And I think that from now, one should see stable to renewal growth over the next period.

items.statement: OFC preform facility mechanically complete, trials starting this month; fiber capacity to expand from 4 to 6 million km by H2 FY26; cabling line within 6 months after fiber commissioning
items.quote: Fiber capacity -- the machine is expected sometime towards the second half of this ye ar. I think somewhere around December time frame and would take another 2 to 3 months to install and commission. So when that is done, fiber capacity will go up from the current 4 million kilometers to 6 million kilometers

items.statement: Global fiber prices recovered from $2.5/km to $3.5/km over last 2-3 months due to US/Europe demand
items.quote: So we are seeing prices firming up now. So it's closer to $3.5 right now as opposed to $2.5, which was prevail ing for most of the year last year

items.statement: EHV market currently $500M, potential $2B in 4-5 years; Finolex operates via JV with vertical process advantage
items.quote: Currently, I think the market size is approximately anywhere between $400 million to $500 million worth likely improvement towards $1.5 billion, $2 billion is not far-fetched.

items.statement: E-beam XLPE solar cables launched Feb with BIS approval; target 20-25k km/month volume; premium building wire with 25-year life also launched
items.quote: I think currently, the volume of these cables that are sold are anywhere between 20,000 to 25,000 kilometers per month, and that can only increase given the fact that our government's target to improve the power generation from solar and wind generation is climbing.

items.statement: Supply wires to major harness manufacturers; harness business ~INR 400-500 crore; Motherson dominant player
items.quote: The size -- currently, our s ize in this market is about INR400 crores, INR 500 crores. Most of the harness manufacturers are our customers

items.statement: Export limited by supplier territory agreements; may explore if preform production internalized
items.quote: So far, we have been looking, but we have contracts with our suppliers who are also in that business overseas. So there are certain terri tories where we have mutually agreed that we will not compete in

items.statement: Preform facility trials starting this month, 2-3 months to stabilize; fiber line expected Dec, 2-3 months commissioning; cabling line within 6 months after fiber
items.quote: The facility is ready. It's been mechanically installed and completed. We are waiting for the production trials to start that is slated for sometime this month. When that is over, then that should take about 2 to 3 months before the trials are over and the plant stabilizes.

items.statement: Preform utilization expected 60-70% from second year of operation; first year lower due to ramp-up
items.quote: So first year who is not going to be very high. But from the second year onwards, I expect at least a ramp-up to initially 60%, 70%.

items.statement: Order book stands at INR1,791 crores including new Jindal Explorer contract
items.quote: Order book position has been updated with the new contract of Jindal Explorer also being included. Order book stands at INR1,791 crores.

items.statement: Blended EBITDA margin of around 35% expected for FY26
items.quote: For the margin, you can take a blended margin of around 35% for the entire year.

items.statement: Gross debt reduced from INR282 crores to INR139 crores; net cash improved from INR51 crores to INR131 crores
items.quote: Our gross debt has fallen from INR282 crores in March '24 to INR139 crores in March '25, and net cash position has improved from INR51 crores in March '24 to INR131 crores in March '25.

items.statement: Debt will continue to reduce aggressively; company is net cash positive
items.quote: Yes, I've already said that. Debt will continue to reduce aggressively. And we are net cash right now. So the debt is only at a gross level.

items.statement: Jindal Pioneer acquisition completed March 5, 2025; deferred payment within 1 year funded from internal accruals
items.quote: The key development in quarter 4 FY '25 was acquisition of Rig Jindal Pioneer on 5th March 2025.

items.statement: Jindal Explorer under refurbishment, expected redeployment in November 2025
items.quote: Jindal Explorer is under refurbishment as we speak. It is expected to be redeployed on the new contract in Nov ember or maybe a little

items.statement: Now own 3 offshore jack-up rigs, operate 2 for ONGC, sixth rig under refurbishment
items.quote: In this quarter, after acquisition of Jindal Pioneer, we now own 3 offshore jack -up rigs and additionally operate 2 jack -up rigs with ONGC, with the sixth rig being currently under refurbishment.

items.statement: Discovery-1 at INR48,324/day and Jindal Star at INR44,000/day; expect higher day rates for upcoming renewals
items.quote: If you look at the rates at which Discovery - 1, Jindal Star, these 2 rigs, they are deployed at 48,324 for Discovery - 1 and Jindal Star is at 44,000. We expect day rates fo r these rigs to be much higher

items.statement: Open to global opportunities beyond ONGC; evaluating Mexico, Middle East, other markets for rig deployment
items.quote: We are looking at opportunities all around the world, and we will go with the best opportunity and whichever is the best option for the company and the rigs.

items.statement: 7 participants for 3 ONGC contracts; 3 competitor rigs desperate for work bid aggressively low
items.quote: Out of the 3 rigs that were to be contracted, there were about 7 participants, and they dropped the prices down to this level.

items.statement: Refurbishment for ONGC deployment typically takes 5-6 months; revenue starts only after deployment
items.quote: For rigs that are expected to be deployed with ONGC, refurbishment is usually 5 to 6 months. And that is also the time which is given by ONGC.

items.statement: No debt required for Jindal Pioneer purchase consideration; will be funded from internal accruals
items.quote: There will be no requirement of any debt to fund that acquisition. The shareholding structure is on the next slide, and that will conclude our presentation.

items.statement: No near-term timeline for consolidating Explorer and Virtue 1 under Jindal Drilling; shareholder approval required
items.quote: No, I don't think so we have any such plans in the near future. But yes, the consolidation is always there in the mind, but I don't have any time lines for that.

items.statement: Exploring diversification into directional drilling, mud logging, related services; no concrete plans in current year
items.quote: We are already in the space of directional drilling and mud logging. We are looking at different related services as well. And as and when we get some feasible options, we will be looking into it more strategically.

items.statement: Shareholder loans to joint ventures declining; full repayment expected in FY26
items.quote: If you look at the loan to joint ventures, it has come dow n from last year. And I think in this year, full repayment is

items.statement: Effective tax rate expected below 25% due to accelerated depreciation on acquired rig
items.quote: It will be lower than 25% because we've acquired the rig. And I'm talking about the current tax rate only. It is likely to be -- it will be lower than 25% because we have acquired the rig and we get accelerated depreciation.

items.statement: ONGC demand currently lower due to BP meetings; expect demand to increase substantially next year
items.quote: ONGC , their demand is less. That's why they're coming out with less tenders because they are having some meetings with BP to streamline their process. Once that's done by the next -- the coming year, their demand would increase substantially.

items.statement: Saudi Aramco laying off rigs creates international market uncertainty; rates flexible, contracts can be cut anytime
items.quote: Saudi Aramco in the middle had laid down a lot of rigs, leading to a lot of uncertainty. They again have laid off 3 or 4 more rigs in this quarter. Hence, the -- in the international market, the rates are flexible. It changes and they can cut your contract at any time.

items.statement: Revenue and EBITDA improved due to Jindal Pioneer acquisition and full quarter of Jindal Supreme operations
items.quote: Revenue and EBITDA improved due to this acquisition and full quarter operations of Jindal Supreme.

items.statement: Further improvement expected in revenue and earnings in Q1 FY26
items.quote: Further improvement is also expected in revenue and earnings in quarter 1 FY '26.

items.statement: Expect AUM mix to shift to 70% retail loans and 30% term loans over next few quarters
items.quote: So you will see the split hopefully changing to 70/30, where 70% over the next few quarters will end up being more retail, and 30% will be on the side of term loans.

items.statement: AUM grew 74% year-on-year in FY25
items.quote: We've grown 74% year on year.

items.statement: AUM grew almost 75% over the last one year
items.quote: I think we've grown almost 75% over the last one year.

items.statement: Blended cost of capital is sub-12%; term loan XIRR typically 16-17% and upwards
items.quote: From a blended perspective, our cost of capital must be sub 12% at this point in time. And typically when we do the term loan, from an (Extended Internal Rate of Return) XIRR perspective, everything is usually 16-17% and upwards.

items.statement: Debt-to-equity is 0.4%, resulting in higher NIMs
items.quote: Our debt to equity right now is fairly low. It's only 0.4%. So our (Net Interest Margin) NIMs end up becoming much higher.

items.statement: Current AUM split is 60% term loans and 40% retail loans
items.quote: If you see today, we almost have a 60/40 split, where there's a 60% weightage towards term loans and almost a 40% weightage towards retail loans.

items.statement: Apollo's average 30+ PAR is around 2.86% vs industry average; NPA less than 1% vs industry ~2.4%
items.quote: If we look at the rest of the industry, the average 30 PAR numbers for Apollo are around 2.86%. And even the NPA numbers on an average in the industry range to around 2.4%, and for us, it's less than a percent.

items.statement: New RBI digital lending guidelines consolidate prior circulars; no negative impact on Apollo due to conservative provisioning including FLDG cover
items.quote: Our team is quite conservative in these matters, and thankfully, that has always been the case for Apollo. So our paths reflect the provisioning even on the FLDG cover that we have. So there again, no negative impact for Apollo.

items.statement: RBI draft co-lending framework expected to have minimal impact as Apollo already operates within outlined norms
items.quote: But the initial verdict here is that not much impact to Apollo, because fortunately, we've been co-lending within the norms of what RBI has outlined in the circular.

items.statement: Term loan partnerships used to conduct deep diligence before converting to sizable co-lending/BC partnerships
items.quote: Once we like what we see, then we end up doing co-lending and BC partnerships with them. When we do these partnerships, they are sizable partnerships now.

items.statement: Distribution provides real-time data from top 10-15 industry players for benchmarking and credit algorithm inputs
items.quote: Given our distribution strategy, we've basically been able to get real-time data inputs from, I would say, the top 10 to 15 players in the industry, which really helps us in the following ways.

items.statement: AI tool 'Senti' monitors all collection calls for tone and compliance; AI voice calling being tested for 10x cost efficiency and 100% compliance
items.quote: We spoke last time about Senti, which is essentially an AI tool which Apollo has built on its own proprietary data, which allows us to monitor all calls which are going to customers and understanding the tone and anything which is potentially non-compliant, it immediately flags it.

items.statement: Onboarded best-in-class collection agencies across India that work with top FinTechs
items.quote: We've also recognized a few best-in-class collection agencies across India who are already working with some of the best FinTechs in the ecosystem today, and we've onboarded them with Apollo.

items.statement: Industry slowdown due to RBI risk weight increase on unsecured loans; seeing early signs of recovery with potential RBI relaxation
items.quote: In the industry we have seen some degree of slowdown, and I think it's been a combination of regulatory scrutiny as well. From the RBI perspective, a few months back they had increased the risk weightages for unsecured books, which led essentially from a top-down perspective less capital to be available.

items.statement: Avoids high debt-to-equity (>2.5x) in digital lending partners due to regulatory volatility risk
items.quote: What we've observed in this space is that debt to equity anywhere upwards of 2.5 in this space starts to look very, very heavy for the company, because a regulatory change may make their book incredibly volatile.

items.statement: ROEs consistently in double digits over last 8 years despite young industry
items.quote: One of the things that we're incredibly proud of is that, if you see our record over the last 8 years, despite it being a very young industry, our ROEs have always been in double digits.

items.statement: Building proprietary tech stack vertically integrated for Apollo and its co-lending/BC partners only; not offering tech to legacy lenders
items.quote: Our focus is more towards vertical integration where Apollo ends up building tech largely for itself, or only for the potential partners it does co-lending or BC lending with.

items.statement: Growth cycle depends on deploying capital with good partners to attract debt capital at right rates
items.quote: The more good partners you work with, the more capital you are able to deploy. The books also perform better and the better the books perform we are able to raise capital at the right rates, and also raise a lot of capital in order to continue the cycle.

items.statement: Expect good progress in co-lending partnerships in coming quarters with interesting partners already taken exposure via term loans
items.quote: We do expect good progress to be coming as well in the quarters ahead, and there are some interesting partners that we've taken exposure on from a term loan perspective that we now will be converting to BC co-lending partnerships as well.

items.statement: Focus on sustainable growth over speed; avoid growing at negative ROE or below FD rates
items.quote: We don't want to be a company which is growing a thousand percent, etc., because the reality is that whenever we've seen companies in the ecosystem do that, it's not led to good results.

items.statement: Exploring WhatsApp, Paytm, Google Pay, UPI for repayment channels to improve collection convenience and timing
items.quote: Now, we're exploring channels such as WhatsApp, even potentially apps like Paytm or apps like Google Pay, where they will see notifications about an EMI which is due, or the loan amount which is due, and just by simply using UPI, they can make the repayment back.

items.statement: AUM dipped slightly from ~85 to ~83 crore quarter-on-quarter; management views this as not meaningful and focuses on annual growth
items.quote: I think it's gone from some 85 to 83, if I have the numbers correctly, so I don't look at it as a meaningful dip either way.

items.statement: Revenue growth guidance of sub-20% for FY26 and 15% CAGR long-term
items.quote: So overall growth, as we mentioned in our previous call also is in the range of somewhere around sub-20%. That's the top line growth we are anticipating in current financial year '25-'26.

items.statement: FY26 growth forecast of 20-25% and 15% CAGR long-term
items.quote: I think going forward in FY '26, we continue a similar between a 20% to 25% growth rate forecast for FY '26.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance of 9.5-10% for FY26
items.quote: So, you can see this kind of a margin maybe closer to about 10% or 9.5%, somewhere in this range going for the next fiscal year.

items.statement: Tooling revenue guidance of INR240-260 crores for FY26
items.quote: next year, we will see somewhere around range of INR240 crores to INR260-odd crores from tooling business.

items.statement: Tooling margin guidance of 12-15% sustained
items.quote: I would say the guidance would be that we should continue anywhere between 12% to 15% on tooling margins, which would be on a sustained basis.

items.statement: LED revenue share target of 65% for FY26
items.quote: And in FY '26, we are actually looking at probably 65% of total revenue coming from LED lighting.

items.statement: Order book of INR2,275 crores with 37% EV and 85% PV allocation
items.quote: Looking ahead, we are pleased to report a healthy order book of INR2,275 crores. Notably, 37 % of this is dedicated to the electric vehicles and 85% is allocated to the Passenger Vehicle segment.

items.statement: 55-60% of order book from Maruti Suzuki and SMG
items.quote: That's correct, almost close to 55% to 60% is from Maruti Suzuki and SMG put together.

items.statement: 50-60% of order book to convert to SOP in FY26
items.quote: almost close to more than 50% to 60% of the order book will actually come in FY '26 as well across different manufacturing facilities.

items.statement: Capex guidance of INR180-220 crores for FY26
items.quote: The guidance for FY '26 would be continuing in a similar time of approximately between INR180 crores to INR220 crores.

items.statement: No specific capex guidance for FY27 but asset turnover expected to improve
items.quote: We do not have any specific capex guidance for FY '27, but considering the massive growth, which we are building in FY '26, we do believe that the asset turnover ratios also should improve compared to FY '25 in FY '27.

items.statement: Chakan Phase 1 capacity utilization at 70-80%, targeting 90% in FY26
items.quote: So, on Phase 1, our capacity utilization is around 70% to 80%. And this year, we are expecting that it will touch somewhere around 90%.

items.statement: Chakan Phase 2 SOP scheduled Q2 FY26, peak revenue INR250-300 crores in FY27
items.quote: The peak revenue from Phase 2 is expected to come in FY '27, and that would be in the range of INR250 crores to INR300 crores.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 EBITDA margin 9.2%, manufacturing EBITDA 9.8%
items.quote: We witnessed a margin of 9.2% for the quarter marking the highest quarterly margin performance of the fiscal year.

items.statement: FY25 manufacturing EBITDA margin 8.7% excluding tooling
items.quote: if we see our manufacturing EBITDA for the quarter 4 is at 9.8% and on a full year basis, we are at 8.7%.

items.statement: LED lighting 58% of FY25 revenue, up from 39% in FY24
items.quote: For FY '25, LED lighting accounted for 58% of our total revenue, a significant rise from 39% in the previous year.

items.statement: 88% of order book dedicated to LED lighting
items.quote: Further, 88% of our current order book is dedicated to LED lighting, underscoring our confidence in expanding this segment.

items.statement: FY25 segment mix: 66% PV, 28% 2W, 6% CV
items.quote: Regarding our segment mix for FY '25, revenue contribution stood at 66% from passenger vehicles, 28% from 2-wheelers and 6% from commercial vehicles.

items.statement: Top 3 customers: Maruti 24%, Mahindra 20%, HMSI 14% of FY25 revenue
items.quote: Maruti contributed 24%, Mahindra 20% and HMSI 14%.

items.statement: Industry outlook 4-5% growth with export restrictions on rare earth elements as risk
items.quote: if I look at the SIAM data, we're actually looking at the overall industry growth of about 4% to 5%, there are certain headwinds, particularly on the export restrictions, what China has done on the REE, which means the rare earth elements.

items.statement: LED import content: LED module imported, PCB localizing, SMT localized, connectors imported
items.quote: LED typically has 4 items. One is the LED module which is primarily being imported and will continue to be imported in the coming years also. The second is a Bare PCB, wherein I mentioned some PCBs that we have already localized, and the remaining ones will get localized in the due course of time. The third thing is related to SMT, which is in India also and for us, we already have our SMT plant,

items.statement: No new term loans in FY26, repaying INR70-80 crores, working capital loans may increase
items.quote: we are not looking for, as we mentioned in our last call, we are not looking for any, new term loan for the business. So, in fact, we will repay somewhere around INR70 crores to INR80 crores in this current fiscal year. And as far as working capital requirement because business expansion will continue, so some working capital requirement would arise, especially because the electronic components Lu

items.statement: Content per vehicle increases ~20% with each technological shift
