items.quote: The average content per vehicle should go up by approximately close to 20% with every technological shift.

items.statement: SIAM warns of industry disruptions in June-July due to China rare earth export restrictions
items.quote: as recent as last week, SIAM has put out a caution note where they say that the industry could have certain disruptions in the month of June and July.

items.statement: SL Lumax revenue INR3,000 crores, 11% growth, 17.9% EBITDA margin
items.quote: SL Lumax has registered a sale of close to INR3,000 crores, with a year-on-year growth of approximately 11% with the EBITDA margin of 17.9%.

items.statement: Expects to sustain strong growth in revenue and margins in FY26 supported by diversification and raw material cost improvements
items.quote: Looking ahead to FY ‘26, we expect to sustain strong growth in both revenue and margins, supported by our strategic diversification efforts and improvements in raw material sourcing and cost management.

items.statement: Total project cost for 75 KLPD biodiesel plant is INR 140 crores, majority already incurred
items.quote: The total project cost is around INR 140 crores for the 75 KLPD biodiesel plant. As mentioned in my speech, we are expecting to commission this in July 2025.

items.statement: 150 KLPD ethanol plant at Bathinda has total CapEx of INR 110 crores, about INR 30 crores incurred so far
items.quote: And the 150 KLPD ethanol plant, total CapEx is around INR 110 crores. And I think the company has incurred about INR 30-odd crores on that front.

items.statement: 150 KLPD ethanol expansion at Bathinda expected to commission by December 2025, all clearances in hand
items.quote: The work for 150 expansion at Bathinda is progressing well, with all clearances in hand, and we are hoping to commission this plant by December 2025.

items.statement: 75 KLPD biodiesel plant at Bathinda expected to commission in July 2025, at advanced stage of development
items.quote: Our 75 KLPD biodiesel plant in Bathinda is at an advanced stage of development, and is expected to be commissioned in July 2025.

items.statement: 60 tonne per hour paddy straw boiler expected to commission by November 2025 to reduce fuel costs
items.quote: In addition, the installation of a 60 tonne per hour paddy straw boiler is in progress, which is aimed to reduce fuel costs further for our company and improve operational efficiency. We are expecting to commission this boiler in November 2025.

items.statement: Maize oil extraction unit final trials started, expected to commission along with biodiesel unit in July 2025
items.quote: We have started the final trials for the maize oil extraction unit. And I am hoping to commission the same along with the biodiesel unit.

items.statement: 250 KLPD ethanol plant at Goyal Distillery planned after 150 KLPD Bathinda commissioning, no timeline given
items.quote: For 250 KLPD Goyal Distillery, we are planning on starting the work for that once the 150 KLPD plant has been commissioned at Bathinda, as we don’t want to overburden our books and ourselves with the multifold expansions.

items.statement: Maize oil extraction unit at Svaksha Distillery expected to commission by October 2025, oil to be processed at Bathinda
items.quote: We are expecting to commission the maize oil extraction unit at Svaksha by October of this year.

items.statement: Biodiesel market gap of 80-90 crore liters OMC requirement unmet, BCL positioned to cater
items.quote: For the biodiesel business, I think the overall requirement by the OMCs for this year was around, I think, 80 crore, 90 crore liters, if I am correct. And out of which they were unable to get anywhere close to that.

items.statement: Distillery margins expected to improve in next 1-2 quarters due to softening raw material prices from FCI rice and maize harvest
items.quote: For the distillery business, we are expecting that the margins for the next at least 1 or 2 quarters should improve since raw material prices are starting to stop in, thanks to the FCI rice and bumper crop for maize, especially in UP, Punjab and Bihar.

items.statement: Overall blended margins set to improve as edible oil business shuts down and distillery/biodiesel become primary revenue contributors
items.quote: So once the edible oil business is shut, of course, the cumulative margins will go up as distillery and biodiesel will be the primary contributor towards the revenue. So of course, the cumulative margins are set to go up with the shutting down of edible oil business.

items.statement: At maize INR 24/kg, maize more profitable than FCI rice at INR 22.5/kg due to rice DDGS price decline
items.quote: So when prices for maize are at INR 24, I would like to change my statement and say that maize is more profitable as opposed to FCI rice.

items.statement: At maize INR 25/kg, profitability around same as FCI rice
items.quote: At INR 25, it’d probably be around the same.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 average maize price around INR 25.5/kg; FY26 expected average INR 25-25.5/kg after MSP increase to INR 24
items.quote: So my forecast for this year, honestly, going by last year, I think it is tough to make a forecast. But with the relief of surplus rice for the ethanol industry, I expect that maize prices for the entire year should average around INR 25 to INR 25.5, because as of yesterday or day before, the government has also increased the MSP for maize to INR 24 now.

items.statement: Current maize prices in May around INR 24-24.5/kg, will reflect in procurement from mid-May
items.quote: Yes, see the maize prices have started to reduce, especially in the month of May. So of course, that will come into effect starting say mid-May to 1st May.

items.statement: FCI rice price fixed at INR 22.50/kg at nearest depot plus freight
items.quote: See, the price is at INR 22.50 per kg. And that is at the nearest depot, plus freight to bring the same to our factory.

items.statement: Bathinda unit currently meets 60% fuel demand from paddy straw, 40% from rice husk; targets 100% paddy straw by Oct-Nov 2025 with new boiler
items.quote: So for Bathinda unit, about 60% of our fuel demand currently is being met by paddy straw and about 40% from rice husk. By October or November of this year, we are hoping that we will be 100% reliant on paddy straw with the commissioning of our new boiler.

items.statement: Paddy straw boiler to provide fixed fuel price for year, benefit of INR 1-2/liter vs rice husk at current low prices
items.quote: But the benefit will be there when and if rice husk prices again increase, which they’re bound to go up, because it is cyclical just like everything else. But paddy straw since we buy for the entire year, will have a fixed fuel price for us.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 ethanol volume up 18% YoY to 45,921 KL; ENA volume 9,313 KL vs 8,185 KL YoY
items.quote: Our distillery segment showed robust volume growth with ethanol volume rising by 18% to 45,921 KL, while ENA volumes reaching 9,313 KL from 8,185 KL from the previous year.

items.statement: All current expansions focused on ethanol, not ENA
items.quote: No, all the expansions that are taking place now are on ethanol.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 raw material mix mostly maize; from Q1 FY26 started using ~30% FCI rice
items.quote: I don’t have the exact figures. But for Q4, I think most of the processing was done on maize. It is mainly from Q1 that we have started to use a little bit of FCI rice as well. About 30% of FCI rice.

items.statement: IMIL segment sold ~17 lakh cases in FY25 with healthy demand, significant market share, momentum expected to sustain
items.quote: Our IMIL segment delivered a strong performance this year with approximately 17 lakh cases sold in FY ‘25, supported by a healthy demand. We continue to hold a significant market share in this segment and expect this momentum to sustain in the coming quarters.

items.statement: Term loans: INR 120 cr (Bathinda expansion, outstanding INR 107 cr, interest subvention), INR 51 cr (Svaksha, outstanding INR 39 cr), INR 65 cr (Svaksha expansion, outstanding INR 65 cr, interest subvention), INR 50 cr (biodiesel, outstandi
items.value: INR 107 cr + INR 39 cr + INR 65 cr + INR 50 cr term loans outstanding
items.quote: The company has a term loan of INR 120 crores for the expansion that took place in Bathinda. And so the INR 120 crore term loan has an outstanding of INR 107 crores now, and it’s under interest subvention. The company had taken INR 51 crores loan for Svaksha. Current outstanding is INR 39 crores. The company had taken an INR 65 crore again, term loan for Svaksha expansion, which is under interest

items.statement: Company actively reducing debt through internal accruals; no specific FY26 repayment target given
items.quote: The company is actively working to reduce its debt through internal accruals.

items.statement: No fund raise mentioned; expansions funded through internal accruals and existing debt facilities
items.quote: Yes. Through internal approvals only.

items.statement: Appointed CEO Varun Gupta to assist in administration, HR, finance, accounts, distillery, biodiesel and administrative work; Kushal Mittal remains involved in day-to-day operations
items.quote: Varun ji has joined us with the vast experience, and he will be assisting the company in all matters, whether that is administration, HR, finance, accounts, and overall, helping the company become more efficient, be compliant. And overall, he’ll be responsible for the distillery business, the biodiesel business, and all the administrative work.

items.statement: Dividend of INR 0.26 maintained; no special dividend for 50th year due to expansion mode and long-term sustainability focus
items.quote: The company is in an expansion mode. And that’s why the dividend of INR 0.26 was announced. And even when the company was growing at a significant, significant speed, when we became from 200 to 700 KLPD company. The company always gave out dividend, even when the promoters had to forego their right to dividend, they did that to ensure the minority shareholders gets their dividend annually.

items.statement: Government unlikely to allow maize/ethanol imports as it would collapse farmer-ethanol ecosystem; MSP increases focused on maize for crop diversification
items.quote: We believe that the government of India will not budge on this request to allow the import of ethanol or even maize. Because see, as I have mentioned multiple times, this policy of biofuels in the country, of course, you hear the benefits that it’s a green fuel. It decreases the import bill for the country. All those are major, major reasons to promote this industry. But the biggest reason we have

items.statement: Revenue target at 850 KLPD capacity: INR 2,100-2,200 crores; additional 250 KLPD to add INR 700-750 crores
items.value: INR 2,100-2,200 crores at 850 KLPD; INR 700-750 crores additional at 250 KLPD
items.quote: See, the first phase is 700 to 850 which we are expecting before the end of this calendar year. So a conservative figure for 850 capacity is around INR 2,100 to INR 2,200 crores in terms of revenue. And the next stage would be post that of 250. So that should give us at least another INR 700 crores to INR 750 crores in revenue.

items.statement: Biodiesel plant at 100% utilization (75 KLPD) expected to generate INR 200-225 crores revenue; EBITDA margin forecast not given yet
items.quote: For the revenue figures, working at 100% capacity utilization at 75 KLPD biodiesel plant should give us around INR 200 crores to INR 225-odd crores in terms of revenue. For the EBITDA margins, I will stay consistent as my statements that I have made in the past. We are not giving a forecast on that front as of yet.

items.statement: FCI rice allocation for ethanol reinstated at fixed price INR 22.5/kg; enhances supply chain efficiency and surplus stock management
items.quote: Following the reinstatement of FCI rights for ethanol production at a fixed price of INR 22.5 per kilogram, the industry has welcomed this policy as a positive development that enhances supply chain efficiency and optimize its surplus stock management.

items.statement: Government increased maize MSP to INR 24/kg for kharif cycle to incentivize crop diversification away from paddy
items.quote: because as of yesterday or day before, the government has also increased the MSP for maize to INR 24 now.

items.statement: No inventory loss in March 2025; some edible oil inventory sold at discount to liquidate
items.quote: Yes, there was no such notional loss. I think with the oil unit shutting down some inventory is being sold at sometimes at a discounted price to liquidate it as soon as possible. But besides that, nothing particular.

items.statement: Land bank value from solvent plant shutdown not evaluated; focus on shutting unit and commissioning biodiesel
items.quote: We haven’t evaluated on the value. Our focus for now is to do as soon as possible, shut down the unit and commission the biodiesel unit. So honestly, we don’t even know. We haven’t inquired.

items.statement: FY26 revenue expected to dip ~20% and profit ~30% due to US headwinds, pricing pressure and higher R&D
items.quote: The company estimates a possible dip in revenue by 20% and profits by 30% due to geopolitical uncertainties and pricing pressure in its core product portfolio in the U.S. and increased R&D expenses.

items.statement: First half FY26 expected to be good, second half weaker than first half
items.quote: I would say that the first half will be good, but second half will not be as strong as the second half. The second half will be weaker than the first half.

items.statement: Annual capex run-rate ~INR300-350 crore; total project pipeline ~INR500-600 crore over 1.5-2 years
items.quote: Every year, we spend about INR300 crores to INR350 crores. So, we have a capex plan of about INR500 crores, INR600 crores, but per year, looks like we're going to spend about INR300 crores.

items.statement: Of FY26 R&D budget, ~INR25-30 crore for NCE programs, rest for generics
items.quote: Of the INR400 crores, how much are we going to spend in NCE and how much go es to Agro, the NCE will probably see about, INR25 crores to INR30 crores, I would estimate in that amount roughly

items.statement: Domestic base business growth 7-10%; key growth drivers Risdiplam (subject to court) and Semaglutide (expected end FY26)
items.quote: I think of the publicly announced pipeline, I think the base business should grow around 7% to 10%. But I think the 2 major launches that will drive the growth. I think one is Risdiplam, subject to the court decision and of course, Semaglutide, which we're expecting maybe end of the financial year.

items.statement: Conservative dividend to preserve cash for acquisitions; no aggressive distribution planned
items.quote: Regarding distribution of the money, as of now, I'm saving all the money for the acquisition. So, we believe that we'll be able to close something. That's the reason why we have not given an aggressive dividend.

items.statement: No need to raise debt for acquisitions currently; comfortable with cash position (~INR3,500 crore)
items.quote: Right now, we don't need that. I think right now, we're very comfortable. I think when it comes to closing, we'll see. I think as of now, I don't want to comment. As of now, we are comfortable, yes.

items.statement: Revlimid profit share: booked some in Q4 FY25, will continue in Q1-Q2 FY26; no quantity restrictions from December 2025
items.quote: For the new quota that we got, we booked some amount in the March quarter, which is the January to March quarter in 2025. And this quota, we will start selling, we're selling now, and we'll sell in the June quarter and the September quarter and then I think December, I'm not able to predict what's going to happen. So that's why we're being cautious. In the March for the '26 year, like it will be a

items.statement: US policy/tariff uncertainty and pricing pressure make FY26 guidance conservative; guidance factors political risk, portfolio change and R&D spend
items.quote: As I said, see when we make an estimation, we consider multiple factors and multiple assumptions. If I could change my assumptions, I'll come and tell you based on how the policies change. But we have assumed the political risk and the change in the portfo lio and the R&D expenditure. So, we have factored certain things in

items.statement: VRS program done ~2 years ago; ongoing cost optimisation ex-R&D
items.quote: We have done a lot of cost cutting. We have done a VRS program about 2 years ago. I think costs, we're looking at it all the time. Yes. it's an ongoing process all the time.

items.statement: Management not comfortable giving ROE estimate for FY26; expects microfinance to be independently profitable by Q2 FY26
items.quote: I do not think I am comfortable giving an estimate at this point.

items.statement: Consolidated profitability expected to continue; microfinance subsidiary expected to be independently profitable by Q2 FY26
items.quote: Honestly, by Q2, we are expecting even micro to be independently profitable.

items.statement: MFI disbursements declined 26% YoY in Q4 FY25 and 35% YoY for full year FY25; April-May 2025 disbursements slow
items.quote: For Namra of finance, quarterly disbursements stood at Rs. 393 crores, reflecting a year-on-year decline of 26%. For the full year, disbursements amounted to Rs. 1,232 crores compared to Rs. 1,895 crores in FY '24.

items.statement: MFI rejection rate near 80%; real income growth flat for 4 years while household retail debt up 40-50%
items.quote: Our rejection rate I think in the micro book and in the MSME book also is almost 80%. So while the inquiry is there, there is just a lot of stress in the rural markets.

items.statement: OPEX increased significantly due to hiring 160 BCMs, 600 recovery officers, higher travel costs; expected to stabilize in absolute terms
items.quote: We have hired around almost 160 BCMs which are more expensive normally than other people in the team. Plus the structure above them will be another 30 people. Plus another 600 or so recovery officers are on the team right now.

items.statement: Namra Finance AUM declined 23% YoY to Rs. 1,686 crores; consolidated AUM declined 15% YoY to Rs. 2,245 crores
items.quote: As of March 31st, 2025, Namra finances AUM declined by 23% from Rs. 2,193 crores in FY '24 to Rs. 1,686 crores in FY '25.

items.statement: Standalone AUM (MSME, micro-LAP, 2-Wheeler) grew 25% YoY to Rs. 560 crores; disbursements up 20% YoY to Rs. 481 crores
items.quote: As of March 31st, 2025, standalone AUM stood at Rs. 560 crores, registering a year-on-year growth of 25%.

items.statement: Consolidated GNPA improved 75 bps QoQ to 3.37% in March 2025; MFI zero DPD collection efficiency improved to 98.8% in March 2025
items.quote: As of 31st March 2025, our gross non-performing assets stood at 3.37%, representing an improvement of 75 basis points from 4.13% in December 2024.

items.statement: MFI zero bucket collection efficiency 98.5% for Q4 FY25, improved to 98.8% in March 2025; consolidated collection efficiency 95.3% for all buckets
items.quote: For the MFI book, zero bucket collection efficiency for the quarter stood at about 98.5% and improved to 98.8% in March 2025.

items.statement: Accelerated provisioning of Rs. 117 crores in FY25 (5.23% of consolidated AUM); Stage-2 assets Rs. 85 crores with Rs. 38 crores provision
items.quote: In FY '25, the company has adopted an aggressive provisioning policy with cumulative provisions for the year standing at Rs. 117 crores, covering 5.23% of the consolidated AUM.

items.statement: 34% of MFI AUM covered under CGFMU scheme as of March 2025; coverage provides 75% guarantee on defaults
items.quote: As of March 2025, 34% of our MFI AUM is now covered under this scheme. And this will increase significantly quarter on quarter.

items.statement: New credit and recovery structure implemented in 140 of 391 branches; full rollout by Q2 FY26; expected to add 1% to OPEX
items.quote: Currently, we have implemented the new credit structure in about 140 of our 391 branches, with the remaining branches to be implemented by Q2 of FY '26.

items.statement: Cost of borrowings stable; marginal cost down 25-50 bps over last 6 months; MCLR not yet reflecting repo rate cuts
items.quote: The marginal cost of borrowing for the last six months has incrementally kind of come down only by about 25 to 50 basis points.

items.statement: Fully compliant with new MFIN guardrails as of March 2025; industry AUM declined from Rs. 4.5 lakh crores to ~Rs. 3.7 lakh crores
items.quote: We are also fully compliant with the new MFIN guardrails as of March end, and we have also successfully completed an ARC transaction in March of 2025.

items.statement: Rural stress persists in Rajasthan, parts of Gujarat; Maharashtra, MP, UP, Bihar showing improvement; Karnataka exposure under 1%
items.quote: I mean, honestly, that changes. Every state seems to be taking its own turn. So if you were to ask me right now, it's probably Rajasthan.

items.statement: MFI attrition rate 62-63% in FY25 (peaked at 68%); target to reduce to 40% in H1 FY26 but dependent on credit cycle improvement
items.quote: So, yes, I think last year we ended at about 62% or 63%, which is overall it had reached all the way to like 68% I believe, so Q 4 was a lot better

items.statement: Completed ARC transaction in March 2025: sold Rs. 185 crores portfolio for Rs. 36.75 crores (15% cash, 85% SRs); 95% written off in FY25
items.quote: We have also successfully completed an ARC transaction in March of 2025.

items.statement: MFI zero DPD collection efficiency: 97.3% in Nov 2024 -> 98.8% in March 2025; PAR 1-30 bucket ~18%
items.quote: November zero bucket was 97.4. We peaked at about 98.8 in March and about 98.5 in April.

items.statement: MFI customers with 3+ lenders: ~23% (down from 26-27% in Sep 2024); daily credit bureau reporting implemented
items.quote: I think three plus would be about 23%, I think it would have come down to 23%.

items.statement: Standalone segments (MSME, micro-LAP, 2-Wheeler) now 25% of consolidated AUM; MSME GNPA 3.38%, zero DPD 99.5%
items.quote: Our other books, which is MSME, 2-Wheeler and micro-LAP, which are now over 30% (Errata: Actual Number to be read as 25%) of the overall book.

items.statement: MSME customers largely distinct from MFI (<5-6% overlap); pilot for individual MFI loans planned late Q1/early Q2 FY26
items.quote: We will probably launch a pilot I think sometime late this quarter or early next quarter, and we will see where things go, on an individual micro finance product.

items.statement: Surplus liquidity of Rs. 269 crores; debt-equity ratio 1.3x; capital adequacy 37.34% (standalone) and 48.37% (Namra)
items.quote: Our consolidated balance sheet remains strong, supported by healthy debt equity ratio of 1.3x and surplus liquidity of Rs. 269 crores.

items.statement: Hired new credit head reporting to CRO; 160 BCMs and 600 recovery officers added; field officer disbursements per FO halved
items.quote: We have hired a new credit head to oversee that who's reporting to the CRO. And as I said, are in different states we are trying slightly different modified versions to see which one works best.

items.statement: Industry-wide degrowth accepted; most MFIs cautious; no consensus on whether to revive JLG culture or adopt individual lending
items.quote: everybody has made peace with the fact that degrowth is not a bad word. Alok Patel: Yes, it happens. Vivek Modi: It happens. And asset quality is going to be the key concern

items.statement: CGFMU premium ~1% of portfolio outstanding per year (~1.6-1.75% over 2-year tenor); expected to offset credit costs
items.quote: So, it's about 1% of the portfolio outstanding of the custom per year. So that should come out to be about 1.6% or 1.75% for the life of the customer.

items.statement: Management expects revenue to increase in FY26 as recently launched properties mature, targeting 40% average EBITDA margin over project life; first-year EBITDA margin reached 34-35% in FY25
items.quote: So, the more lucrative and more incremental EBITDA margin you will find in '26. As well as, in terms of turnover also you will find a major chunk of incremental revenue in top line.

items.statement: Operating 17-18 resorts with 775+ rooms; plans to build 5-10 resorts in FY26 adding ~505 rooms; Vision 2028 targets 2,500+ rooms across 55-65 locations
items.quote: In this year, we have planned to build five to 10 resorts, which we are under progress. So, right now we are operating in 17 to 18 resorts, still two, three locations is under development.

items.statement: ~Rs 100 crore of work-in-progress to convert to fixed assets in FY26 for Thinnakara-II (200 rooms); additional Rs 30-40 crore needed to complete 4-5 current resorts
items.quote: Major way we have invested CAPEX, in Thinnakara there is 200 rooms. So, this year, our work in progress will convert into development around Rs. 100 crores, approximately Rs. 100 crores, and work in progress goes to the fixed assets.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin 34.02% in FY25 vs 35.09% in FY24; dip due to 60% of resorts launched in FY25; expects margin expansion as properties mature over 6-12 months
items.quote: So, 1% EBITDA margin variation. This variation is dependent upon the proportion of the newly started resorts in this year was maximum.

items.statement: ARR at new properties like Jawai (Rs 18-22k vs guided Rs 25k) and Kevadiya lower due to seasonal effects, marketing strategy, and government date blocks; expects improvement after 1 year of operations
items.quote: Always, we need to have minimum one year for improving ARR status of the new project. So, Jawai is a new project.

items.statement: Strategic partnerships with IHCL SeleQtions (management contract for Bangaram/Thinnakara) and Mahindra Holidays (80-room bulk inventory allocation); Mahindra pays no fees, brings sales; IHCL fee minor, industry-standard
items.quote: Mahindra is not taking any money from us, any charges from us. Mahindra is giving a contribution to us in terms of sales, number one.

items.statement: Rann Utsav 2024-25: master franchisee for 400 luxury tents via Lallooji & Sons; Praveg operates 76 own rooms; Q4 recognized Rs 1.5 cr from bulk booking, Rs 7-8 cr from own rooms, Rs 2 cr from events
items.quote: It's a Rs. 1.5 crores contribution in terms of accounting standards. We have bulk done a business, but it will be treated as a principal concept.

items.statement: Occupancy ~50% in FY25 on adjusted available room nights (1.6-1.7 lakh vs 2.5 lakh theoretical); expects higher in FY26 with full-year operations of 18 resorts
items.quote: Yes, the average beyond that we have achieved.

items.statement: Company is debt-free; no plans to raise debt; funding via internal accruals, warrants, and asset-light development model where landowners fund capex
items.quote: We are a debt-free company right now. We do not want to raise any debt. That is our strategy.

items.statement: Warrant funds suffice for current expansion; promoter group may contribute if needed; asset-light model generates development revenue without capex
items.quote: We have already resources to have a fund of warrants that will suffice to develop this high resort.

items.statement: International expansion progressing: Serengeti (Tanzania) got environment clearance, 25-room resort to start soon; exploring Masai Mara (Kenya) acquisitions; expects higher per-room revenue than India
items.quote: Serengeti, we have just two days before got environment clearance, that is the final certification for that project. And the project team is working on it.

items.statement: Shift to high-end experiential hospitality (caves, jungle, island) with lower competition and location advantages; not pursuing city metro hotels; engineering team of 50 executes unique designs
items.quote: We want to work only in experiential hospitalities, beautiful, scenic, rivers, seashores, jungles, like that places were we can give more experience to my tourists.

items.statement: Lakshadweep permits simplified: Praveg now issues guest vouchers and handles backend KYC with government; no police clearance needed; flights increased from 1 to 4, 3 more planned
items.quote: Now t hey have issued our direction to Praveg, then Praveg gives vouchers, and Praveg KYC becomes the entry voucher, and Praveg will do back wo rk with that government authority to issuing the permits

items.statement: Lease/rent cost Rs 16 crore in FY25 (~10% of revenue); expects operating leverage as revenue grows on fixed cost base
items.quote: Rs. 16 crores. This year we paid about Rs. 16 crores rent, total. So, it's about you can understand 10% of the total revenue.

items.statement: Acquired Abhik and Bidhan (advertising) for smart toilet/hoarding credentials; enables contracts like GUDA (300 hoardings), HPCL Maharashtra/Goa; expanding to Delhi, Gurgaon, UP, Rajasthan
items.quote: The last two years, the logic behind acquisition of the particular company, the major purpose was to create a SPV which has exclusivity of smart toilets project in Ahmedabad.

items.statement: Advertising revenue grew 80-90% YoY in FY25; smart toilet model: zero capex, Rs 1-5 lakh/month hoarding revenue per unit; targets 1,500 units over 5-10 years
items.quote: Sir, you can see this first year of revenue, that's incremental around 80%, 90% of the last year's revenue.

items.statement: Kevadiya revenue impacted 15-20% due to government date blocks not converting; re-strategized with conferences and weddings; Kumbh Mela diverted tourists in Q4 FY25
items.quote: My Kevadiya performance in earlier year and this year, there is a variation of about 15% in total sell volume. 15% to 20% sell volume is impacted.

items.statement: FDA warning letter received for Gagillapur facility; remediation ongoing with three consulting firms; operations slowdown expected for another quarter or two
items.quote: On February 26 , 2025, we received a warning letter from the FDA for the site. The warning letter does not affect the supply of approved commercial products. However, it may temporarily impact the FDA's review of pending product submissions from this facility until the ma tter is resolved.

items.statement: Gagillapur facility operations slowdown due to FDA remediation; expected to continue for another quarter or two
items.quote: While manufacturing and distribution continue, the ongoing remediation measures have resulted in a slowdown of operations, which impacted our Q4 output and is expected to continue for another quarter or two.

items.statement: New product launches from GPI facility in US including lisdexamfetamine capsules and chewables, paracetamol-oxycodone, paracetamol-hydrocodone, dofetilide capsules
items.quote: During Q4, we received approval for lisdexamfetamine capsules following the early approval of the chewable tablet formulation in Q3. With this, we now have both dosage forms, capsules and chewables approved and commercially launched, enhancing our presence in the CNS and segment.

items.statement: Genome Valley Phase-1 (2.5 billion dosage) commissioned with commercial dispatch of monograph products; Phase-2 (7.5 billion dosage) commissioned in current quarter with validation started
items.quote: Our new formulation facility at Genome Valley under Granules Life Sciences is progressing well. Phase-1 with a capacity of 2.5 billion dosage has been commissioned and commercial dispatch of monograph products are ongoing.

items.statement: Genome Valley Phase-2 capacity of 7.5 billion dosage available from next month; expect 40-50% utilization this year, 90% by FY27 end after FDA/EU approvals expected in Q2 FY26
items.quote: 7.5 billion is, I think, you can say 7.5 billion capacity by next month onwards, okay. So, 7.5 billion from next month, but it will take us time to get into full utilization, because we must need to get approval from the FDA and the European authorities, which we expect to have in Q2. Once we get this approval, we will start full production and then I think by possibly this year, we may do about 4

items.statement: Acquired Senn Chemicals (Swiss peptide CDMO) in April 2025; integration in progress; entity at breakeven/slight loss with CHF20M annual sales
items.quote: We have completed acquisition formalities in April, and integration activities are in progress. We would provide more updates in the coming quarters.

items.statement: FY26 capex guided at Rs. 600 crores including GLS, oncology, peptide investments and Senn Chemicals capex; Senn Chemicals acquisition at Rs. 450 crores enterprise value
items.quote: So FY '26, overall CAPEX estimate is about Rs. 600 crores. This includes further CAPEX, which we have to incur for Granules Life Science and also oncology and peptide investment.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 gross margin 63.4% (+333 bps YoY, +169 bps QoQ) driven by higher formulation sales mix; FY25 gross margin up 635 bps YoY
items.quote: Our gross margin as a percentage of sales for Q4 FY '25 was 63.4% as compared to 60.1% in Q4 FY '24. Gross margin as compared to Q4 FY '24 is up by 333 basis points achieved due to higher finished dosages, sales with higher margin.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 EBITDA margin 21.1% (-67 bps YoY, +83 bps QoQ) impacted by FDA remediation consultancy fees; FY25 EBITDA grew 10% to Rs. 9,452M
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter was Rs. 2,524 million, that is 21.1% of sales as compared to Rs. 2,557 million, that is 21.7% of sales in Q4 FY '24, a decrease of 67 basis points from Q4 FY '24.

items.statement: No formal FY26 revenue/EBITDA guidance given; management expects FY26 to be better than FY25 despite Gagillapur slowdown continuing for 1-2 quarters
items.quote: We cannot give you any guidance on this, but definitely all I can say is it's going to be better than last year. And I also want to make it clear that the slowdown on operation in Gagillapur will continue for a quarter or two. Despite that, we think that we will do better than last year.

items.statement: Cash-to-cash cycle 202 days in Q4 FY25 vs 213 days Q3 FY25 and 161 days at FY25 start; operating cash flow Rs. 3,183M in Q4 vs Rs. 1,315M in Q3
items.quote: Our cash-to-cash cycle was 202 days in the current quarter, as compared to 213 days in Q3 FY '25 and 161 days at the beginning of the year.

items.statement: Net debt reduced to Rs. 7,061M in Q4 FY25 from Rs. 8,289M in Q3 FY25 and Rs. 8,421M at March 2024
items.quote: Our net debt was Rs. 7,061 million, as compared to Rs. 8,289 million in Q3 FY '25. Our net debt was Rs. 8,421 million at the end of March '24.

items.statement: FDA remediation costs ~Rs. 60 crores in FY25 (consultancy + air freight); will continue in Q1-Q2 FY26 but declining; air freight lower with better planning
items.quote: So, I will just quantify not only professional expenses, all kinds of expenses, including air freight and US FDA consultancy expenses, all have been close to Rs. 60 crores for FY '25.

items.statement: API/PFI revenue share <25% and declining as APIs consumed in-house for formulations; paracetamol API sales impacted by global overcapacity
items.quote: Yes, currently it is less than 25% and this is how the trend also we see going forward, as Chairman clarified in the earlier conversation. So we are producing API more for in -house consumption.

items.statement: R&D spend Rs. 238 crores in FY25 (+20% YoY); 127 total dossiers filed (85 US ANDAs, 16 pending; 18 Europe, 10 pending; 24 ROW, 8 pending); 3 US ANDAs and 6 EU dossiers filed in Q4
items.quote: Over the last financial year, Granules' R&D spend was Rs. 238 crores versus the Rs. 199 crores in FY '24 , representing a 20% increase in investment, which demonstrates our commitment towards R&D.

items.statement: ADHD portfolio: 10 products in pipeline including day-1 and day-181 launches, first-to-file opportunities; lisdexamfetamine API validation and DMF filing expected Q1 FY26 for vertical integration
items.quote: We have been developing a robust ADHD portfolio with about 10 products in the pipeline for development, which includes day one launches and day 181 launch opportunities, including some first to file.

items.statement: Oncology portfolio: ~10 products under development (NCE-1, first-to-file, day-181); first US/EU ANDA filed in Q4 FY25; revenue expected from FY28 onwards
items.quote: We continue to expand our oncology portfolio with around 10 products currently under development. This includes NC E-1 day one launches, first to files, and day 181 opportunities.

items.statement: US revenue ~79% of total in Q4/FY25; strategy to grow Europe (11 filings in FY25) and ROW absolutely but US remains biggest growth driver due to market size
items.quote: So we have been working on the North America strategy for almost 10, 12 years now in terms of filings, etc. So that market has been and will continue to be our biggest growth driver.

items.statement: US tariff risk: management communicating with customers that prices must increase if tariffs imposed; cannot absorb impact; believes level playing field as all generic players affected
items.quote: We are talking to all our customers in the US about the possible impact. And we have been mentioning that if duties, tariffs come in, we will have to increase prices, there is no way we can absorb it.

items.statement: FY25 capex Rs. 5,700M (Rs. 3,135M in GLS); CZRO project going slow with minimal spend in FY25; priority on GLS, oncology, peptide facilities
items.quote: CAPEX spend during the quarter was Rs. 1,598 million, and for the year was Rs. 5,700 million, primarily invested in Granules Life Sciences of Rs. 3,135 million in FY '25.

items.statement: Formulation sales grew 18% in FY25 despite Gagillapur production pause in September and H2 slowdown; API/PFI impacted by price erosion and demand issues
items.quote: Formulation sales grew by 18% despite a voluntary paused of production in September '24 at our Gagillapur facility, in response to US FDA observations and with remediation efforts, slowdown of production in H2.

items.statement: Europe sales decline driven by paracetamol API demand drop and price erosion; not expected to return to COVID-era levels; future growth from formulation launches
items.quote: Europe was mostly driven by paracetamol API with some of the big brands. And there was a slowdown there, it's only picking up, but I don't think it will go back to where it was.

items.statement: R&D productivity measured by quality filings (NCE-1, first-to-file) in ADHD/oncology; ROI benchmarks per ANDA type; management satisfied with progress and returns
items.quote: So R&D spend productivity is seen through one, the number of quality filings that we are doing both in US and Europe in ADHD and oncology segments. I think that is the first measurement that we see.

items.statement: Senn Chemicals acquisition provides immediate peptide CDMO capabilities (liquid/solid-phase synthesis) and GLP-1 development progress; medium-term focus on CDMO growth and GLP-1 for own portfolio and CDMO
items.quote: On the Senn acquisition, the medium -term, I think we will be focusing on A, improving the CDMO segment. So as already mentioned in the speeches that there are four areas where there is already enough customer base.

items.statement: Peptide R&D facility planned in Hyderabad followed by peptide manufacturing in India; large volume commercialization in India; developments in Switzerland; capex details to be clarified next quarter
items.quote: There is going to be a lot of CAPEX that has to come up in Switzerland. And also, we are putting up a peptide R&D facility in Hyderabad, and which will be followed by a peptide manufacturing also.

items.statement: Sustainability: EcoVadis Gold rating (top 5% pharma globally), CDP climate rating B, SBTi validation of climate goals, supplier sustainability program launched
items.quote: Granules received a gold rating from EcoVadis, placing us in the top 5% of the pharmaceutical companies globally in our very first corporate -level assessment.

items.statement: Group expects double-digit revenue growth excluding SCS and EBITDA margin of 12-14% for FY26
items.quote: We expect that the group will have double -digit revenue growth. This is even excluded even SCS, we still expect to have double-digit EBITDA I mean, double-digit revenue growth, and we expect EBITDA margin to be 12% to 14%.

items.statement: SCS business expected to turn EBITDA positive by Q4 FY26 with full year revenue around USD 40 million
items.quote: by Q4, we should be turning EBITDA positive. I think that is the target for SCS for the current year. The business of that SCS to be generally give an idea, will be around USD 40 million for the full year.

items.statement: Capex budget for FY26 is INR 160 crores
items.quote: I think the total capex budget for the current year is INR160 crores.

items.statement: Targeted price increase program underway; secured Rs 11-12 crore price increase effective July 1 and August 1 for integrated plant customers.

items.quote: No, no, no taxation. We are charging the making charge from here only. So we are paying tax here in India.

items.statement: Largest competitor 4-6x larger (2-3 tons/month); Sky Gold 50% more frugal (employee+other cost 1.5% of sales vs 2x for peers); PAT margins superior despite lower markup; turnaround 15-25 days vs 30-45 days for leader; growing 2-3x faster th
items.quote: Sky Gold is 50% more frugal compared to our competitors. Our employee cost and other expenditure add up only to 1.5% approx of sales, which our competitors operate at 2x higher cost. Our PAT margins are superior despite operating at a lower markup compared to the leaders.

items.statement: Unorganized-to-organized shift driving demand; Indian market Rs 5-6 lakh crore organized + Rs 9 lakh crore unorganized; lightweight and 18/14 carat gaining share due to high gold prices; export demand strong in GCC, Malaysia, Singapore
items.quote: We feel that Sky Gold is at an inflection point to gain market share from the large unorganized base and organized players in space. This is one of the primary reason why we went to expedite our plans to increasing our capacity from 1 ton per month to 4 tons per month.

items.statement: Gold sourced from Indian banks (with $4-5 premium) and Dubai subsidiary (at $10 discount); 3D printers (8-9) enabling weight reduction; ERP implementation for inventory, gold loss, receivables monitoring
items.quote: We will get the gold in Dubai and send it here for job work. And this will give a comfort to the customer. They are getting the same rate of gold as in Dubai. So this will scale our business.

Anchit mentioned about 50 stores being rolled out during the year, and that is getting reflected over here.

items.statement: Beauty physical retail same-store sales growth 15% in FY25 despite volatile market; stores break even within first year
items.quote: Same-store sales growth, I think this is the metric which we are very happy about, which is 15% same-store sales growth in what I think has been a volatile and slightly tepid market on the physical retail side for most of the country, but I think delivering very strong like-for-like growth shows that there is clear product market fit for Nykaa's retail network as well.

items.quote: So the operating cash flow now stands at INR467 crores. And what I would like to also point out is after lease payments as well as capex, there is still a significant amount of surplus cash. So this is a reflection of the strong cash flows that we have started to generate over time.

items.quote: We would like to update all of you that in May 2025, we received NCLT approval for both the schemes, which is a merger of LBB into Fashion. So I think it's been a sort of deliberate strategy to focus on Nykaa platforms and deemphasize third-party platforms for fashion specifically.

items.statement: Net working capital is close to one month; further improvements expected but not as steep as current year.
items.quote: Yes. So we are currently very close to a month in terms of net working capital. So I would say from here, yes, obviously, there would be more and more improvement opportunities, but unlikely to be as steep as what you have seen in the current year.

items.quote: So the likes of Victoria's Secret or a Rare Rabbit or a Hopscotch, always on online platforms, our experience has been that when we add strong brands, business tend to be incremental in nature. It doesn't cannibalize existing business because we are always able to unlock new use cases from sometimes the same customers as well as acquire new customers on the back of great brands.

items.statement: Beauty gross margins improving across all three sub-segments: eB2B meaningful scope, own brands healthier with room to improve, multi-brand retail benefiting from ad income growth and premiumization mix.
items.quote: So eB2B probably has meaningful scope to improve relative to where it is today. items.statement: Price-based competition in beauty comes and goes; some players use beauty to offset weakness in other categories; brand partners dislike discounting; no guarantee it won't return.
items.quote: It seems to be for now, but you never know. It can come up at any t ime. It's not the right way to do -- to build this category and our brand partners generally do not like it because it dilutes their

items.quote: Fashion business is not very asset heavy because -- yes, we are focusing on building more and more brands through marketplace than inventory-led. And the inventory-led business is mostly restricted to fashion own labels.

items.statement: Nykaa Now uses micro-fulfillment centers (dark stores), not physical stores; store hyperlocal capability exists but used mainly for luxury; stores are destination format in expensive real estate.
items.quote: Nykaa Now is being done in a more traditional rapid delivery quick commerce type model, which is to leverage the dark store concept or as we call it the micro fulfillment centers. items.statement: eB2B fulfillment cost, S&D cost decreasing and gross margin improving year on year.
items.quote: eB2B is continuing every year to bring its fulfillment cost down, its S&D cost down and improving its gross margin as well.

items.statement: eB2B requires a few more years of investment before profitability; long-term guidance given last year will be updated at Annual Day.

items.statement: Expects FY26 and FY27 EBITDA margins around Q4 FY25 level of 24.6%, plus or minus 0.5 percentage points

items.statement: Expects to sustain past 30% year-on-year revenue growth momentum for coming few financial years

items.statement: Commercial tower of ~45,000 sq ft at Grand Hyatt Mumbai in design stage, to enter development in coming months
items.quote: We are in the design stage for the development of a commercial tower in our Grand Hyatt property. The commercial tower size would be approximately 45,000 square feet. And this is slated to go into development process in the coming months.

items.statement: Forward bookings show ~12% growth potential for seasonally weak Q1-Q2 FY26 vs prior year
items.quote: But this year we see a huge, huge demand rise compared to last year for these slow months, and our books overall on all our hotels have shown a potential growth of almost 12%.

items.statement: April FY26 ARR grew 11%+ YoY in Mumbai and 10-11% YoY in Delhi on top of strong FY25 base
items.quote: In April, we have seen on top of and remember, this is on top of the strong growth in '25 that has happened all through. In April, we have seen 11% plus ARR growth in Mumbai and Delhi we have also seen for our asset between 10% to 11% ARR growth in April.

items.statement: May FY26 saw some impact from cross-border tensions in Delhi and Ahmedabad; June-July bookings strong, expect recovery by year-end
items.quote: May, of course, as everyone else has iterated, there is some impact, but we believe the business is strong. The pickup in Mumbai is very strong towards the end of May. Where has it been affected? I think Delhi and Ahmedabad are two locations which were close to the border and would probably have an impact. But I think the business is very strong in the month of June and July, as said by Mr. Saraf

items.statement: FY25 corporate EBITDA margin 38% (flat YoY); Q4 FY25 margin 44% driven by Grand Hyatt stabilization and strong ARR/occupancy
items.quote: We are at 38% while on the full year we are stable, or we are flat on the EBITDA. On the quarter-on-quarter basis, there is a sharp increase in the EBITDA margin, and we expect that this trend should hold in the current year.

items.statement: Grand Hyatt Mumbai ARR rose from ~Rs. 10,500 in Q1 FY25 to >Rs. 14,400 in Q4 FY25 (~37% increase) via product upgrade and mix shift to higher-paying transient guests
items.quote: Q1, FY ‘25, on average, let's say, blended Grand Hyatt ARR was in the vicinity of roughly around 10,500. Q4, we are surpassed 14,400 as an ARR. Now, it's a function of strength in the micro market and also the benefit of focusing more on transient and higher paying customers by offering a much more upgraded product and reducing our contribution on the traditional contract or the airline business.

items.statement: Grand Showroom (new ballroom) at Grand Hyatt Mumbai generated Rs. 9 crore in first six months; expected to contribute Rs. 25-28 crore in first full year of operations
items.quote: Another key highlight has been the F&B contribution where the Grand Showroom since operationalization has achieved a Rs. 9 crore revenue. And we anticipate in the current year, Grand Showroom itself to contribute roughly around Rs. 27 crores to Rs. 28 crores.

items.statement: MICE and F&B combined grew >15% YoY in FY25; Grand Hyatt Mumbai and Andaz Delhi Aerocity are leading MICE players in their markets
items.quote: I think year-on-year growth in F &B and MICE combined has been upwards of 15%. And this trend will continue. Grand Hyatt is a leading MICE player in the Mumbai market, and so is Andaz in the Delhi-Aerocity market.

items.statement: FY25 portfolio RevPAR grew 13.7% YoY in Q4; full-year ARR up 8% YoY (Delhi +19%, Mumbai +10%, Lucknow +11% in Q4); occupancy flat for year but rose in Q4 (Mumbai 82%, Delhi 84%, Ahmedabad 92%)
items.quote: On the key performance metrics, the highlight has been 8% growth in overall ARR. And the star performers here have been Delhi and Mumbai, where Delhi ARR Y-o-Y has grown 19% and Mumbai by 10%. And that trend has continued in Q4, where on top of a strong sequential growth, Delhi contributed 22% growth in ARR, Mumbai 10% Y-o-Y in Q4. And Lucknow has been also a strong performer on ARR, which saw 11%

items.statement: Kaziranga ALILA expected opening ARR range Rs. 12,000-15,000
items.quote: It would range from Rs. 12,000 to Rs. 15,000 starting..

items.statement: Net bank debt/EBITDA at 1.4x (gross bank debt Rs. 776 crore, cash & deposits Rs. 246 crore including Rs. 155 crore residual GCP); average borrowing cost ~9%
items.quote: So, what we refer to, as I said and I repeat, is net bank debt-to-EBITDA. So, if you look at the balance sheet, we have Rs. 776 crores of gross bank debt, which is the consolidated bank debt on the books today. The other borrowings are primarily promoter ECBs, which you see on the balance sheet, right? So, when we talk about the borrowing power in the headroom, we are talking about net bank debt-t

items.statement: Internal peak net debt/EBITDA ceiling set at 3.5-3.7x for growth funding
items.quote: We would never want to kind of go beyond a peak EBITDA on a consistent basis beyond a certain number that we have set internally. So, without breaching any of these internal targets, we would have sufficient headroom for growth to fund the expansion plan.

items.statement: Acquired 6.5-acre semi-built 220-room hotel near Bengaluru Airport (to become 245 keys) at Rs. 350 crore; acquired 10-acre land in Kaziranga for 115-key ALILA resort
items.quote: We acquired a partially constructed 220-room hotel on land measuring 6.5 acres near Bangalore Airport. Let me repeat. We acquired a 6.5-acre land with a semi-built 220 room hotel near Bangalore Airport. This was a tremendous achievement, and I feel very, very happy that we were able to acquire this asset at a very competitive and reasonable price.

items.statement: ROFO on two Saraf family-owned hotels (737 keys) underway via cashless share swap; advisors and valuers appointed
items.quote: We also have received ROFO of two Saraf family-owned hotels. Advisors and valuers have been appointed, and the acquisition process is underway pending necessary approvals. I shall keep you updated.

items.statement: In advanced discussions for two strategic assets to add 500 keys; will update when deals signed
items.quote: Juniper is currently actively negotiating two attractive opportunities in strategic locations to add 500 keys to our portfolio. We shall update you as soon as the deals are signed.

items.statement: Grand Hyatt Mumbai renovation complete (new ballroom, restaurant Cellini, bar, refurbished rooms/apartments); all revenue streams active
items.quote: Renovation is now complete, including the showroom, that's the new ballroom, a new restaurant, Cellini, the bar, refurbished rooms and apartments. The whole hotel is fully operational with all revenue streams active and generating income.

items.statement: Ahmedabad and Hampi hotels refurbished in FY25 with enhanced F&B and new banqueting venues
items.quote: We also completed the refurbishment of our hotels in Ahmedabad and Hampi during the last fiscal year and enhanced our food and beverage spaces and added new banqueting venues to the hotel.

items.statement: Grand Hyatt Mumbai shifted mix toward higher-paying transient guests, reducing airline/contract business
items.quote: Now, it's a function of strength in the micro market and also the benefit of focusing more on transient and higher paying customers by offering a much more upgraded product and reducing our contribution on the traditional contract or the airline business.

items.statement: Fairmont opening in Mumbai micro-market not hurting Grand Hyatt; April occupancy up 9 pp YoY; new luxury supply expected to push ARRs higher for existing players
items.quote: In April, Grand Hyatt saw 9% point increase Y-o-Y on occupancy. So, you know, we are not witnessing any impact from the opening of Fairmont. In fact, the Fairmount opening will only help ARR improvements across the micro comset. We have shared, given any new asset coming in at that segment in which we are operating, will only push up the ARRs and help the existing players.

items.statement: Employee cost at 16-17% of revenue in Q4; reverting to normative level but not back to prior 13% due to senior hires for upgraded product
items.quote: We do see while we may not go back to the same levels as the previous year on the employee cost, but we are now reverting to a normative level. So, in the previous quarters, there were some one-off charges or there were increase in manpower cost on a quarter-on-quarter basis. But we are now reverting back to a normative level of manpower cost. And yes, but we may not go back to the last year level

items.statement: One-time renovation/employee costs of Rs. 33 crore in FY25 (non-recurring); Bengaluru Phase-1 fire incident isolated, no impact on FY26 opening timeline
items.quote: So the total one time which includes broadly the R&M and also you know the manpower or the employee cost and incentives which were expended through the year is roughly for full year FY ‘25 roughly around Rs. 33 crores.

items.statement: Andaz Delhi Aerocity occupancy ~80% in FY25
items.quote: So, last full year, the occupancy level at Andaz is roughly 80%.

items.statement: Board approved divestment of Kuttukaran Green (Piaggio) and Vision Motors (Honda) for total Rs 70 crore, expected completion by July; proceeds to fund network expansion outside Kerala
items.quote: I am pleased to share that the Board of Directors has approved the divestment of both these entities for total consideration of Rs. 70 crores. We anticipate the transaction will be completed by July.

items.statement: Long-term growth guidance of 15% year-on-year remains unchanged despite FY25 challenges
items.quote: That on a long-term basis continues to be the same. As we said earlier, this year was a flip. And there is no change as far as the long-term strategy of the organization in terms of growth as well as the growth strategies continues to be the same.

items.statement: Capex plan of Rs 30 crore for FY26 excluding potential acquisitions
items.quote: CAPEX we are planning is about Rs. 30 crores for the next financial year. This excludes any acquisition that we are already in discussions with.

items.statement: Ather EV expansion into Maharashtra with 4 outlets (2 Nagpur, 1 Chandrapur, 1 Chhatrapati Sambhaji Nagar) operational by Q2 FY26; JLR 3S facility in Hingna Nagpur operational by H2 FY26; Maruti 3S facility in Avalahalli Bangalore launched w
items.quote: With Ather, we have entered a new state, Maharashtra, marking a significant step forward in our EV strategy. Each upcoming facility will include an experience center, a service center, and a warehouse. Two outlets will be set up in Nagpur, with one each in Chandrapur and Chhatrapati Sambhaji Nagar, formerly Aurangabad. Operations at these locations are expected to commence in Q2 FY '26.

items.statement: FY25 EBITDA margin 3.2% vs 5.1% in FY24; Q4 FY25 EBITDA margin 2.2%; target to return to 5.1% EBITDA margin in FY26 despite new outlet costs
items.quote: We would want to get back to the EBITDA margins of 5.1% which we have clocked in FY '24. That is our aim irrespective of the cost of JLR, Nagpur new setup that is coming up or any other, the Karnataka setup which we have started in Arena. We nevertheless would like to get back to the 5.1% of FY '24.

items.statement: Discounts in April-May FY26 nearly half of FY25 average; FY25 full-year average discounts: Arena ~Rs 9.5k, NEXA ~Rs 12k; Q4 FY25 peaks: Arena ~Rs 13-14k, NEXA ~Rs 17-18k; April FY26: Arena ~Rs 5.5k, NEXA ~Rs 7.5k
items.quote: However, when you look at April and May, April for ARENA was about 5.5K and May was about, okay, May is still not completed. April was 5.5K for Arena and NEXA was around 7.5K, which is what I mentioned earlier also that we have been able to bring it down by 50%. And we expect to hold it through the year.

items.statement: FY25 working capital 46 days (inventory days 45); March 2025 inventory levels brought back to March 2024 levels; target Arena inventory ~35 days, NEXA ~41-42 days by June then lower
items.quote: So, ARENA we are looking at closer to about 35 days through the year in terms of inventory. And NEXA, say, by June, we should be bringing it down to about 41 -42 days, and a lower number over the next three quarters.

items.statement: Debt-to-equity 0.7x, net debt-to-equity 0.6x, net debt-to-EBITDA 2.2x; internal target debt-to-equity 1:1 giving ~Rs 200 crore leverage headroom; divestment proceeds may fund acquisitions
items.quote: Internally we have a target that normally would like to keep our debt equity as 1 as to 1. As we speak in March, we ended up with, I think, 0.67 debt. So, we have enough leverage of around Rs. 200 crores, if at all, to make it to 1 as to 1.

items.statement: Service-to-sales volume ratio stable at 28x; service revenue target 14% of total revenue; service revenue growth guidance 20-25% over next couple of years
items.quote: Yes, service to sales ratio continues to be at 28 and will remain there. But however, what we are looking at is to improve the productivity of serv ice and the labor per car that we generate. And with those initiatives we will be improving profitability. But the ratio per se, I think, would more or less remain the same, plus or minus a few points

items.statement: NEXA contribution increased to 40% from 35-36% in FY24; NEXA grew 15-16% in FY25 while Arena de-grew ~10%; EV revenue grew 2.4% to Rs 87 crore; JLR sales margin ~6%, service margin ~18%
items.quote: Contribution of NEXA has gone up to 40% as of now compared to say 35%-36% in the last year. So, in Kerala, NEXA has been growing at a much higher pace than the national average.

items.statement: Market share: Kerala Arena ~24%, NEXA 21-22%; Tamil Nadu Arena 11.5-12%, NEXA ~21%; Kerala service market share 31-32%, body shop 35-36%
items.quote: So, in terms of Arena market share, we should be ending the year closer to about 24%. And then NEXA, it should be somewhere between 21% to 22% in Kerala. In Tamil Nadu, in ARENA, we should be closer to between 11.5 % to 12% and NEXA should be about 21%. Service, we have a market share in Kerala around 31 %-32% in terms of the service market share. But in terms of body shop, we are at about 35%-36%

items.statement: New vehicle sales FY25: 44,087 units (-5.5% YoY); Pre-owned: 10,600 units (-0.6%); Service volumes: 10.42 lakh (-1.1%); Q4 FY25 new vehicles: 10,370 (-6.7% YoY)
items.quote: Coming to the full year FY '25's performance, the new vehicle sales clocked about 44,087 units versus 46,665 last year, which shows a degrowth of 5.5%.

items.quote: We have also taken a one-time manpower correction measure, which is expected to deliver an annualized benefit of around Rs. 7 crores in FY '26.
