items.quote: Having said that, the Range Rover, the Range Rover Sport , Discovery Sport, Range Rover Evoque, all are being manufactured in India, locally manufactured. So , not much of a change there. People were most probably speculating on the Defender. But unfortunately, right now the Defender is made in Slovakia, not in UK. So , any FTA agreement with UK actually does not Popular Vehicles and have any effe

items.statement: CV segment mixed: passenger segment strong, construction green shoots, cargo steady, SCV negative growth expected; small commercial segment drop due to financing challenges for first-time users
items.quote: The small commercial segment has seen a drop per se in terms of numbers. So , that we are not too sure going forward given both in terms of finances for first-time users, etc. being still a little subdued. SCV, we don't see growth at all. We probably see a negative number on a SCV even this year.

items.statement: Accenture hired for transformation deep dive focusing on sales manpower productivity; one-time manpower correction implemented; 10,000 employee strength supports service referral network
items.quote: We also got a third-party perspective by hiring Accenture to conduct a deep dive into our ongoing transformation journey. One of the key focus areas was sales manpower productivity, targeting an increase of additional car per salesperson per month.

items.statement: CRISIL reaffirmed long-term rating CRISIL A/Stable and short-term CRISIL A1 on Rs 468 crore bank loan facilities
items.quote: Credit rating: CRISIL ratings has reaffirmed the rating awarded to the company as the long-term rating of CRIS IL-A / stable and short -term rating of CRISL -A1 on the outstanding loan of around Rs. 468 crores bank loan facilities of the company

items.statement: Divestment proceeds of Rs 70 crore plus other resources to fund core business growth and network expansion outside Kerala; acquisition discussions ongoing targeting Q1/Q2 FY26 closure
items.quote: The proceeds from the divestment, along with other resources previously committed to these subsidiaries, will be redirected to accelerate the growth of our core business. This move reinforces our commitment to focusing on key growth drivers and creating long-term value.

items.statement: State-wise revenue FY25: Kerala 62%, Tamil Nadu 23%, Karnataka 10%, Maharashtra 5%; target to reduce Kerala contribution below 50%
items.quote: State-wise revenue as of 31st March , 2025 : Kerala contributed to 62%, Tamil Nadu 23%, Karnataka 10%, and Maharashtra 5%.

items.statement: FY26 revenue guidance of INR 1,300 crores with EBITDA margin of 19-20%, subject to biomass tariff impact
items.quote: As mentioned during our last earnings call, we are on track to achieve a top line revenue of around INR1,300 crores in FY '26, reflecting over 50% growth compared to the FY '25 base. While we are confident of delivering an EBITDA margin in the range of 19% to 20%, the recent downward revision in tariff for our biomass power plant may impact profitability an d margins at the same is not reversed or

items.statement: INR 100 crores capex in FY26 for Anjar expansion and seamless pipe plant; maintenance capex INR 10-15 crores annually
items.quote: So as far as the new capex is concerned, we are already undergoing expansion of our new Anjar facility, of which we shall be doing another INR 100 crores of capex in FY '25, '26. And as far as our maintenance capex is concerned, that shall be always in the range of INR 10 crores to INR15 crores on overall group level.

items.statement: Order book of INR 1,275 crores as of April 30, 2025; piping segment order book INR 1,000-1,100 crores for FY26
items.quote: As of April 30, 2025, our order book stood at INR 1,275 crores, offering strong visibility going forward.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 operating EBITDA margin 22.2%, up 797 bps YoY; FY25 margin 15%, up 196 bps YoY
items.quote: Correspondingly, our operating EBITDA margin expanded by 797 basis points year-on-year and 1,868 basis points quarter -on-quarter to 22.2%. For the full year, operating EBITDA stood at INR123 crores, up 20.7% year-on-year with a margin expansion of 196 basis points to 15%.

items.statement: Oil & gas 73% of order book, power 20%; FY26 piping revenue INR 1,000-1,100 crores from India plus Thailand subsidiary
items.quote: And coming to the breakup of the oil and gas and power, we still have good orders from oil and gas. It's around 73% of the total value, what we have as of today. And from power, we have around 20%.

items.statement: Anjar facility adding 15,000 MTPA capacity by October 2025; seamless pipe plant commercial production by January 2026
items.quote: We expect to commission an additional 15,000 metric ton per annum capacity by October 2025, bringing the total capacity at Anjar, excluding heavy fabrication to 30,000 metric tons per annum. Simultaneously, the development of our high-wall seamless pipe plant is advancing on schedule. We remain on track to commence commercial production by January 2026.

items.statement: PSERC reduced biomass tariffs: Muktsar from INR 8.59 to 3.50/unit, Abohar from 7.47 to 5.42/unit; annual revenue impact INR 260M + 125M; review petition filed
items.quote: The tariff for the Muktsar plant was reduced from INR 8.59 per unit to INR 3.50 per unit, while the tariff for the Abohar plant was revised from INR7.47 per unit to INR5.42 per unit. Going forward, the annual revenue impact due to revised tariffs related to expected to be approximately INR260 million for the Muktsar plant and INR 125 million for Abohar.

items.statement: Strong pipeline from power sector (BHEL planning 10 boilers/year, 5 outsourced); ExxonMobil rate contract for 18 months expecting INR 40-50 crores in FY26
items.quote: So we got the rate contract from ExxonMobil USA. So that will be like for their various projects which they are executing it. So this recent one is for like 18 months, they have signed the rate contract, and we are expecting around INR 40 crores, INR 50 crores business in this financial year from them.

items.statement: Dow Chemical order ~$50M (75-80% execution in FY26); Linde kits orders; BHEL fittings orders INR 60-70 crores
items.quote: Sir, we have this Dow chemical order, which will be executed in this year. Apart of the Dow, we have a lot of order from this Linde now, Linde for the kits. Then fittings BHEL orders are there for the pipe fittings as on date. So these orders will be executed.

items.statement: Order booking target INR 1,600-1,700 crores in FY26; minimum order book INR 1,000 crores at any time
items.quote: The worst scenario, what I consider the hit rate will be around like INR 1,600 crores to INR 1,700 crores, w e should be booking the orders

items.statement: Logistics cost savings from Anjar facility (50% raw material imported, 50% revenue exported) to drive margin improvement
items.quote: Yes, definitely. And going forward, since 50% of our raw material we used to import and 50% of our overall revenue, we are exporting. Therefore, since the volumes of oil and gas sector jobs are quite higher, therefore, the logistics cost in -- particularly in oil and gas sector is a major cost factor, which decides the EBITDA margin. So we are going to save a lot of expenses on account of logistic

items.statement: Power sector execution cycle <1 year (9-11 months); oil & gas 6-18 months; FY26 revenue skewed to oil & gas, later years may level to 50-60% power
items.quote: Sir, in power sector, we shall not be getting more than 9 months' time. Maybe maximum 10, 11 months, but less than a year in any case.

items.statement: No US tariff impact currently; cost competitiveness protects against potential future tariffs
items.quote: No, there's absolutely no impact, sir, as of now. And even if it tomorrow comes, since our costing is much more competitive and it's going to be with all the countries. So I don't think we should have any impact on that.

items.statement: Q1 historically weak due to holidays; expect substantially better Q1 FY26 than previous years
items.quote: Sir, historically, April is the slowest month because people go on holidays and all those things. But in general also, we have a very poor quarter 1, but then subsequent quarters keep on ramping up and the quarter 4 is always the best. And the same thing is going to happen in this year also. But we shall be doing substantially much better Q1 than any other previous year, I can only tell you that.

items.statement: CWIP of INR 150 crores to be capitalized in FY26 plus INR 100 crores new capex; gross block to increase from ~INR 650 crores
items.quote: So just for clarity, sir, the CWIP as of now stands at almost INR 150 crores. That will get capitalized next year fully plus INR200 crores. So INR250 crores will get added to roughly INR650-odd crores of gross book? Sameer Agarwal : Yes. You are correct

items.statement: Q4 FY25 EBITDA margin of 18.1% cited as reference point; no formal forecast given
items.quote: What I can tell you is that our margins in Q4 were significantly better than what they were for the whole year. So, if you look at that as a guidance, I think that could be a good number to begin with.

items.statement: Global insoluble sulphur demand expected to grow 2-3% near term
items.quote: The global market is expected to grow at about 2%-3% over the near term.

items.statement: India insoluble sulphur demand expected at 22,000-23,000 tons for current year
items.quote: As far as India is concerned, I can say that the demand in India is about 22,000-23,000 tons. More about 23,000 tons is what we expect to be the demand this year.

items.statement: Indian demand estimated at 8-9% of global demand
items.quote: I believe the Indian demand could be about 8%-9% of the global demand. 8% or thereabout.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 EBITDA margin 18.1% vs 16.6% in Q3 FY25
items.quote: EBITDA margins stood at 18.1% which was 16.6% during Q3 FY25.

items.statement: FY25 (9 months) EBITDA margin 17.9%
items.quote: EBITDA margins were 17.9%.

items.statement: Freight cost reduction from 9% (FY25 avg) to 7.2% (Q4) improved margins
items.quote: In the last quarter they came down from 9% for the year to 7.2% for the quarter ended March '25.

items.statement: Anti-dumping duty recommended: $307/ton on China imports, $257/ton on Japan imports
items.quote: What DGTR has recommended to the Finance Ministry is $307 of anti-dumping duty on imports from China and $257 of anti-dumping duty for imports from Japan.

items.statement: Chinese import price into India around INR95/kg
items.quote: Currently, if you look at the average price of import from China, that will be somewhere around INR95 is the average import price of insoluble sulphur from China.

items.statement: Coating oil prices stable
items.quote: More or less they are stable.

items.statement: Maintenance capex only, typically INR10-13 crores per year
items.quote: Usually, it is in the range of INR10 crores to INR12-INR13 crores.

items.statement: Capacity utilization around 70% in FY25; can go up to 100%
items.quote: So, the capacity utilization this year has been around 70%.

items.statement: China not a direct player in US or Europe; predominantly in Southeast Asia
items.quote: China today is predominantly present in Southeast Asia. China and Southeast Asia. Gautam Rajesh: Understood. Akshat Goenka: Today, they are not a direct player in the West

items.statement: Domestic market share 55-58%; no significant reduction expected even without anti-dumping duty
items.quote: Currently, our market share is already down to around 55%-58% in the domestic market. I do not see any significant reduction in domestic market share even if the duty is not imposed.

items.statement: Competitors (two in China, one in Japan, Flexsys) all have strong balance sheets
items.quote: All our competitors have strong balance sheets. Of the significant competitors, there are two in China, one in Japan, and one is multinational by the name of Flexis. All have strong balance sheets.

items.statement: Anti-dumping duty recommendation cleared by DGTR, under Finance Ministry consideration; hopeful for June notification
items.quote: The recommendation for imposition of anti- dumping duty on imports of insoluble sulphur from China and Japan is un der consideration of the Finance Ministry. It has already been cleared by the DGTR and we are hopeful of the imposition of this anti-dumping duty happening in the month of June

items.statement: No hedging of sulphur or oil prices; limited debt restricts stock build-up
items.quote: No, it is not possible to hedge sulphur prices or oil prices. The only way we can do it is to increase stock. But then there is a limited debt. So, there is no way to hedge prices.

items.statement: Debt to equity at comfortable 0.14x for FY25
items.quote: Debt to equity for the year stood at a comfortable 0.14x.

items.statement: Full-year (including Q1 in OCC) revenue INR413 crores, EBITDA INR74-75 crores
items.quote: full -year turnover was including the chemical business turnover for the first quarter, which was in Oriental Carbon and Chemicals Limited, the total revenue was INR413 crores. Garvita: INR413 crores. With EBITDA margin of? Anurag Jain: It could be around INR74 crores-INR75 crores

items.statement: Volumes flat year-on-year with insignificant growth
items.quote: For the current year, the volumes have not grown significantly. There has been insignificant growth over the last year.

items.statement: Demerger implementation charge of INR3.5 crores in Q4 FY25; normalized EBITDA margin would be ~3% higher
items.quote: That is right. These are majorly stamp duty charges that we paid during the quarter. And if that was not there, then our other expenses would be less to that extent.

items.statement: Dividend payout ~35% of last three quarters earnings; policy considers cash flows, working capital, capex
items.quote: So obviously, our stated policy does consider the fact that we have to look at the net cash flows, the actual cash flows, including anticipated increase in working capital requirements, capexes, and if we need to shore up funds for other requirements and then give out the dividend.

items.statement: Focus on customized grades for global tire manufacturers and sustainability
items.quote: Going forward, we will continue to focus on product innovation by offering customized grades that meet stringent technical specifications of global tire manufacturers We will drive sustainability by enhancing production efficiency and reducing our carbon footprint.

items.statement: Cost optimization achieved in raw material and fixed costs
items.quote: We have again been successful in doing a bunch of cost optimization in both raw material as well as fixed costs.

items.statement: US tariff war no direct or indirect impact on OCCL business with America
items.quote: We do not see any impact. In fact, we have been in talks with our customers and currently we do not see any impact of tariff on our business with America.

items.statement: Revenue target for FY26 is INR 700-850 crores
items.quote: The band is between INR 700 and INR 850 crores is our target band on the revenue.

items.statement: Blended margin target is 17-18% with aspiration to reach 20%
items.quote: We believe the blended would still be upwards of 16%, 17%. We would ideally like to target 20%.

items.statement: Peak consolidated revenue capacity post expansion is INR 2,000 crores
items.quote: I agree, sir. That would be our peak capacity at what we are right now.

items.statement: Consolidated order backlog stands at almost INR 750 crores
items.quote: Our strong consolidated order backlog at this quarter stands almost close to INR 750 crores.

items.statement: Quality Power bid pipeline exceeds INR 1,000 crores; Mehru bid pipeline exceeds INR 400 crores
items.quote: The bid pipeline for Quality Power as on last month is excess of INR 1,000 crores. And for Mehru is excess of INR 400 crores.

items.statement: Mehru order book surged beyond INR 350 crores in recent months
items.quote: The order book at Mehru has surged beyond INR 350 crores in the last few months.

items.statement: Sangli facility capacity to increase nearly 9-fold within 18 months; IGBC Gold/Platinum certification targeted
items.quote: Overall, our production capacity in Sangli will increase nearly 9-fold within the next 18 months.

items.statement: Mehru capex on track for 45% capacity addition in 4-5 months
items.quote: At Mehru, the planned capex is on track and expected to deliver shortly about 45% additional capacity in the next 4-5 months.

items.statement: Cochin factory adding capacity for medium voltage markets; HVDC/FACTS capacity online by H2 next year
items.quote: We are adding additional capacity in our Cochin factory that will be able to cater to the medium voltage markets. But for the HVDC and FACTS, we will be taking orders from about 6 months' time because the factory will be online by second half of next year.

items.statement: Quality Power peak revenue capacity from current factory block is INR 1,500 crores; Mehru peak is INR 450-500 crores
items.quote: Post the current expansion, what we have as Quality Power in the factory block, we believe we have facility to deliver almost close to INR 1,500 crores from the current factory. Mehru, we are anticipating we should peak out at about INR 450 to INR 500 crores.

items.statement: Coil product margins roughly north of 20-22% or higher
items.quote: Roughly north of 20%-22%, sir, or higher.

items.statement: Endoks (Turkey) margins historically 20-25%, currently 20-22% due to inflation
items.quote: They have been traditionally around 25% plus, but this year we are looking at about 20% to 22% primarily because of inflation-related costs at that market.

items.statement: HVDC/FACTS market growth expected 40-50%; HVDC order surge expected by Q3 FY26
items.quote: We would see a surge in the numbers by, I would say, third quarter this year.

items.statement: Global supply shortages in high voltage equipment (220kV+) with European factories booked 6-7 years out
items.quote: Most of the European factories, on an average, are closed for 6 to 7 years. And Europe is normally the hub for all high voltage electrical equipments.

items.statement: Onboarded new customers/utilities from Sweden, Finland, Iraq, Romania, Italy, Brazil, South Korea, Hong Kong, Australia, Middle East
items.quote: We have successfully onboarded notable new customers and utilities from Sweden, Finland, Iraq, Romania, Italy, Brazil, South Korea, Hong Kong, Australia, and across the Middle East.

items.statement: Long-term contracts signed: 3-year with Fingrid (Finland), 4-year with Israeli utility
items.quote: We have announced two long-term contracts, one with Fingrid, that is Finland utility, which signed a 3-year contract with us. Recently, again, a global utility from Israel signed a 4-year contract with us.

items.statement: Power quality solutions ~40-45% of revenue; coil products ~INR 160 crores; transformers miniscule
items.quote: Our power quality is at this moment about 40%-45% of our total revenue.

items.statement: HVDC qualified products: reactors, line traps, instrument transformers, medium-voltage oil-filled transformers
items.quote: We have also qualified for line traps. We have qualified for instrument transformers. We have qualified for medium -voltage oil -filled transformers for special applications, like zigzag - connected earthing transformers

items.statement: Revenue geography shifts yearly: US was largest, then Europe, now Middle East/Australia, India may be largest next year
items.quote: A couple of years back, America was our biggest market. Last year, Europe was our biggest market. This year, I believe, Middle East and Australia is our biggest market. Maybe next year, we are looking at India being our biggest market.

items.statement: Turkey exposure minimal: <INR 8 crores offers from Turkish sub to India, <INR 5 crores from India to Turkey
items.quote: We have less than INR 8 crores of spending offers from our Turkish subsidiary to Indian customers, and less than INR 5 crores from Indian companies to our Turkish customers.

items.statement: Net debt down 77% in FY25; cash and bank balances ~INR 210 crores
items.quote: net debt has come down by 77 % putting us in a significantly stronger position to pursue growth without compromising financial discipline. Our cash and bank balances now stand at nearly INR 210 crores

items.statement: Promoters extended INR 125 crore soft credit line at concessional rate
items.quote: The promoters have extended an INR 125 crore soft credit line at a concessional rate.

items.statement: Working capital increased due to high Q4 sales (higher debtors) and Mehru acquisition consolidation
items.quote: our working capital increased because of the high sale in the last quarter and which also resulted into the increase in d ebtors. It also, due to the acquisitions of new Mehru Electrical

items.statement: Promoters waived dividends of ~INR 5 crores to conserve capital for investment cycle
items.quote: We have consciously and transparently decided to waive off our dividends, amounting to approximately INR 5 crores to conserve vital capital during this crucial investment cycle.

items.statement: HVDC project timeline: 3 years for Quality Power, 4 years for end customer; order cycle 2-3 years for HVDC, 12-15 months for FACTS
items.quote: HVDC order is normally about 2 to 3 years where you bill every month. A FACTS order is about 12 to 15 months.

items.statement: Turkey geopolitical risk monitored by Risk Committee; operations stable, minimal local competition, global project execution
items.quote: Our Risk Committee has continuous diligent oversight to manage and mitigate any related concerns, if any.

items.statement: Targets US$108 billion gross revenue by 2030 with 40% ROCE
items.quote: The number of all the groups and everything put together, we are targeting for 2030 will be US$108 billion on the top line. And of course, the ROCE remains same at 40%.

items.statement: Capex guidance for FY26 is INR 6,000 crores plus or minus 10%
items.quote: Looking at all these new developments, our capex guidance for the next year and including for our existing business is about INR 6,000 crores plus or minus 10%.

items.statement: 50% of FY26 capex is regular and 50% growth-oriented, majority towards non-automotive
items.quote: 50% of this is regular capex and 50% is purely growth-oriented. Majority of the growth business is towards the non-automotive piece.

items.statement: Large business order book of approximately US$88 billion
items.quote: Finally, there is no better proof of the stability and strength of the diversified business model than a large book business order of approximately US$88 billion.

items.statement: Non-auto order book of US$2.7 billion includes US$1.3 billion from aerospace
items.quote: you've given $2.7 billion of non-auto order book. And then in other slides, we've given $1.3 billion is coming from aerospace.

items.statement: Modules and polymer business faced cost pressures in Q4 due to launch issues and European production decline
items.quote: Definitely, that was a place where we had the maximum pressure because of course, the customer mix over there is still figuring out that their program launches.

items.statement: European transformative plan targets EUR 50 million cost optimization over next couple of years
items.quote: We have already announced a series of transformative measures in Western and Central Europe to breathe with the market, enabling a cost block optimization of approximately EUR 50 million, which we hope to be realized over the next couple of years.

items.statement: Consumer electronics capacity on track to reach 15-17 million units by end of FY26
items.quote: Consumer electronics is having a very rapid ramp-up and is on track to reach a capacity of 15 to 17 million units by the end of FY '26.

items.statement: INR 900-1,000 crores spent on consumer electronics capex in FY25 out of INR 2,600 crores commitment
items.quote: I think we have done around about INR 900 crores to INR 1,000 crores out of the INR 2,600 crores.

items.statement: Majority of remaining consumer electronics capex to be spent in FY26 for large greenfield starting mid-FY27
items.quote: Going by that, a majority of it should get spent in this year if we are going to be ready for that facility in mid of next year. So I would imagine most would get spent.

items.statement: Aerospace business grew 5x in a year, now Tier 1 supplier to Airbus across portfolio
items.quote: In the aerospace business, which we started in this 5-year journey, has already grown 5x in a year. And today, we're proud to say it's a Tier 1 supplier to Airbus across its portfolio.

items.statement: Vision Systems achieved lifetime sales of over US$400 million in camera monitoring systems for CV segment
items.quote: The Vision Systems vertical has made strong inroads into camera monitoring systems in the CV segment with lifetime sales of over US$400 million.

items.statement: Achieved 3CX10 customer diversification target
items.quote: On the customer front, I'm happy to announce that we've already achieved 3CX10.

items.statement: More than 50% of FY25 revenues from emerging markets
items.quote: More than 50% of our revenues in FY '25 came from emerging markets.

items.statement: Yachiyo now cross-selling beyond Honda, targeting German and American carmakers
items.quote: Now they have already broken ground with new ones. Next step is to bring in the German carmakers and American carmakers as well into the fold.

items.statement: Working capital expanded by approximately INR 2,000 crores in March 2025 due to pre-buying and safety stock buildup
items.quote: Our working capital as of March 2025 has expanded by approximately INR 2,000 crores, and there is an opportunity to reduce it in ensuing quarters.

items.statement: Net debt-to-EBITDA at 0.9x, lowest in 5-year period
items.quote: While delivering an all-round growth and expansion, we remain focused on free cash flow and are able to bring the leverage ratio to the lowest level at 0.9 net debt-to-EBITDA in the 5-year period.

items.statement: Board approved in-principle debt raising of INR 8,500 crores on estimated basis
items.quote: It's an in-principle approval that has been sought from the Board. And obviously, when we do raise it, you will hear about all the details, including the use of proceeds and so on.

items.statement: Board recommended bonus issue in ratio of 1:2 (one bonus share for every two held)
items.quote: To commemorate this special occasion, the board has recommended a bonus issue in the ratio of 1:2. That is, one bonus equity share for every two equity shares held.

items.statement: Majority of US sales USMCA compliant; constructive discussions with customers on tariff pass-through, no material financial impact expected
items.quote: we follow a global-local strategy and hence, majority of our U.S. sales is USMCA compliant. For the remaining portion of the sales, we are in constructive discussions with our customers regarding the pass-through of tariff-related charges and do not seeing material financial impact.

items.statement: Acquisition strategy requires customer standing behind the acquisition; 47 acquisitions all doing well
items.quote: But I have always been guiding my people that you have to make sure that a customer is standing behind asking for that particular acquisition.

items.statement: FY25 revenue grew 15% YoY to INR 113,600 crores; EBITDA up 17% to INR 10,877 crores; PAT concerned share up 40% to INR 3,803 crores
items.quote: Motherson has delivered its best-ever performance to date, reporting full-year revenues of approximately INR 113,600 crores, an increase of 15% year-on-year. EBITDA rose by 17% to INR 10,877 crores, while profit after tax, our concerned share is up 40% to INR 3,803 crores compared to FY '24.

items.statement: 5-year CAGR: revenue 19%, EBITDA 21%, PAT concerned share 68%
items.quote: In this period, we have grown revenues at about 19% CAGR, EBITDA at 21% CAGR and PAT concerned share at 68% CAGR.

items.statement: Global light vehicle production declined ~1% to 89.7 million units in FY25; emerging markets showed resilience
items.quote: global light vehicle production declined by about 1%, reaching around 89.7 million units. This softness was most apparent in the developed markets, while emerging markets such as India and China demonstrated resilience and registered low single-digit growth.

items.statement: Signs of softening production volumes in current year due to trade uncertainties and platform mix changes
items.quote: As we ride through the current financial year, there are signs of softening of production volumes, driven mainly by uncertainties created by evolving trade dynamics and evolving platform mix.

items.statement: Consumer electronics JV eligible for PLI and state-level SPAC incentives for electronic manufacturing
items.quote: Yes. We are eligible for that, including some of the SPAC-related, which are special -- especially created by the local government, the state government for the electronic manufacturing piece.

items.statement: Trade policy uncertainties creating pre-buying, safety stock buildup, and working capital expansion
items.quote: The uncertainties around trade dynamics led to pre-buying and buildup of safety stock in March 2025. This implied higher receivables and inventories, and consequently higher working capital.

items.statement: Capex guidance of INR7,500 crores for FY26
items.quote: We have decided INR7,500 crores capex for '25-'26.

items.statement: Capex to increase from FY27 onwards with major chunks from FY27
items.quote: And as we go ahead, once the packages are tendered out and the activity starts, then the chunk of investments will come from the next year. I mean, some chunk will come in '25-'26. From '26-'27 onwards, major chunks will start coming in terms of capex.

items.statement: Peak capex expected around FY28-29, potentially INR10,000-15,000 crores higher than current INR7,500 crores
items.quote: If it is INR7,500 crores today, so it may increase by around INR10,000 crores, INR15,000 crores, something like that.

items.statement: Target to increase capacity from 20 MT to 35 MT by 2030 via brownfield and greenfield projects
items.quote: Right now, we are at around 20 million tons of capacity, and we want to go towards 35 million tons of capacity by 2030.

items.statement: Debottlenecking to add 2-3 MT by 2028; ISP brownfield 0.5 MT by FY27-28, full 7 MT by 2029
items.quote: by 2028, we are expecting to increase it by maybe around 2 million to 3 million tons, something like that, around 3 million tons, something like that by then because debottlenecking projects will come quickly.

items.statement: Best ever annual sales of 17.9 MT in FY25, up 5%; Q4 sales 5.33 MT, up 20% QoQ and 17% YoY
items.quote: sales volume has grown by around 5% to stand at 17.9 million tons. This has resulted in reduction in the inventory of the finished goods. And this is the best ever annual sale s performance by the

items.statement: Q4 saleable steel production 4.72 MT (finished 4.09 MT); Q4 sales 5.33 MT including 0.36 MT from NMDC Steel
items.quote: In Q4, the Q4 total volume was 4.72, isn't it? Total saleable steel production volume was 4.72, out of which finished volume was 4.09 million tons in Q4.

items.statement: Expect margins to improve in coming quarters due to positive demand outlook and safeguard duty
items.quote: We are hopeful that the margins will improve further for the company in the quarters to come as the overall outlook is quite positive for sustained growth in domestic consumption.

items.statement: April-May NSR: long ~INR55,000/t, flat ~INR50,500-50,700/t; imported coal cost ~INR17,000-17,500/t
items.quote: for the long products, the NSR in April and May are almost like INR55,000 per ton. And so far as flat is concerned, there's improvement in the flat products post this safeguard duty and which is around INR0,500, INR50,600, INR50,700, like that.

items.statement: Imported coking coal cost fell from INR20,000/t in Q3 to INR18,500/t in Q4; now hovering ~INR17,000-17,500/t
items.quote: between quarter 3 and quarter 4, there is a reduction of around INR1,500 because in quarter 3, it was average around INR20,000 per ton, which came down to INR18,500 in quarter 4.

items.statement: Target semi-finished share below 14% (10-12%) in FY26 vs ~15% currently; new TMT mill at Durgapur in 2.5 years to reduce semis further
items.quote: we are targeting semis of less than 14%. That means around 10% to 12% we are targeting because we are taking various other steps for that.

items.statement: Q4 sales include 0.36 MT from NMDC Steel under marketing arrangement
items.quote: It includes steel from NMDC -- NSL, NMDC Steel Limited to the tune of around 3.6 lakh tons.

items.statement: Borrowings reduced to INR29,811 crores (Mar'25) from INR30,593 crores (Mar'24); peaked at INR35,659 crores (Jun'24)
items.quote: The borrowings stood at INR29,811 crores as against INR30,593 crores as on 31st March 2024, with a reduction of around INR700 crores during the year.

items.statement: Current debt ~INR26,700-26,800 crores; plan to reduce further in FY26; will fund capex via internal accruals and other instruments
items.quote: Today, the debt is around INR26,800 crores, INR26,700 crores, something like that, and we're planning to reduce it further in this financial year.

items.statement: Employee cost to reduce by INR400-500 crores in FY26 due to natural separations; Q4 jump of INR500-600 crores from discount rate, pension provision, PRP
items.quote: we are expecting a further reduction in the coming financial year, which is '25-'26 by at least INR400 to INR500 cr. This is our expectation.

items.statement: Next pay commission due CY2027; new expansion plants to have lower manpower cost via automation and AI
items.quote: Pay revision, as you know, actually, it happens every 10 years. So next is due in 2027. So we'll look into that whenever it comes, any guidance, et cetera.

items.statement: Safeguard duty notification expected to stabilize domestic prices; monsoon season a near-term risk
items.quote: With the safeguard duty notification coming into picture recently -- which has come into picture recently, we are hopeful that the domestic prices should stabilize and give a boost going forward. However, the ensuing monsoon season needs to be negotiated safely with hopes for better results in the coming quarters.

items.statement: Crude steel production target ~20 MT+ in FY26 vs 19.17 MT in FY25; saleable steel ~19.2-19.3 MT
items.quote: crude steel numbers were 19 million tons in '24-'25. We are looking at a number of around 20 or beyond in -- good numbers.

items.statement: BF productivity improved to 2.02 t/m3/day from 1.88; coke rate reduced to 421 kg/thm from 440 kg/thm; specific CO2 emissions down >3% YoY
items.quote: The annual average BF productivi ty, blast furnace productivity, has gone beyond 2 tons per meter cube per day. The same stood at 2.02 as against 1.88 in the previous year

items.statement: Operational efficiency savings of INR650 crores in FY25; targeting higher savings in FY26
items.quote: we have improved our technological parameters during this year and which has resulted in around INR650 crores of advantage in terms of cost.

items.statement: Monsoon season may keep prices subdued in near term; imported coal prices may increase slightly from current stable levels
items.quote: more so because the monsoon is going to come. So during that time, it will remain a little subdued. And after that, we expect better improvement in that.

items.statement: Pellet plants on BOO basis (no capex); 4 MT plant at Goa to use Jharkhand low-grade fines; Bhilai mines pellet plant starting May/Jun, others at tendering stage (3 years)
items.quote: INR7,500 crores doesn't include the pellet plant because pellet plants are coming in the BOO -- on BOO basis. So the capex will be done by the BOO operator.

items.statement: Iron ore fines sales from Bolani mines (Odisha) ongoing; Jharkhand sales await state government permission
items.quote: We have sold some quantities from Bolani Mines only in Odisha Group of Mines. And going forward, we are planning more sales from Bolani and also in Chhattisgarh going forward because after improving mining over there only, then we'll be able to sell something from Chhattisgarh as well, from Rowghat mines. But presently, we are selling from Bolani, and that will continue.

items.statement: Railway price revision provision of INR625 crores in Q4 (net of INR61 cr adjustment); full year provision INR2,200 crores
items.quote: INR625 crores is the figure for quarter 4. The net figure is INR625 crores, INR685 crores minus some other adjustment of INR61 crores is INR625 crores for quarter 4. And that is a part of the total figure of INR2,200 crores for the entire year.

items.statement: Decarbonization drive in 3 phases; MoUs signed with technology providers; specific CO2 emissions reduced >3% YoY
items.quote: During FY '24-'25, the specific CO2 emissions reduced by over 3% over the previous year, and we are making all efforts to reduce it further.

items.statement: Management declined to provide production or financial guidance, citing uncontrollable price factors and a policy of not giving forward estimates.
items.quote: Sandeep, I would like to tell you, I've been in this business for more than 40 years. In either way, I'll be wrong. So better to not give any guidance.

items.statement: Capital outlay for North-East region for the next two financial years is INR 250 crores.
items.quote: Our capital outlay for the North-East region for the next 2 financial years continues to be INR 250 crores.

items.statement: Dirok field can produce over 50 mmscfd but is restricted to ~15.6 mmscfd due to lack of demand; expects to reach 35-40 mmscfd once pipeline connectivity is established.
items.quote: Although this field can produce more than 50 million cubic feet of gas per day, we have to restrict the production due to lack of demand.

items.statement: B-80 oil storage capacity is 850,000 to 900,000 barrels; currently holding ~390,000 barrels.
items.quote: It can go up to, say, 850,000 to 900,000 barrels.

items.statement: Environmental clearance obtained for 40 development and 3 exploration wells in Kharsang; contract awarded for first phase of 9 development wells; first well producing ~200 bopd.
items.quote: We have obtained environmental clearance for drilling 40 development wells and 3 exploration wells in Kharsang Block in Arunachal Pradesh on 28 th February of 2025.

items.statement: Revised development plan for Dirok approved by DGH; plan to drill North Dirok well to Barail formation starting Q4 FY26 subject to rig availability.
items.quote: The revised development plan for Dirok has been approved by DGH for the extension of the block. We plan to drill a well in North Dirok upto the Barail formation and subject to the availability of the rig, we will start the drilling in the fourth quarter of this year.

items.statement: Signed Revenue Sharing Contract for B-15 block on April 15, 2025; planning cost-effective development for 2 discoveries; targeting production within 30 months.
items.quote: We signed the Revenue Sharing Contract on April 15, 2025 for Block B-15 in the Mumbai offshore, a discovered small field with an area of about 332 square kilometres.

items.statement: Acquired AEPL's 40% interest in B-80, now hold 100%; acquisition cost INR 315-320 crores; deferred payment of ~INR 137 crores due over 2 years.
items.quote: So, all put together, it should be somewhere around INR 310 crores or INR 315 crores, in the range of INR 315 crores to INR 320 crores.

items.statement: Dirok gas sales limited by local demand; expects demand constraints to reverse once North-East Gas Grid connects to National Grid, believed operational in FY26.
items.quote: As and when the concept of common carrier is accepted and the gas grid connectivity is established, the situation of the demand constraints would get reversed. It is difficult to predict the timeline, but we believe it should be operational in '25-26.

items.statement: Dirok gas price realized at USD 8.45/mmbtu in Q4 FY25 vs USD 8.25/mmbtu previous quarter; B-80 gas price at USD 12.09/mmbtu vs USD 10.78/mmbtu previous quarter; PY-1 gas price moving to PPAC-linked ~USD 6.75/mmbtu from GAIL.
items.quote: The price realized in the current quarter is USD 8.45 per mmbtu, whereas it was USD 8.25 mmbtu in the previous quarter.

items.statement: Management holding ~390,000 barrels of oil inventory targeting sale at ~USD 75/bbl; willing to sell if prices reach that level or if storage capacity (900k bbl) is reached.
items.quote: We would like to sell the oil around US$75 per barrel. That's our benchmark price for us and if we are any time when we reach to that level, we will get it. We'll get to offload.

items.statement: Term loan outstanding ~INR 81.67 crores; India Ratings reaffirmed IND A rating with outlook revised to Positive; may raise debt up to INR 200-250 crores (max 10% of market cap) for offshore capex if internal generation insufficient.
items.quote: As on today, the term loan outstanding is about INR 81.67 crores. India Ratings has reaffirmed the rating IND A and revised the outlook from 'Stable' to 'Positive' for INR 500 crores bank loan.

items.statement: Management targets debt not exceeding 10% of market cap (~INR 200-250 crores); offshore drilling on deferred payment terms; talking to bankers for lower interest rates.
items.quote: See, we never wanted to have a debt more than 10% of our market cap. That's the level we wanted to have it. So, we will be looking somewhere around INR 200-250 crores if we are not able to generate internally.

items.statement: Acquired AEPL's 40% stake in B-80 for INR 315-320 crores; 100% revenue and cost now consolidated; awaiting government approval for formal capitalization and fair value recognition.
items.quote: No, it's a done deal and 00% revenue is accounted in our books. 100% cost is taken over because we have taken over the income and expenditure there on to it and we are waiting for the formal approval from the Government.

items.statement: Expecting final clearance of Ring-Fenced PSC along with Palej block extension in Cambay; intangible asset of INR 9 crores recorded for Ring-Fenced PSC signing.
items.quote: We are also expecting the final clearance of the Ring-Fenced PSC along with the extension of the Palej block. This could add substantial value to the Cambay blocks.

items.statement: PY-3 block (21% interest) under arbitration/legal dispute with ONGC; issued legal notice; invested INR 385 crores; not an active partner currently.
items.quote: We have issued a legal notice. It will be come to an end through the dispute resolution.

items.statement: B-80 gas price now moving akin to imported LNG price; PY-1 gas price shifting to PPAC-linked term sheet with GAIL at ~USD 6.75/mmbtu on GCV.
items.quote: The gas price in the Western region is now moving akin to the imported LNG price.

items.statement: B-80 oil inventory ~390,000 barrels held for better price realization; not in pressing need to liquidate at lower prices.
items.quote: We have about 390,000 barrels of oil in stock and are expecting a better price to realize before we sell that.

items.statement: Dirok average gas production and sales FY25: 17.76 mmscfd vs 19.96 mmscfd FY24; Q4 FY25 sales volume 0.37 Bcf vs 0.44 Bcf previous quarter.
items.quote: For the year 2024-25, the average production and sales were 17.76 compared to 19.96 mmscfd in '23-24.

items.statement: B-80 production FY25: 275,000 barrels oil and 1.9 Bcf gas vs 320,000 barrels oil and 2.5 Bcf gas FY24; Q4 FY25: 60,544 barrels oil and 0.44 Bcf gas.
items.quote: For the year, the production is 275,000 barrels of oil and 1.9 Bcf of gas compared to 320,000 barrels of oil and 2.5 Bcf of gas.

items.statement: Kharsang first development well producing ~200 bopd; drilling cycle ~21-25 days per well plus hook-up; targeting one well per month.
items.quote: The well is producing about 200 barrels of oil per day.

items.statement: PY-1 targeting minimum 5-6 mmscfd per well from 3 planned wells; drilling to commence after Petro Vietnam report by end June 2025.
items.value: 5 million to 6 million cubic feet per day
items.quote: Each well, we are targeting at least minimum of 5 million to 6 million cubic feet per day.

items.statement: B-80 production impacted by valve issues and monsoon risk; workover planned (~30 days total for 2 wells) and additional drilling post-monsoon to restore volumes.
items.quote: See, actually that, some valve was not functioning, so we have to shut it for a few days and very few days and when we got to open it up, small, small issues will come up and unfortunately, that has happened in the last quarter.

items.statement: DNPL pipeline common carrier status and National Grid connectivity timeline uncertain; dependent on Oil India, PNGRB, and national interest; no visibility on exact reasons for delay.
items.quote: It will be driven by Oil India. It will be driven by PNGRB. It is driven by the national interest. So, and Oil India, in our gas also 50% is Oil India's gas, Dirok Gas.

items.statement: B-80 facility charging model changed from day-rate to per-barrel rate to ensure sustainability of MOPU, FSO, and SPM assets under lower oil prices.
items.quote: Until the workover and additional drilling in B-80, the charge to the subsidiaries has been moved from a day rate to a rate per barrel of production. This will ensure the sustenance of all 3 assets.

items.statement: Site restoration fund deposit of INR 90 crores held in bank for future site restoration; not payable to third parties.
items.quote: No, no, site restoration fund means we have deposited that much money, right? So that is in the bank.

items.statement: Engineering order book at INR 2762 crores at end of Q4 FY25
items.quote: At the end of Q4 financial year 25 the total order book for the engineering division stood at INR 2762 crores.

items.statement: Roha greenfield resin plant capex around Rs.400 crores with 80% debt
items.quote: As we have informed in earlier calls, the total CAPEX of the Roha plant is in the region of around Rs.400 crores, and the debt component is around the 80% of that.

items.statement: Chemical margins lower in Q4 due to seasonality and input cost increases; price hikes initiated
items.quote: The 4th Quarter, if you are comparing with the immediate preceding quarter, there has been a decline , due to the seasonality of certain product lines. And also we have seen some input cost increases. We have now taken action to pass on the price increases to the customers.

items.statement: Engineering margins under pressure from legacy projects; UP Jal Nigam and another large order causing headwinds
items.quote: There are a couple of large projects that we are working through the execution which we talked about in the last call are giving us headwinds in this segment . As we, said a short while back, these are multiyear contracts and margins will be under pressure for these jobs.

items.statement: No full-year FY26 guidance; will provide outlook at end of Q2 FY26
items.quote: As per company practices, we should be able to come back and give you a guidance, a broad guidance in the end of the 2nd Quarter.

items.statement: Debtor days increased to ~160 days due to UP project funding issues and March invoicing spike
items.quote: One major contract which has contributed to the increa se in debtors is the UP contract, as I mentioned the funding issues in this contract has led to an elongated debtors level in this contract. items.statement: SAP implementation causing minor disruption; expected to normalize by third month of Q1 FY26

items.statement: UP Jal Nigam project execution to continue through FY26 and into early FY27; conservative backlog assumption includes possible foreclosures
items.quote: This will continue definitely in this financial year, and maybe early part of the next financial year , both these jobs will continue for the entire financial year.

items.statement: Sri Lanka order progress positive with authorities committing funds to expedite
items.quote: Regarding the Sri Lanka order there has been positive development at the quarter end with the Sri Lanka authorities committing funds to expedite the job progress .

items.statement: Delhi Jal Board order was minuscule and now completed; removed from presentation
items.quote: And just to follow up on in the last presentation we had mentioned Delhi Jal Board , that was a very minuscule part which has since been completed.

items.quote: Phase 1 will entail expenditure of INR 350 crores and Phase 2 would be another, I think, about INR 200 crores to INR 225 crores. So the funding would be , right now, what we have thought is through internal accruals and some debt.

items.quote: INR 150 crores for the current year as well as some spillover would happen in the next financial year also. Hiten Boricha: Okay. And sir... Nakul Sethi: We have already spent INR 40 crores of the

items.statement: Overall capacity utilization across three plants was close to 70% in FY25
items.quote: I think overall, I think all the three plants together, we had a capacity utilization of about close to 70%.

It happened around the third week of May. So we can look ahead for the next few quarters to be much far, far better than the previous quarter.

items.statement: FY25 EBITDA margin improved to 12.49% from 12.07%; management expects to maintain similar margins in FY26
items.quote: We are expecting that same kind of margins, we should be able to maintain in the current financial year also.

Karnataka, we took a price increase, and we took a price increase in the nearby state Pondicherry and Kerala. We took a price increase in Odisha as well when the duty went up.

items.statement: Market positions: #1 in Madhya Pradesh, #2-3 in Karnataka, #2 in Delhi, near #1 in Jharkhand, #2 in Odisha; strengthening portfolio with three millionaire brands
items.quote: We are number one player in Madhya Pradesh. So we are number two , number three player in Karnataka. We are number two in Delhi. We are almost number one in Jharkhand, almost, close to number one, going neck to neck with a leader. We are number two in Odisha.

items.statement: FY25 total income INR 14,474 million (+13% YoY), EBITDA INR 1,807 million (+16%, 12.49% margin), PBT INR 1,437 million (+18%, 9.92% margin), net profit INR 1,045 million (+21%)
items.quote: For the whole of FY25, our total income increased to INR 14,474 million from INR 12,864 million, showing a year-on-year growth of around 13%. Our EBITDA for the financial year reached INR 1,807 million, reflecting a growth of 16% on a year-on-year basis with a steady margin of 12.49%.

items.quote: Capex were done for both Woodpecker and for the Odisha plant. So Odisha plant advantage of this capex will come from this current year onwards.

items.statement: Electrical contacts revenue growth expected to surpass 20% in FY26

items.quote: We see that by FY 27 we feel that this would bring in an opportunity of a year on year, opportunity of 150 crores year on year, which will build a much wider landscape for Shivalik and Shivalik products.

items.quote: To some extent, we have quantified, but it is too early to intimate to the market, but we must intimate maybe the on the next concall.

items.statement: Net debt remained at zero in FY25 with cash flows exceeding capex
items.quote: while net debt stayed at zero, we also continued to generate cash flows in excess of our capital expenditure

items.statement: North America EV market conditions settled with increasing inquiries and customer capacity buildup

items.statement: Shifting procurement to domestic suppliers to de-risk from global quality volatility; exploring backward integration partnerships
items.quote: We by favoring domestic suppliers to eventually work towards de risking from the global quality volatility and exploring partnerships for full-fledged backward integration.

items.statement: Strengthening R&D capabilities with dedicated department to support portfolio and accelerate new product development
items.quote: The goal here is to establish a more robust and dedicated R & D department to support our current product portfolio and accelerate all new product development.

items.statement: Tariff impact minimal (3-4% of revenue); long validation cycles prevent inventory front-running; customers ordering conservatively

items.quote: So these usually can take anything between 12 to 18 months, if you're being optimistic, and that's when it then gets released for commercial production.

items.quote: One can say that maybe we might be around 25%, 26% over a longer period of time for 2 to 3 years.

items.quote: We have a firm plan for capex of about INR38 crores, about INR15 crores out of that will be for debottlenecking keeping in mind the change in product mix and then a land purchase of about INR20 crores.

items.statement: Order book INR95 cr as of April 1, FY26 railroad sales target INR25 cr
items.quote: The order book is at about INR95 crores as of now and the railroad sales in FY '26 will be roughly about INR25 crores.

items.statement: FY25 capacity utilization 45%, Q4 FY25 55%, targeting 59% in FY26 and >90% in 2-2.5 years
items.quote: Our capacity utilization for FY '25 is at 45%. As per the current year's production and financial plan, we will end with 62% and hopefully we should cross 90% over the next 2 to 3 years.

items.quote: We also added additional countries where we are exporting. We are now exporting to about 18 countries. Hopefully in 1 or 2 quarters we'll add 1 more country, maybe 19 countries.

items.statement: Cost-plus model with 1-quarter lag price adjustment; input price declines benefited FY25 margins temporarily
items.quote: See, what happens is when input prices go down, the price corrections happen with a 1 quarter time lag. So from Q1 to Q2, there were lower input prices so we gained for it.

items.statement: FY25 revenue mix 46% domestic, 54% exports; US tariffs 10% from April 2 absorbed by customers on ex-works basis
items.quote: During Q4 FY '25 and for the full fiscal year, our revenue mix remained well balanced with domestic sales contributing 46% and exports accounting for 54% of total sales.

items.statement: US reciprocal tariff 10% effective April 2; management expects no adverse impact as India tariffs better than peers
items.quote: See as of now, the additional tariff of 10% has already been kicked in from April 2. Our customers are absorbing this increase in cost because our sales are all on ex-works basis.

items.statement: FY25 capex INR86.5 cr over last 3 years; company remains debt-free with INR75 cr free reserves
items.quote: In-spite of company spending of INR86.5 crores on capex and quarterly dividends of INR43.7 crore totalling to INR130.2 crore in last 3 years, it continues to be totally debt free with INR75 crores in free reserve.

items.statement: 4-year CAGR: Revenue 24.27%, EBITDA 35.41%, EBIT 51.54%, PAT 56.56%
items.quote: Revenue from operations, 24.27%; EBITDA, excluding other income, at 35.41%; EBIT, excluding other income, at 51.54%; PAT 56.56%.

items.statement: Railroad component development issues; hopeful of resolution within 90 days

items.statement: No Chinese competition in domestic market; India and China dominant globally; cost advantage vs Europe/US drives market share gains
items.quote: I think in the Indian market there are only Indian players. The re are no Chinese players coming into India. That's A. B, the two emerging markets which are dominating our kind of industries is India and China

items.quote: See, when the output goes up, for a quarter you will see inventory buildup which will be then converted to sale in the following quarter. So there is no delay of shipments from the customers.

items.statement: Debt-free for second consecutive year; disciplined capital allocation and tight working capital management
items.quote: I'm also pleased to report that for the second consecutive year, we have maintained a debt free position reflecting our disciplined capital allocation and tight working capital management.

items.statement: Featured in Fortune India Top 100 Emerging Stars; credited team dedication for performance
items.quote: We are also delighted to share that Steelcast Limited has b een featured in Fortune India's Top 100 Emerging Stars, a recognition awarded to companies demonstrating exceptional performance

items.statement: Targets US$108 billion gross revenue by 2030 with 40% ROCE
items.quote: The number of all the groups and everything put together, we are targeting for 2030 will be US$108 billion on the top line. And of course, the ROCE remains same at 40%.

items.statement: Capex guidance for next year is INR 6,000 crores plus or minus 10%
items.quote: Looking at all these new developments, our capex guidance for the next year and including for our existing business is about INR 6,000 crores plus or minus 10%.

items.statement: 50% of FY26 capex is regular and 50% growth-oriented, majority towards non-automotive
items.quote: 50% of this is regular capex and 50% is purely growth-oriented. Majority of the growth business is towards the non-automotive piece.

items.statement: Large business order book of approximately US$88 billion
items.quote: Finally, there is no better proof of the stability and strength of the diversified business model than a large book business order of approximately US$88 billion.

items.statement: Non-auto order book is $2.7 billion including $1.3 billion from aerospace
items.quote: you've given $2.7 billion of non-auto order book. And then in other slides, we've given $1.3 billion is coming from aerospace.

items.statement: Modules and polymer margins under pressure due to European production decline and launch issues; worst behind, improvement expected
items.quote: We saw around about 8% or 9% decline in the automotive production, which meant the volume throughput was somewhat limited in the European market, which was the largest part of the business in MPP. And hence, the cost looks elevated on that account as well.

items.statement: Aerospace margins dipped due to AD Industries acquisition and greenfield ramp-up; profitability to improve in coming quarters
items.quote: Of course, you're seeing numbers now with the addition of AD Industries as well. That was also a unit that was struggling with profitability. So of course, we are making huge inroads together with the customers to improve that and driving group synergies to bring that to the level where we expect in

items.statement: Global light vehicle production declined ~1% to 89.7 million units in FY25; emerging markets showed resilience

items.statement: Signs of softening production volumes in current year due to trade uncertainties and platform mix changes
items.quote: As we ride through the current financial year, there are signs of softening of production volumes, driven mainly by uncertainties created by evolving trade dynamics and evolving platform mix.

items.statement: Majority of US sales USMCA compliant; constructive discussions with customers on tariff pass-through for remaining portion; no material financial impact expected
items.quote: we follow a global-local strategy and hence, majority of our U.S. sales is USMCA compliant. For the remaining portion of the sales, we are in constructive discussions with our customers regarding the pass-through of tariff-related charges and do not seeing material financial impact.

items.statement: Net debt-to-EBITDA at 0.9x, lowest in 5-year period; well within stated policy

items.statement: Vision Systems achieved >US$400 million lifetime sales in camera monitoring systems for CV segment

items.statement: Achieved 3CX10 customer diversification target; >50% revenue from emerging markets in FY25
