items.quote: I'd say we are now very close to line of sight on being EBITDA breakeven, yes. But that is subject to a big if, which is the fact that pricing needs to hold steady at these levels.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 material inflation was flattish; precious metals up, steel and aluminium soft
items.quote: So overall, while there were some pockets of inflationary pressure, the broader softness, particularly in the metals and energy complex helped maintain a relatively stable cost environment for the quarter. And therefore, in net terms for this last quarter, quarter 4, material inflation was about flattish.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 commodity inflation expected; aluminium surged, steel/ABS/rubber firm, precious metals declining
items.quote: On the material cost front, alumin ium prices have surged and there is some firmness on a few lines like steel, ABS and rubber. These are expected to be partially offset by declines in precious metals : palladium, rhodium and platinum. However, I expect to see some amount of commodity inflation in net terms for the quarter.

items.statement: Electric portfolio now nearly 20% of domestic revenue, up from under 10%
items.quote: And what we must recognize in this is the fact that the electric vehicle portfolio has moved from being under 10% of our domestic revenue to nearly 20% on a full year basis in the course of this current year.

items.statement: Chetak 35 series launched Dec 2024, third variant 3503 launched end May 2025, new entry-level variant coming June 2025
items.quote: With the introduction of the third 35 series variant, which is the 3503 in end May 2025, as well as the impending introduction of a new variant in June as an upgrade to the entry level and large selling 2903, the Chetak portfolio will become very potent.

items.statement: Freedom CNG motorcycle retailed 60,000 units, reaching 10-11% penetration in CNG-dense areas like Kerala and Delhi
items.quote: It has already retailed 60,000 units basis its key proposition of 50% cut in fuel costs, being adopted mostly by long-distance riders in high- pump density areas. We are now very specifically and vigorously targeting this cohort, a long-distance rider in high pump density areas to drive up the penetration of Freedom, which has reached even 10% to 11% of the 125cc segment in some CNG dense areas li

items.statement: Domestic 125cc+ market share eroded from 26% in FY24 to 24% in FY25; countermeasures in place from April
items.quote: From an estimated market share of 21% in financial year '23, we went up to 26% in FY '24 and have closed at 24% in FY '25 in the 125cc+ segment. Our countermeasures to reverse this are already in place from April onwards.

items.statement: Chetak EV market share rose from 13% in Q4 FY24 to 25% in Q4 FY25, becoming #1 electric 2-wheeler brand
items.quote: From a market share of 13% in Q4 FY24, Chetak has clocked a market share of 25% in Q4 FY25, a rise of 12% points on the back of the launch of the highly successful 35 series platform in end December. The quarter 4 market share also placed Chetak as the number one electric two-wheeler brand in India.

items.statement: E-auto market share doubled from 17% in FY24 to 33% in FY25; #1 position in April and May 2025
items.quote: The E auto segment of the industry grew at about 60% in FY '25. And here, we have doubled our market share from 17% in FY '24 to 33% in FY '25. The momentum continues with Bajaj securing the number 1 position in electric autos in April and I am told in May till date.

items.statement: Rare earth magnet supply from China at risk; new end-use declaration process defined but approvals pending; production impact possible by July
items.quote: Having said this, I must point out a dark cloud on the horizon in terms of continued supply of rare earth magnets from China, which are an essential component of high-performance EV motors. While finally a process for end use declaration for non-military users has been defined, which includes certification by the Chinese embassy in India and a couple of authorities finally in China, we are yet to

items.statement: Q4 FY25 USD/INR realization at 86.5 vs 84.3 in Q3 FY25 and 83 in Q4 FY24; rupee appreciated end of quarter
items.quote: On the currency side, we had tailwinds. It was the quarter when USD INR hit its peak and so therefore dollar realization for the quarter came in at 86.5 versus 84.3 in the previous quarter and 83 for the same time last year. However, the rupee appreciated towards the end of the quarter, as you'd be aware and that had a slight impact on our financials as we had to restate our receivables at the clo

items.statement: Currency turning from tailwind to headwind in Q1 FY26 as dollar realizations soften; ~$500M quarterly dollar-linked sales
items.quote: Currency, which was a tailwind so far, appears to be an emerging headwind in this current quarter, quarter 1, as dollar realizations have started to soften. And given our quarterly dollar-linked sales of approximately 500 million thereabouts, the lower USD INR realization will weigh down on the margins in this near term.

items.statement: Netherlands subsidiary arranged €800M debt funding for KTM: €200M cash infused FY25, €600M debt provided last week for creditor quota
items.quote: Very clearly, what we said was that our Netherlands subsidiary, BAIHBV has arranged a debt funding package of about Euro 800 million to enable the continuity of the KTM business by paying off the approved quota to the creditors, that was approved by them in the February meeting in furtherance of the debt restructuring with the approval of the court of Austria and for infusing funds into the compan

items.statement: Intent to acquire controlling stake in Pierer Bajaj AG (PBAG) via call option for up to €50.65M, exercisable till May 31, 2026; regulatory approvals in 2-3 months
items.quote: Alongside, our Netherlands subsidiary also entered into a call option agr eement on 22nd May itself with Pierer Industries and the parent of Pierer Industries, which I will use as a short form called PIKO for the rights to purchase either by itself or by a third party nominated by ourselves from Pierer Industries, the shares that they hold in Pierer Bajaj, recognize that Pierer Industries holds 50

items.statement: Board approved dividend of INR210 per share, total ~INR5,900 crores, 72% payout on reported PAT
items.quote: The Board of Directors at its meeting today also approved a dividend of INR210 per share today. That will total a tad below INR5,900 crores when we pay this out in a couple of months, which will reflect a 72% payout on our total reported profit after tax.

items.statement: BACL turned PAT positive in Q3 FY25, full year profit for first time; AUM ~INR9,500 crores, disbursals crossed INR10,000 crores
items.quote: It turned PAT positive in Q3 and has now reported a full year profit for the first time, marking a significant milestone in its journey towards sustainable profitability. With 100% pan-India coverage , disbursals have crossed the INR10,000 crore s mark and BACL is now firmly positioned as a strategic enabler in our ecosystem.

items.statement: KTM restructuring: creditors accepted 30% quota paid by May 23, 2025; auditors needed solvency proof before signing off
items.quote: You'll be aware that the creditors of KTM had accepted the restructuring plan and approved it back in February, where essentially a quota of 30% of the claims had to be paid by 23rd of May 2025. At that point of time, the auditors also needed to see the company to demonstrate its ability to remain solvent and as a going concern. And until such time that event wasn't completed, they weren't able to

items.statement: Free cash flow robust at INR6,500 crores for FY25
items.quote: Free cash flow continued a strong track record and remained robust at INR6,500 crores for the year.

items.statement: Consolidated PAT INR7,325 crores, dragged down by ~INR900 crores share of loss from KTM investment
items.quote: Consolidated profit came in at INR 7,325 crores. It was dragged down by the share of loss that we had to account from our investment in the global KTM business that reported a loss and the results of that business flows into our Netherlands subsidiary, wh ich, in turn, w e consolidate. The share of that loss accounted for us between the first half and the se cond half added up to about INR900 cror

items.statement: Management confident of meeting 5-year plan ending CY28; current inventory at 85% of target; expect to add at least 3,000 rooms to pipeline in FY26 taking total above 20,000 rooms, 3 years ahead of CY28
items.quote: As of the 31st March 2025, the current total inventory for Lemon Tree stands at 85% of the 5 year target. In fact, we are also confident that we will add at least 3,000 rooms to our pipeline this financial year, taking the total inventory this year above the 20,000 numbers, i.e., 3 years in advance of CY28

items.statement: Internal EBITDA margin target for FY28 is at least 55%, up from 49.4% in FY25
items.quote: Our internal expectation is at least 55%.

items.statement: EBITDA margin to stabilize above 50% after renovation expenses drop from 3% of revenue in FY26 to 1.2%-1.3% ongoing; tech investments to fall from 1.4% to 0.2% of revenue
items.quote: Post which renovation expenses will close at 1.2%-1.3% of revenue on an ongoing basis which will help stabilize EBITDA margin over 50%

items.statement: Renovation capex of Rs. 130 crore planned for FY26 (3% of revenue), down from Rs. 100 crore in FY25; will drop significantly in FY27
items.quote: This year we will invest Rs. 130 crore in renovation. At the end of which we will drop from 2.2 %, in fact this year it will be 3% of the revenue. But then suddenly we will drop to 1.2 %

items.statement: 70% of owned portfolio (6,000 rooms) renovated; higher-value renovation to complete in FY26; minor refurbs to continue into FY27 at lower spend
items.quote: At present I think we have renovated about 70% of the portfolio and the higher value renovation, we will do another 30% this year and knock it off.

items.statement: Signed 15 new management/franchise contracts in Q4 FY25 adding 833 rooms to pipeline; operationalized 2 hotels adding 121 rooms
items.quote: On the asset light side in Q4 we signed 15 new management and franchise contracts adding 833 new rooms to our pipeline and operationalized 2 hotels adding 121 rooms to our operational portfolio.

items.statement: Total group inventory at 212 hotels and 17,116 rooms as of 31 March 2025; 10,269 rooms across 111 hotels operational
items.quote: As of 31st March, this year, the total inventory for the group stands at 212 hotels and 17,116 rooms divided into 10,269 rooms and 111 hotels being operational and the rest in pipeline.

items.statement: Retail demand share target 66% by CY28 from 45% in FY25; driven by loyalty program relaunch (Infinity 2.0), website upgrades, and structural shift in Indian middle-income discretionary spend
items.quote: With this we should start seeing an uptick in the retail demand share which stood at 45% in FY25 to achieve the target of 66% by CY28

items.statement: Aurika Mumbai ARR expected to hit Rs. 11,000-12,000 in winter 2025; Q4 FY25 EBITDA Rs. 42 crore at 67% margin on Rs. 880 crore investment
items.quote: We are pretty confident that Aurika's ARR will hit. I mean if you look this winter it will nearly certainly be over Rs. 11,000 - Rs. 12,000 and then that becomes the run rate.

items.statement: Consolidated debt reduced by Rs. 190 crore in FY25 to Rs. 1,699 crore; debt/EBITDA improved to 2.67x from 3.57x; expect Rs. 300 crore repayment in FY26, Rs. 400 crore in FY27
items.quote: The repayment is not Rs. 400 crore a year, it will be Rs. 300 crore this year, Rs. 400 crore next year.

items.statement: Fleur Hotels IPO under discussion; aim to create asset-owning development vehicle; Lemon Tree to become asset-light brand/tech/management platform; may deconsolidate to show higher management fee growth
items.quote: By the next board meeting we will try and come up with a very definite plan - what we are going to do with the listing of Fleur and how Fleur will be the vehicle that does asset development assets.

items.statement: Keys hotels targeting north of Rs. 60 crore net EBITDA in FY27 after full renovation; Q4 FY25 margin reached 40%
items.quote: What I said to you is that when it's fully renovated and it will continue throughout this year also, what we are targeting is roughly north of Rs. 60 crore net EBITDA from this portfolio. And I would therefore like to just give this guidance that is in FY27 it will be north of Rs. 60 crore.

items.statement: Geopolitical tensions and COVID surge in May 2025 caused revenue growth to drop from 20-21% in Mar-Apr to 14% in May; Q1 FY26 expected mid-to-high teens growth
items.quote: We grew about 20% in March, 21% in April and then in May it crashed to 14%. We will end this quarter maybe in the mid to high teens, so that is the effect.

items.statement: Loyalty program has 1.5 million members vs 11,000 rooms (136 per room); target 2 million members and 100 per room; currently generates 25-30% of business vs Marriott's 65%
items.quote: Lemon Tree has about 1.5 million members and it has 11,000 rooms. We think in another 3 years we will be operating 20,000 rooms or maybe 4 years. We have 2 million members by say in the next few months we will have also 100 members per room.

items.statement: Global hotel chains entering India is positive; will rationalize pricing, improve quality, and consolidate fragmented unbranded supply (90% of 1.5M rooms unbranded); Lemon Tree positioned to capture small-hotel franchise via Keys brands and
items.quote: I think it's a good thing personally. I am not talking only from a Lemon Tree perspective. When a market gets more organized, pricing becomes rational, customers get used to better quality and then the high performers are the ones who are delivering that.

items.statement: Strategic focus on Lemon Tree, Lemon Tree Premier, Aurika for managed portfolio; Keys Prima/Select/Lite for franchise of small hotels; Red Fox to be repositioned or converted
items.quote: Keys Prima, Keys Select and Keys Lite will become the vehicles for franchise for small hotels supported by tech and distribution from Lemon Tree. Lemon Tree and Lemon Tree Premier and Aurika will be the managed part of the brands which will grow in future.

items.statement: International expansion opportunistic and asset-light; targeting destinations where 26M Indians travel (expected 100M by FY30); Dubai first foray; expect presence in all key outbound destinations in 3-5 years
items.quote: Not strategic but opportunistic and fundamentally asset light. So, wherever Indians go. So, I will give you, I think I gave this example a year ago, I think 18 million foreign arrivals come to India of which I think 7 -8 million are Indians only and the other 10 -11 are foreigners. But 26 million Indians go out and we expect that by FY30 it will become 100 million.

items.statement: Cash profit Rs. 382.4 crore in FY25 (up 30%); Rs. 100-120 crore capex, Rs. 200 crore debt repaid, Rs. 60 crore cash on books
items.quote: Total cash profit generated by the company during FY25 was Rs. 382.4 crore, an increase of 30% over FY24.

items.statement: Lemon Tree aims to become dividend-distributing company within 1-2 years post Fleur IPO; will need minimal capital for marketing, tech, distribution
items.quote: I would expect Lemon Tree to become very asset light, very high in profit and a dividend distributing company within the next 1-2 year.

items.statement: Aurika Shillong benefits: 5% interest subvention, 75% LTV, 3.5% effective interest cost, 10-year GST refund, low lease rent
items.quote: The government has been very kind. In the auction they have given us a subvention on the interest rate of 5%. When we look at Debt to Equity of say 1:1, here we can get away with loan to value of 75% and that too the interest costs will be at 3.5% and there is a GST refund for 10 years.

items.statement: No management changes mentioned; focus on execution, frugality, and cost control
items.quote: We look at fundamentally trends to decide strategy and after that what we are very focused on is basically the execution and the cost. We really are very focused on frugality.

items.statement: Standalone debt ~Rs. 300-350 crore; repaying Rs. 70-80 crore annually on 15-year tenure with ballooning structure; Fleur debt separate (60% owned, 40% APG); cash flows not fungible between entities
items.quote: There is Rs. 300 – Rs. 350 crore of debt in Lemon Tree. I am giving you very illustratively, it's around that number. We would be repaying Rs. 70 – Rs. 80 crore of that.

items.statement: Fleur Hotels to become development and asset-owning vehicle with identified pipeline; Lemon Tree to be brand/tech/management platform; governance firewalled
items.quote: Where to go, what to develop, how to finance it and they will own all the assets. So, there will be a development cum asset owning company with a large pipeline which we have already identified. And Lemon Tree will become more asset light and will be a brand/technology/management platform.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 revenue Rs. 379.4 crore (+15% YoY), net EBITDA Rs. 205 crore (+17% YoY), margin 54% (+109 bps); ARR Rs. 7,042 (+7%), occupancy 77.6% (+557 bps), RevPAR Rs. 5,462 (+15%)
items.quote: In Q4 this year Lemon Tree recorded its highest ever 4th Quarter revenue at Rs. 379.4 crore. Our revenue grew 15% compared to Q4 last year while net EBITDA grew 17% YoY to 205 crore, translating into a net EBITDA margin of 54% which increased 109 bps YoY.

items.statement: FY25 revenue Rs. 1,288 crore (+20%), EBITDA Rs. 637 crore (+20%), PAT Rs. 108.1 crore in Q4 (+29%), cash profit Rs. 382.4 crore (+30%)
items.quote: The total revenue for the year stood at Rs. 1,288 crore which was an increase of 20% over FY24 and the EBITDA stood at Rs. 637 crore for the full year, which also increased by 20% over FY24.

items.statement: Management fees: Rs. 44.4 crore in Q4 (+16% YoY), Rs. 149 crore FY25 (+22%); third-party fees Rs. 16 crore (+11%), Fleur fees Rs. 28.3 crore (+19%)
items.quote: Total management fees for Lemon Tree stood at Rs. 44.4 crore in Q4, an increase of 16% over YoY and 149 crore for the full year, an increase of 22% over FY24.

items.statement: Hopeful to achieve 10-12% growth in e-commerce segment going forward.
items.quote: Last 2 years have been a little challenging, and there has not been much growth. But going forward, because of these plans that we have talked about just now, we are hopeful that we will be able to, we are ambitious that we should be able to, target that kind of a growth.

items.statement: Operating EBITDA margins expected to be maintained at similar levels.
items.quote: Without other income, I think we will be able to maintain beyond that.

items.statement: Coal India e-auction volumes to increase, driving revenue upward.
items.quote: Based on that we can have a fair assumption that the number of events will increase and the revenue should be on the upward trajectory only.

items.statement: MMRPL expected to grow with EPR policy, positive outlook over 3-4 years.
items.quote: So these are 2 factors which should drive the numbers up, which is why we have a positive outlook over the next 3 to 4 years of this business now coming into a steady state and growing.

items.statement: MMRPL profits may take at least a couple of years.
items.period: at least a couple of years
items.quote: So at least a couple of years that we'll be able to take till that EPR policy matures and gives us a proper impetus to drive a profit there, sir? At least a couple of years.

items.statement: Steady state tax rate expected at 25% under lower regime.
items.quote: Yes, yes. Because as per that taxation laws, once we have opted for lower regime, so it will has to be at the lower regime because we cannot change that option.

items.statement: New office and DR site in New Delhi to be ready in a couple of months.
items.quote: Another couple of months.

items.statement: Leasing portal ready, to be rolled out in a couple of months.
items.quote: The leasing portal is more or less ready. It should be rolled out in a couple of months.

items.statement: ERP solutions for mining to be marketed within this financial year.
items.quote: It is still in the development stage, and we will be able to market it within this financial year.

items.statement: Revenue split: 90% private, 10% government.
items.quote: It is very difficult because we do not have any such kind of segmentation like that. But more or less, it is in the range of 90:10.

items.statement: Coal segment contributed about 10% to e-commerce revenue last year.
items.quote: Last year, it may be around maximum 10%.

items.statement: Coal India auction contribution in Q4 was 4-5% of e-commerce revenue.
items.quote: And as we have got the business back in the last quarter, so it can be in the range of 4% to 5%.

items.statement: Rights Issue of INR124.23 crores subscribed 1.45 times with marquee institutional and retail participation
items.quote: As you know, we had done an issue of INR124.23 crores, which got issued about 1.4 5 times. Besides the promoters also witnessed the subscription by a lot of marquee institutional and retail investors, quite encouraging for us.

items.statement: Antara Senior Care won Operator of the Year - Senior Living at 13th Asia Pacific Eldercare Innovation Awards
items.quote: Also very glad to report that Antara Senior Care also got awarded as the Operator of the Year - Senior Living at the 13th Asia Pacific Eldercare Innovation Awards.

items.statement: Antara Purukul, Dehradun received first certificate of excellence from ASLI after Grant Thornton audit
items.quote: Pleased to report that Antara Purukul, Dehradun is the first independent senior living community to receive this prestigious certificate of excellence from ASLI.

items.statement: Sold 3 floors at Max Towers for INR105.08 crores, strengthening balance sheet for growth capital
items.quote: We have completed the sales now and received a complete consideration of INR105.08 crores. This is in line with what our broad capital allocation and asset monetization strategy was.

items.statement: Estate 360 Gurgaon sold 90% inventory (260 of 292 units) with INR239 crores collections at 94% efficiency
items.quote: As of 31st March, we have sold 90% of the inventory. So 260 of the 292 units have been sold till March '25. Some more units have been sold in April and May, but that's the update for next quarter.

items.statement: Confident of selling entire Estate 360 inventory within Q2 FY26
items.quote: And we are confident within Q2 FY '26, we'll be able to sell the entire inventory.

items.statement: Active discussions with Max Estates for second senior living development on contiguous land in Gurgaon
items.quote: We are already in active discussions with Max Estates for a probable partnership i n second development in the same geography, it's a contiguous piece of land, therefore, economies of scale will also kick

items.statement: Added 234 beds in FY25 across Gurgaon, Noida, Bangalore; 43 beds operationalized in Chennai May 25; 150 beds under fit-outs targeting ~500 total
items.quote: On Antara Assisted Care, we have added 234 beds in care homes during FY '25. Our bed capacity increased to 300 in the three geographies, Gurgaon, Noida, and Bangalore, 43 beds in ECR operationalized in May '25, and there are 150 beds more under fit outs.

items.statement: Care Homes and Care at Home reported double-digit revenue growth over comparable last quarter
items.quote: Both care homes and care at home have reported very healthy revenues with double-digit growth over comparable last quarter.

items.statement: AGEasy NPS improved from 13 to 38 in last 9 months with 29,500 repeat customers and 2 lakh lives touched
items.quote: Our NPS is extremely healthy, which vindicates the customers' confidence in our offering, which is growing steadily from 13 to now 38 NPS score in the last 9 months.

items.statement: Noida Phase 1 sold out with INR394 crores collected at 98% efficiency, 15% growth over last year
items.quote: In Noida, we had sold out all the inventories in March '23. The collections are better than planned. We have a 98% collection efficiency, totally collected so far INR394 crores, 15% growth over last year.

items.statement: Noida Authority kept occupancy certificate in abeyance; writ petition filed in Allahabad High Court
items.quote: While we're ready for position, unfortunately, as some of you know, we have made the application of the occupancy certificate. It's been kept in abeyance by the authority waiting for the larger ambiguity around Sector-150 being sorted out.

items.statement: Appellate Authority ruled in favor for Noida Phase 2 RERA registration; RERA directed to review application
items.quote: On Phase 2 of Sector-150, where there was earlier a setback from RERA, we had taken the issue up with the Appellate Authority, very pleased to inform you that the authority has ruled in the favor of the developer company, advised RERA to review the application for r egistration of Phase II and give a reasoned order

items.statement: Noida Phase 2 launch delayed but will sell at far higher price points than Phase 1
items.quote: While there will be a delay in the launch of Phase II, the silver lining is the market con tinues to grow, and therefore, the price point at which it will start selling is far, far, far higher than Noida Phase 1 price point

items.statement: Dehradun operational revenue INR24.5 crores (12% YoY growth); community operations profitable INR1 crore, 2 years ahead of plan
items.quote: The operational revenue from Dehradun increased to about INR24.5 crores for FY '25, a growth of 12% over corresponding last year. Very pleased to inform you again the community operations has now reported a profit of INR 1 crore 2 years ahead of our plan, is now operationally cash positive and profitable as well.

items.statement: New Gurugram project with Max Estates: 1 million sq ft senior living, launch expected Q2 FY26
items.quote: The project launch is expected to be in Q2 FY '26. Also actively pursuing the Chandigarh opportunity, the definitive agreements have been agreed with, expected to be executed soon.

items.statement: Chandigarh project: 1.01 million sq ft, 374 units, launch Q4 FY26; will exceed 1.5 million sq ft annual development target
items.quote: The groundwork has begun for our project launch in Q4 '26. This is a 1.01 million square feet development with 374 units. With that, we'll be far higher than the promised 1.5 million square feet development every year.

items.statement: Antara Assisted Care net revenue INR65.2 crores FY25 (2-3x YoY); Q4 FY25 INR23.5 crores (22% QoQ, 2.7x YoY); crossed INR100 crores annual run rate
items.quote: For Antara Assisted Care, the revenue -- overall net revenue, INR65.2 crores, a growth of 2 to 3x over last year. During Q4 '25, net revenue was INR23.5 crores. It grew by 22% sequentially over Q3 FY '25 and a year-on-year growth of 2.7x.

items.statement: Care Homes: 234 beds added FY25 (98 Gurgaon, 83 Bangalore, 53 Noida, 43 Chennai, 150 under fit-outs); targeting ~500 beds
items.quote: We added 234 beds, 98 in Sector 24, Gurgaon, 83 in Bannerghatta, Bangalore, 53 in Noida, 43 operationalized in Chennai in May '25, and 150 beds under fit-outs expected to be operational over the next 3 months.

items.statement: Care Homes net revenue INR7.6 crores FY25 (38% YoY); Q4 FY25 INR2.3 crores (14% QoQ, 66% YoY); served 240 patients Q4, 2,250 since inception
items.quote: On financial performance for Care Homes, net revenue of INR7.6 crores in FY '25, a year-on-year growth of 38%. During Q4 FY '25, net revenue of INR2.3 crores with a sequential growth of 14% over Q3 FY '25 and a year-on-year growth of 66%.

items.statement: Care at Home FY25 revenue INR17.3 crores (86% YoY); Q4 INR4.6 crores (52% YoY); contribution margin 14% (from 9%), NCR margin 25% (from 19%); Chennai breakeven Q4
items.quote: We've also increased the penetration of high-margin services like critical care and physiotherapy. We have now achieved the highest ever revenue of INR17.3 crores in FY '25 with a strong year-on-year growth of 86% led by the high-margin service offerings.

items.statement: AGEasy net revenue INR40.4 crores FY25 (3.6x YoY); Q4 INR16.6 crores (30% QoQ, 4x YoY); crossed INR75 crores annual run rate
items.quote: On AGEasy which includes the erstwhile MedCare business, it achieved the highest-ever net revenue of INR40.4 crores in FY '25, a strong year-on-year growth of 3.6x. During Q4 FY '25, the net revenue was INR16.6 crores and Q4 FY '25, the sequential growth of 30% over Q3 FY '25 and a year-on-year growth of 4x.

items.statement: AGEasy monthly revenue rate grew from INR52 lakhs (Jun 24) to INR3.6 crores (Mar 25); 8x growth in daily revenue rate on Amazon with sharp ROAS improvement
items.quote: The AGEasy monthly revenue rate has grown from INR52 lakhs in June '24 to INR1.3 crores in September, INR3 crores in December '24 and INR3.6 crores in March '25. So overall, an 8x growth in daily revenue rate on Amazon with sharp improvement in the return on advertising spend, or ROAS, as we call it.

items.statement: Initiated imports from China improving cost of goods by 20%; will explore more products once supply chain stabilizes
items.quote: We've initiated imports from China, as you know, which has improved our cost of goods by 20%, which hopefully will flow through margin as well. Once we are able to stabilize this supply chain, we'll explore other products from China as well.

items.statement: Partnerships with BOAT (tech), Dr Lal PathLabs (diagnostics), Wellbeing Nutrition (nutraceuticals), Axis Bank (Silver Linings), Axis Max Life (annuity), IIT Delhi (innovation)
items.quote: We also partnered with Dr Lal PathLabs, a leading diagnostics player to lau nch customized geriatric packages for seniors to strengthen our geriatric care services. The pack age has been created based on our learnings and their

items.statement: Consolidated FY25 revenue INR164 crores (16% lower); Q4 FY25 INR46 crores (16% QoQ); EBITDA loss INR37.2 crores Q4 (vs INR24.7 crores) due to marketing spend for Assisted Care growth
items.quote: Consol revenue at INR164 crores for FY '25, 16% lower, which I've been telling you over the last few calls, that as we launch more residential communities, this will keep on going up, but as gone up, it's also healthy because of the higher revenue in AGEasy and strong growth in Care Home and Care at Home.

items.statement: Treasury and monetizable assets INR250 crores (Mar 25); net worth INR359 crores; raised INR124.23 crores rights issue + INR105 crores Max Towers sale
items.quote: Overall, our treasury and other monetizable assets stood at a healthy number of INR250 crores as of March '25. The company's consolidated net worth stands at INR359 crores of March '25. In addition, we have successfully has now raised about INR124.23 crores, have also monetized the sale of three towers about INR105 crores in Max Towers.

items.statement: Planning Fundraise 2 in latter part of year to fund ambitious senior living growth

items.statement: Export benefits INR454 million in FY25 offset by 5.77% countervailing duty on US sales linked to those benefits
items.quote: Please, you also have to keep in mind with regard to our sales in U.S.A., we are also paying 5.77% as our countervailing duty, which is mainly being levied on us because of these so called export benefits, okay?

items.statement: No major investment planned for FY26 except power backup and efficiency improvements to reduce energy costs
items.quote: Right now, there are no plans for additional investment, except for some power backup systems and all that more to look on efficiency factors to improvise the efficiency and the cost with regard to reducing energy costs.

items.statement: RTE share dropped to 10% of volume in FY25 from 16% in FY24 due to lack of EU market access
items.quote: The share of current year. Of course, current year, it has dropped down to 10%. Last year, it was 16%, on a volume terms.

items.statement: Cautiously optimistic due to US tariff uncertainties; expect clarity by end of June or early July; tariffs affect global consumption patterns beyond US
items.quote: We are very positive. We remain optimistic on the part of the trade talks, but end of the day, we should see how the results will come out because we do notice every day, every week, we understand that the talks between India and U.S. are very positive, and they are looking forward for an early agreement, but at the same time, we can't be on a high optimism as such because we also have to be a lit

items.statement: Legacy provisions for hatchery debtors cleared over past 2 years; impacted profitability in FY23-25
items.quote: The company had been having some provisioning, which has been done for some legacy-related issues like earlier, some like hatchery debtors and all that, they were - some of them were also there, which were also creating an overall issue for the company.

items.statement: Shrimp sales volume 2,349 MT in Q4 FY25 (2% YoY growth); 10,534 MT in FY25 vs 10,949 MT in FY24
items.quote: Shrimp sales grew 2% year-on-year to 2,349 metric tons in Q4 FY '25 as against 2,302 metric tons in Q4 FY 24. For FY '25, it stood at 10,534 metric tons as against 10,949 metric tons in FY '24.

items.statement: Management acknowledges loss of some US customers to Ecuador in FY23-24; regained customers and diversified to EU
items.quote: we did lose some of our customers to -- for a brief period, at least for a year like 2 years ago, which has also has happened in 23 and a little bit in carly 24, which we have been gaining them back

items.statement: Revenue guidance for FY26 is INR 250 crores, implying 20-25% growth over FY25, excluding Shotgun contribution
items.quote: my revenue guidance for this financial year is about INR 250 crores

items.statement: Targets 15-20% CAGR year-on-year growth over the next few years
items.quote: We're looking to grow at a CAGR of 15% to 20% year-on-year

items.statement: Saw robust recovery in Q1 FY26 and expects it to continue
items.quote: With respect to demand, we've seen a robust recovery in Q1, and we see that continuing this year as well going forward

items.statement: Gross margins improved 200 bps YoY to ~79% in FY25 driven by product mix and operational efficiencies
items.quote: Gross margins improved by 200 basis points year -on-year driven by an enhanced product mix and operational efficiencies

items.statement: Capex for FY26 expected under INR 15 crores for routine efficiency improvements, down from ~INR 40 crores in FY25; excludes hospitality project
items.quote: We expect that number for this financial year to be under INR15 -odd crores for this fina ncial year. So nothing major. Last year, we were approximately INR40-odd crores that we spent

items.statement: Total installed capacity increased by one-third to 5.4 million liters in FY25 (Akluj 4.8M + Bijapur 0.6M)
items.quote: This year, we've increased our total installed capacity by one third , bringing it to 5.4 million liters

items.statement: New vineyard plantation of ~100 acres at Jambhali underway; 40 acres planted so far; viable yield expected in 3 years
items.quote: Typically, it takes about 3 years for us to get a viable yield out of any new plantation. So this capex is underway in a place called Jambhali in Ahmednagar district, where we have already planted approximately 40 acres. The net planting area we will get in this land is about 100 acres

items.statement: TiLT available pan-India; Shotgun launched in Maharashtra, Kerala, West Bengal, Uttar Pradesh; targeting 10+ states by end of FY26
items.quote: With respect to Shotgun, we are already available in the states of Maharashtra, Kerala, West Bengal and Uttar Pradesh. And we will be looking to be available in 10-plus states by end of this

items.statement: Working capital constitutes two-thirds of INR 100 crore borrowings
items.quote: out of which two third is the working capital and one third is the term debt

items.statement: Hospitality project (tourism facility) still in planning stage; targeting opening in 2027
items.quote: We are still in planning stage. We haven't yet begun construction. We are still very much attempting to have the facility ready by and open in 2027

items.statement: Expanded team and onboarded new talent in FY25 to build capabilities for future growth
items.quote: We continue to strengthen internal capabilities throughout this year, onboarding new talent, expanding the team and laying the groundwork for future growth

items.statement: Shareholder approval received for capital raise up to Rs. 750 crores; rights issue planned in Q2 FY26 with promoter participation
items.quote: We have received shareholder approval for capital raise during March for up to Rs. 750 crores. The Board Committe e has been formed to oversee this capital raise, including a possible righ ts issue in Q2 FY '26

items.statement: Targeting ~20% AUM growth in FY26 from current base of Rs. 6,819 crores
items.quote: I think we can look at about 20% kind of the growth from the current base. That's the number that will work out.

items.statement: Disbursements in FY26 expected to be roughly equal to AUM size given second-half skew
items.quote: I think the disbursement number will also be in line with roughly about the AUM size only.

items.statement: Loan officer productivity target of 340 borrowers per LO by end of FY26 from current 228
items.quote: Our target in current financial year will be to improve borrowers to LO count to about 340 borrowers from the current 228 number.

items.statement: Loan officer productivity target of Rs. 1.1 crores per LO by end of FY26 from Rs. 0.6 crores currently
items.quote: We would like to increase productivity and efficiencies at branches and expect to improve our loan officer productivity to about Rs. 1.1 crores per loan officer by end of FY '26 from the current Rs. 0.6 crores at end of FY '25.

items.statement: X-bucket collection efficiency improved to 98.9% in March 2025 (ex-Karnataka), up from 98% in December
items.quote: Spandana had witnessed improvement in key lead indicators in March and our X-bucket collection efficiency at the end of March 2025 improved to 98.9% if I exclude Karnataka out of it.

items.statement: Current X-bucket collection efficiency trending at ~97% overall in April-May (97.8% ex-Karnataka)
items.quote: However, April and May there has been a slight blip. We are presently trending at about 97% and thereabouts on the current bucket or X bucket.

items.statement: Borrowers with 4+ lender exposure reduced from 23% in Feb 2025 to ~20% currently
items.quote: We have been consistently seeing an improving trend in the lender overlap as well. About 23% of borrowers had exposure to four or more lenders, including Spandana, in February 2025, which has now reduced to about 20%.

items.statement: Recoveries from GNPA/90+ buckets including write-off pool were Rs. 52 crores in Q4 FY25 vs Rs. 44 crores in first three quarters; FY25 total Rs. 96 crores
items.quote: Overall, we were able to recover Rs. 96 crores during FY '25.

items.statement: Standalone GNPA 4.85% and NNPA 0.96% at end FY25; maintaining 80% PCR
items.quote: The standalone GNPA at the end of FY '25 was 4.85%, an increase of 3.4% over FY 24. Standalone NNPA was at 0.96%, an increase of 0.7% over FY '24.

items.statement: Credit costs expected to normalize in H2 FY26; elevated in H1 due to Stage 2 flows
items.quote: However, in the second half of the financial year, we are positive that these numbers would start normalizing.

items.statement: 51% of existing borrowers qualify for new loans under stricter credit rules; 34% have some negative flags but 96% current with Spandana
items.quote: Of our existing borrower base, at the end of March 2025, about 51% of the borrowers qualify for new loan under the stricter credit rules that we have adopted internally.

items.statement: LAP and Nano loans subsidiary Criss Financial AUM crossed Rs. 200 crores, closed FY25 at Rs. 233 crores with 99.6% collection efficiency
items.quote: The AUM under these products crossed Rs. 200 crores for the first time. And we closed the financial year with Rs. 233 crores AUM under these product lines.

items.statement: Weekly model branches (14% of business) deliver 99.3% X-bucket collection efficiency vs 98.9% overall; will continue growing weekly portfolio
items.quote: We have about 14% of our business in weekly branches. And we would obviously grow that portfolio given the portfolio quality is definitely better than what we see in monthly branches.

items.statement: Covenant breaches total Rs. 438 crores (Rs. 260 cr capital markets, Rs. 178 cr term lending); waivers obtained, not constraining growth
items.quote: The number stacks up presently at Rs. 438 crores in total where Rs. 260 crores is from the capital markets and about Rs. 178 crores from the term lending side.

items.statement: Borrowed Rs. 4,482 crores in FY25; marginal cost of borrowings 11.9% in Q4 (up 20 bps YoY and QoQ); bank share 57% of borrowings
items.quote: During the year, we borrowed Rs. 4,482 crores. The borrowings were calibrated, keeping in view the disbursement and the organization's liquidity requirements.

items.statement: Yield down 1.7% YoY to 22.5%; NIM down 1.3% YoY to 12.8% due to lower yield and higher marginal cost of borrowings
items.quote: on the portfolio was down by 1.7% year-on-year to 22.5%. Yield declined by 41 bps over the previous quarter. NIM for the year was at 12.8%, down by 1.3% year-on-year

items.statement: No plan to increase borrower pricing; NIM improvement to come from cost of funds reduction
items.quote: I don't see a need or a reason right now to look at the pricing at the borrower level.

items.statement: Liquidity position over Rs. 2,000 crores (24% of assets) at end March 2025
items.quote: Our liquidity position at the end of March 2025 were over Rs. 2,000 crores, which is about 24% of our assets on our balance sheet.

items.statement: Adopted credit rules beyond Guardrail 2 in Jan 2025; SRO deferred Guardrail 2 implementation to April 1, 2025
items.quote: While Spandana adopted credit rules confirming to the Guardrail 2 and even going beyond in January of 2025, the deferment of Guardrail 2 implementation by SRO to 1st of April 2025 prompted us to rationalize our disbursements in Q4.

items.statement: Field attrition 56% in FY25; added branch quality managers and 700 dedicated collection officers for 90+ DPD buckets
items.quote: The increased stress resulted in elevated attrition at the field level. And taking cognizance of these issues, we have increased the bench strength, which had impacted the efficiencies in the interim.

items.statement: CEO search underway; Board evaluating internal and external candidates for long-term strategic fit
items.quote: the Board will do what is in the best interest of the organization and they wi ll definitely follow an approach which is comprehensive, probably evaluating both internal and external candidates to see who fits the need

items.statement: No forensic audit conducted; RBI routine audit only with suggestions for improvement being complied with
items.quote: I would like to re iterate that there has been no forensic audit on the company whatsoever.

items.statement: Operational risk from cash collections increased industry-wide in Q2-Q3 FY25; reinforcing controls via branch quality managers, increased audit frequency
items.quote: Spandana too faced these issues during the 2nd, 3rd Quarter of the financial year. However, we are continuously working to reinforce control mechanisms through measures such as increased headcount on branch quality managers, increasing internal audit frequencies and coverage, etc.

items.statement: North India AUM share increased to 22% from 13% in FY22; maintaining geographical diversification
items.quote: North India now contributes about 22% of the AUM as against 13% in FY '22. We continue to maintain our spread going forward.

items.statement: Capital adequacy 37%, gearing 2.1x, liquidity ~Rs. 2,000 crores; comfortably placed for growth
items.quote: We are comfortably placed in terms of capital adequacy at 37% and close to Rs. 2,000 crores in liquidity. Our gearing at 2.1x is also accommodative of future growth.

items.statement: Aadhaar e-KYC via NPCI e-Setu (face recognition + OTP) being implemented; no AUA/KUA license yet
items.quote: We are working with the NPCI and others for the e-Setu piece, where we will be able to do this much more smoothly. It will be Aadhaar-based customer identification where other than the OTP, there will also be a face recognition that we will use.

items.statement: Management expects revenue growth of 8-10% annually and PBT margin around 15% over the medium term.
items.quote: As the Director of Finance has brought out, we expect the revenue growth of anywhere between 8% to 10% and our PBT margins we expect around 15%.

items.statement: Current order book is Rs 32,260 crore; expected to exceed Rs 1.25 lakh crore upon signing P-75 additional and P-75(I) submarine contracts.
items.quote: We are expecting the P-75 additional submarines and the P-75(I) submarines contract to be signed in this financial year. And that is expected to increase our order book from the present Rs. 32,000 crore to more than Rs. 1.25 lakh crores.

items.statement: P-75 additional submarine contract value estimated at Rs 30,000-40,000 crore; signing expected as early as next month.
items.quote: Yes, it's expected to be in the range of anywhere between 30,000 crores to 40,000 crores.

items.statement: FY25 EBITDA margin 28.24% vs 26.93% in FY24; Q4 EBITDA margin 13.74% due to Rs 532 crore provision for two loss-making contracts.
items.quote: The operating profit is Rs. 1,940.43 crores giving an operating percentage of 16.97% and PBT to revenue is 27.2 % against 26 % which we reported last year and the EBITDA margin of 28.24% against 26.93% reported in last year.

items.statement: Rs 532 crore provision made in FY25 for potential losses on Coast Guard FPV and Denmark contracts; will be reviewed quarterly.
items.quote: Actually in my opening remark I mentioned that other than 532 crores which is we have made a provision this year, others are normal business provisions. This 532 crores we are making as an estimate for a loss which we may incur in our two of the contracts.

items.statement: Capex of approximately Rs 4,000 crore planned for Nhava yard and newly acquired port land to augment capacity.
items.quote: we have also taken up l and from the port for taking up small ships and we are also doing having major CAPEX plans in that land as well as in the N hava yard which we have which we have a CAPEX of approximately Rs. 4,000 crores

items.statement: Capacity augmented from 6 to 11 submarines; can construct 10 major warships and 11 submarines simultaneously; capacity expected to at least double when capex programs operational.
items.quote: We have already augmented our capacity from construction of 6 submarines to 11 submarines because we are preparing to take both the additional submarines of 75 and the six P-75(I) for which we have already set up the SSA facility or the submarine section assembly workshop.

items.statement: No debt planned for capex; healthy balance sheet with Rs 11,000-12,000 crore cash (Rs 6,000 crore margin money, rest advances).
items.quote: As of now, we are having quite healthy Balance Sheet and we do not expect, but it will be based on the economic performance, we will see.

items.statement: FY25 revenue Rs 11,432 crore (+2% YoY); Q4 revenue Rs 3,174 crore; FY26 revenue growth guided at 8-10% (later revised to 10-15%).
items.quote: This year we have recorded the highest revenue from operations which is Rs. 11, 432 crores and the profit before tax is Rs. 3,109 crores.

items.statement: Coast Guard FPV and Denmark contracts together worth ~Rs 3,500 crore; deliveries extend to FY30.
items.quote: That will be put together around Rs. 3,500 crores.

items.statement: Order book ~2/3 fixed-price with reasonably high margins (P-15B, P-17A, P-75 ~Rs 20,000 crore); rest fixed-price with lower margins.
items.quote: So approximately Rs. 20,000 crores projects on fixed cost and the rest are also fixed cost but they are with the lesser margins.

items.statement: Diversifying beyond MOD: ONGC orders ~Rs 6,500 crore; commercial export order for multipurpose vessel ~Rs 715 crore with option for 4 more.
items.value: Rs 6,500 crore ONGC; Rs 715 crore export
items.quote: We have already got a significant amount of contracts from the offshore segment from ONGC. Our order book from ONGC is approximately Rs. 6,500 crores and from commercial shipbuilding is the multipurpose vessel which we have got from a European client which is approximately Rs. 715 crores.

items.statement: Subcontracting/outsourcing costs increased due to 27 ships under simultaneous construction; executing work outside premises is costlier than in-house.
items.quote: So because we have around 27 ships to be built simultaneously, some of this work will have to be executed outside. Now at the same time we are unable to give the entire ship outside. So these blocks have to be transported. Transportation cost is also involved. So therefore there is an increase compared to executing the work within our premises.

items.statement: Raw material costs locked in at early procurement stages; staggered deliveries to control inventory and cost.
items.quote: We do the procurement and the negotiations with the supplier at the early stages. However, we ensure that the delivery is staggered so that the inventory is controlled and the costs are minimal to the shipyard.

items.statement: P-75(I) submarine project: >60% indigenous content (vs Scorpene); technology transfer from ThyssenKrupp; potential export orders for TKMS to be built at MDL.
items.quote: There will be more than 60% of indigenous content in this submarine, much higher than what we have done for the Scorpene project. Yes, please go ahead.

items.statement: No compensation for contract signing delays; provisions for liquidated damages on P-75 submarines partially reversed (4 of 5 boats), first boat reversal expected this FY.
items.quote: If the signing of the contract get delayed, we don't get any additional compensation for it.

items.statement: Master Ship Repair Agreement with US Navy signed; only small subset of fleet can be accommodated due to draft limitations; no immediate commercial contribution expected.
items.quote: So we are still one of the contenders. So the issue is, the vessels t hat are coming for repairs, some of them are large and it will not fit into our current infrastructure. So w e will participate that signed agreement only for projects which can be accommodated within our premises

items.statement: Goa Shipyard listing decision rests with DIPAM/MOD (Govt holds 51%, MDL 47%); MDL will remain shareholder per government decision.
items.quote: Actually, this is the decision of DIPAM because we are just a shareholder based on the government guidelines, and we are not making a decision for their listing or not. That will be decided by DIPAM and MOD as per their intention and we will continue to be their shareholder, as per the decision of the MOD.

items.statement: Next Generation Corvette order awarded to GRSE and GSL, not MDL.
items.quote: The bids were opened and I think it's gone to GRSE and GSL and not to MDL.

items.statement: Out of Rs 32,000 crore order book, ~Rs 24,000 crore expected to be invoiced over next two years.
items.quote: Out of the 32,000 crores, may be almost 24,000 across the next two years.

items.statement: P-75 additional submarine revenue expected to contribute at least 10% of contract value in FY28; preparatory work already commenced.
items.quote: Yes, you could say that because this P-75 AS project is a repeat of the Scorpene P-75 project which have already delivered to the Navy and we have already commenced some kind of a preparatory work. So I think confidently we can say yes, it will contribute at least 10% of the order book of 75 AS, contract value of 75 AS will come in as a revenue for FY'28.

items.statement: Upcoming RFPs: P-17 Bravo frigates (Rs 70,000 crore) and MCMV (Rs 44,000 crore) likely in coming months; MDL well positioned for both.
items.quote: both the Navy is likely to come out with the RFP for the 17 Bravo frigates shortly, which is a 70,000 crore project. And we are poised best to take on that although it is going to come on a competitive bidding but MDL with its proven capability and infrastructure and having demonstrated to have cons tructed and delivered these ships profitably we are best placed to actually win these contracts. In

items.statement: Early stages of examining tie-ups with global shipyards (e.g., Korean) under Ministry of Shipping's cluster development plan; options open for good business opportunities.
items.quote: We are in the very early stages of examining this, but we will keep our options open wherever we are presented with good business opportunity.

items.statement: Global shipbuilding margins ~15%; MDL's recent 26-27% PBT margin driven by late-stage high-margin projects (P-15B deliveries); prudent to guide ~15%.
items.quote: See, if you look worldwide, the shipbuilding margins are approximately 15%. So the guidance of 15% is accurate. But what we must understand that in shipbuilding, revenues and profits are directly correlated to the order book and the life cycle stages of current projects.

items.statement: FY26 revenue growth expected 8-10% (CFO) to 10-15% (CFO later); large submarine orders need design finalization before revenue ramps up.
items.quote: You have seen a growth of 20% on a year-to-year basis, but that was a time when we had a steady order book. Since the order book for new P-75 and P-75(I) is little bit delayed, so some time will be going towards the design and finalization of the basic parameters for their execution. So it may not be correct to say that this 20% will be maintained. But by and large we will see that the growth of t

items.statement: P-15B and P-75 delivered projects have Rs 3,700 crore and Rs 2,700 crore backlog for guarantee liabilities and base/depot spares; to be liquidated by FY27-28.
items.quote: So if you see 15 Bravo, we have 3,716 has been shown, so there also the liabilities are not yet over. So we keep that for future contingencies if any because depending on the operational needs of the ship we need to, some expenditure has to be incurred. So 2 to 3 ships are still under guarantee.

items.statement: B2C biscuit and bakery revenue growth guided at low to mid-teens for FY26, back-ended with H1 slower
items.quote: On the B2C side, the business of Biscuit and Bakery together, we have a guidance that for this year, what it looks like B2C business, we will be growing kind of low to mid-teens kind of stuff.

items.statement: Export biscuit revenue growth guided at mid-teens for FY26
items.quote: very confident that in exports, we should be able to grow mid-teens kind of growth in this financial year.

items.statement: Domestic biscuit revenue growth guided at low teens for FY26, back-ended
items.quote: on a full year basis, again, I expect mid to -- low to mid-teen kind of growth on a domestic side.

items.statement: Bakery revenue growth guided at mid to high teens for FY26
items.quote: So Bakery business for the current financial year '26, we expect it to grow somewhere mid to high teens.

items.statement: EBITDA margin recovery to 13-14% range targeted for full year FY26, normalization expected by end of Q3
items.quote: Our endeavor is that. Absolutely, our endeavor is that, that we kind of achieve that on a full year basis.

items.statement: Margin normalization expected to take 6-9 months (until end of Q3 FY26) due to calibrated price hikes and commodity tailwinds
items.quote: it would take about 6 to 9 months' time as it looks like now for us to get into the full margin recovery

items.statement: Capex cycle to wind down considerably from FY27 as Khopoli and Calcutta projects complete in FY26
items.quote: our capex cycle will start coming down considerably from FY '27.

items.statement: New product development (NPD) revenue contribution target of ~5% for FY26 from recently launched and upcoming differentiated products
items.quote: we are targeting to get close to 5% of our revenue. That's our target. So we want to get close to 5% of our revenue contribution coming out of NPD.

items.statement: Launched premium differentiated products: 25% butter shortbread cookies, Teddies animal crackers, English Oven ready-to-eat muffins/brownies, Zero Maida Pav, NaturBaked clean-label range; pipeline focused on differentiated not me-too produc
items.quote: we have clearly decided that we will stay away by our innovation bucket over the next few years. We will stay more on a differentiated product rather than me-too product.

items.statement: Rural consumption recovering steadily; mild uptrading in low MRP packs; urban demand expected to improve from tax slab revisions
items.quote: we are encouraged by a steady recovery in rural consumption. We are also witnessing mild uptrading within low MRP packs as consumers increasingly opt for higher-value offering.

items.statement: Export biscuit volume contribution 50-53% of total biscuit volume in FY25; potential tariff changes create uncertainty but global partnerships remain strong
items.quote: it's a 50% to 53% kind of range.

items.statement: Long-term contracts cover 75-80% of wheat/flour needs; buying timed at harvest (Apr-May) for best prices; palm oil ~17-20% of biscuit RM basket
items.quote: We end up doing long contracts, which are -- where we would cover around 75% to 80% of the material, depending on the quality of the flour we need.

items.statement: Board recommended final dividend of INR 3 per equity share for FY25 subject to AGM approval
items.quote: the Board has recommended a final dividend of INR 3 per equity share subject to approval of the shareholders at the upcoming AGM of the company.

items.statement: Potential tariff changes announced end of Q4 create uncertainty for export portfolio
items.quote: towards the end of Q4, the announcement of potential tariff changes introduced a degree of uncertai nty in the external environment

items.statement: IT infrastructure revamp underway with ERP upgrade and AI/ML integration for smarter operations; manufacturing and supply chain digitization expected to yield benefits in coming years
items.quote: We are undertaking a complete revamp of our IT infrastructure, with a key focus on upgrading our core ERP system supported by AI and ML integration to drive smarter, faster and more connected operations.

items.statement: Guides 20-25% CAGR on core revenue over 5 years, not year-on-year
items.quote: So we have been guiding at 20%-25% CAGR growth on our core revene, not a year-on-year growth.

items.statement: Expects core EBITDA margin to move towards 22-23% over next 2-3 quarters
items.quote: No, actually the core EBITDA margin will move towards 22%-23%.

items.statement: Order book of Rs 8,300 cr; 58% long tail expiring by 2040, balance over next 12 years
items.quote: So of the Rs. 8,300 crores, on a percentage basis, close to 58% is having a long tail which will expire by 2040. The balance would be executed over the next 12 years.

items.statement: Bulk of processing capex at fag-end; no significant capex foreseen in existing processing contracts post monsoon
items.quote: So bulk of our CAPEX at our processing units are almost at the fa g-end of our life. So I would say the core EBITDA margins and the reported EBITDA margins should kind of merge over the next 2-3 quarters.

items.statement: PCMC WTE plant achieved ~90% PLF in Q4 FY25, up from 76% in Q3; FY25 average ~82%
items.quote: The company's waste to energy facility in PCMC delivered exceptional operational performance, achieving a remarkable plant load factor of approximately 90%, a significant increase from 76% in the preceding quarter.

items.statement: C&D plant at Dahisar processing 250-300 TPD, ramping to 600-700 TPD in next 6 months; design capacity 700 TPD
items.quote: we handled around 250-300 tons per day for the last 4 months. And the average realization would be around Rs. 1,405 per ton. That is our trend. So we expect that in the next 6 months, this number of 250-300 tons per day kind of processing will increase to 600-700 tons.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 total tonnage 1.36 mn tons (+20% YoY); FY25 total MSW 4.93 mn tons (+6% YoY)
items.quote: Over the course of FY '25, we managed total MSW volume of about 4.93 million tons, reflecting a 6% year-on-year growth.

items.statement: C&D tipping fee Rs 1,405/ton; escalation sticky but expected to be made up with approvals
items.quote: Escalation, which is a part of business, has been slightly sticky in the last period, which we feel can be made -up with the appropriate approvals coming in time.

items.statement: FY25 RDF sales ~148,000 tons, compost ~21,200 tons; both up sharply YoY
items.quote: For the full fiscal year, RDF sales increased to about 1,48,000 tons and compos t sales nearly doubled to around 21 ,200 tons compared to 1,46,000 tons and 10,000 tons effectively in the previous year.

items.statement: Bid submitted for 5 WTE tenders (3 South, 1 West, 2 more in progress); bidding for 8 Mumbai C&T packages + 1 South package
items.quote: When it comes to processing projects, we have already submitted 3 waste to energy tenders, 2 in the South and 1 in the Western part of the country and 2 more waste to energy projects we are currently working on the tenders.

items.statement: Advanced talks with large Indian corporate for MSW-to-steam captive project (non-municipal)
items.quote: As we speak, we are in the advanced stage of discussion with a very large Indian corporate to set-up a municipal solid waste to steam project.

items.statement: Bombay HC set aside Kanjurmarg denotification; BMC to restore forest status in 3 months; State/BMC to appeal to SC; concession rights protected
items.quote: On 2nd May 2025, Bombay High Court set aside the 2009 denotification of approximately 120 hectares at the Kanjurmarg Landfills, thereby restoring its status as a protected forest under the Forest Conservation Act 1980 and the Indian Forest Act 1927.

items.statement: Gross debt Rs 473 cr, cash Rs 132 cr, net debt Rs 341 cr (net D/E 0.4x); WACD ~9.1%; DSO stable at 101 days
items.quote: As of March '25, the group's gross debt stood at approximately Rs. 473 crores with cash and bank balances of around Rs. 132 crores, resulting in net debt of approximately Rs. 341 crores.

items.statement: VGF: Rs 45 cr of Rs 50 cr received, used to retire debt; balance Rs 5 cr due in 6 months
items.quote: So out of the Rs. 50 crores, we have received Rs. 45 crores of the VGF funds and the same has been used to retire debt and provide collateral to the lender. The balance Rs. 5 crores is due in the next 6 months' time.

items.statement: Cash flow from operations post tax up 34% YoY to Rs 187 cr; DSO stable at 101 days
