items.quote: For FY '25, our revenue from operations stood at INR1,486 crores against INR1,370 crores in FY '24, showing a growth of 8.41% and EBITDA for the year stood at INR110 crores.

items.statement: Revenue target INR3,300 crore for FY26, INR5,500 crore for FY27, INR8,500 crore for FY28
items.quote: We expect the said expansion to increase our top line , hence our aspiration is INR3,000 crores plus in FY26, INR5,500 crores plus in FY27 and INR8,500 crores plus in FY28.

items.statement: PAT target INR300 crore for FY26, INR700 crore for FY27, INR1,300 crore for FY28
items.quote: We also expect margin accretion resulting in increase in profit after tax, hence our target for the same is 300 plus in FY26, 700 plus in FY27 and 1,300 plus in FY28.

items.statement: PAT margin guidance 11.1% for FY26, 14.01% for FY27, 16% for FY28
items.quote: In our earnings presentation, we have again given a guidance that our PAT margins will be close to 11.1%. So, there is again a margin expansion of 150 basis points. For FY26-FY27, again we have given a guidance of a margin expansion of 250 basis points from 11.1% to 14.01%.

items.statement: Unit 3 Jaipur 3 GW module line 80% complete, operational in 4-6 weeks
items.quote: 80% of this Unit 3 construction work is already completed and we expect it to operationalize within next 4 to 6 weeks.

items.statement: Narmadapuram MP expansion: 4 GW module, 3 GW cell, 54,000 MT aluminium frame; land secured, machinery orders placed, construction start Q1FY26, cell ops H1FY27
items.quote: we are setting up a 4-gigawatt solar module, 3-gigawatt solar cell and 54,000 metric ton aluminium frame capacity expansion in Narmadapuram, MP where we have already secured possession of the land and machinery orders have been placed very soon and we expect to start construction by Q1FY26 and begin operations of our 3-gigawatt solar cell line by H1FY27.

items.statement: Cell line capex ~INR1,300 crore; funding INR300 crore internal accruals, INR1,000 crore debt at <9% (SBI, BOB) and ~9.25% (IREDA, PFC, REC)
items.quote: Out of INR1,300 crores, INR300 crores is from internal accrual and INR1,000 crores is from debt. We are in advanced discussion with four banks and two institutions. They are giving us green signal to move and they are ready to fund this amount.

items.statement: Module capacity 950 MW (Mono PERC) currently; Unit 3 adds 3 GW TOPCon; full 4 GW TOPCon by Sep 2025
items.quote: Currently in our unit 1 and unit 2 we have 950 megawatts of the Mono PERC manufacturing capacity and unit 3 is 3000 megawatts that is completely TOPCon N-type and we also transfer our unit 1 and unit 2 to TOPCon facility within next three months.

items.statement: Cell production line 3 GW single phase, ramp up by Jan 2027, full facility 15-18 months
items.quote: No, no. It's a single project. The complete line will be 3 -gigawatt and will be ramped up and installed in one phase only.

items.statement: Consolidated order book INR2,500 crore+ across channel, government, rooftop, EPC, developer contracts
items.quote: Our company is having a strong order book of INR2,500 crores plus on consolidated basis across all verticals including channel partners, government scheme, rooftop solar, EPC and developers contracts.

items.statement: KUSUM pipeline: 130 MW RREC secured, bidding 700+ MW Component A, expect 350+ MW win
items.quote: We have already secured 130 megawatts of the RREC, means Rajasthan Renewable Energy Corporation tender at the government buildings in the Rajasthan. The second one is our KUSUM Component A and KUSUM Component C. And other than this we are already tendering for KUSUM Component A 700 plus megawatts which might be open within this month only.

items.statement: Rooftop EPC pipeline 100+ MW execution in FY26
items.quote: Our rooftop projects vertical focuses on installing rooftop solar modules for various corporate and state government rooftop tenders. It is gaining momentum with 100 plus megawatt pipeline being executed in FY26.

items.statement: FY25 EBITDA margin 12.8% (+140 bps YoY); PAT margin 9.5%
items.quote: EBITDA has been increased by 103% to INR170 crores in FY25 due to improved business mix and strategic cost optimization measures. We saw benefit of scale occurring to our EBITDA resulting in margin increase of 140 bps to 12.8%.

items.statement: EPC/KUSUM margins slightly higher than module manufacturing; EPC revenue INR400 cr FY26, INR700 cr FY27
items.quote: The margins in this KUSUM and EPC business are slightly higher than our module manufacturing business. And the revenue contribution is already we have envisaged in our ending call presentation. It is INR400 crores out of INR3300 crores in the current financial year.

items.statement: Dealer/distribution margins 2-5% better than large project supplies; dealer mix 15-20% of revenue
items.quote: Definitely, the margins are better in the dealer-distribution network and the retail network than the big project supplies and that should be difference somewhere around 2%-5%.

items.statement: Robust demand across all segments driving volume growth and capacity utilization
items.quote: There is robust demand for solar modules across the country, across the segments. So this is the main reason, and we have utilized our capacities.

items.statement: Working capital cycle 31 days in FY25 vs 44 days FY24; improved via better payment terms and dealer network focus
items.quote: Our working capital day cycle stands at 31 days in FY25. The working capital days in FY25 was lower as compared to 44 days in FY24 due to better payment terms negotiated on both sides, payables and receivables.

items.statement: Net debt negative INR206 crore; cash INR313 crore; raised INR395 crore via preferential issue
items.quote: Moving on in terms of liquidity, we have cash and cash equivalents of INR313 crores. We raised INR395 crores via preferential issue during year for our expansion plans as stated by Manish. The net debt was negative to INR206 crores.

items.statement: ALMM mandates modules from approved list for PSU projects; ALCM effective June 2026 mandates cells from approved list for govt, net metering, open access projects
items.quote: Government has also announced approved list of cell manufacturers that is called ALCM set to be in effect from 1st June of 2026, mandating that all solar photovoltaic modules used in government, net metering and open access renewable energy projects should be used in ALMM and ALCM list.

items.statement: MP incentives: free land (INR1/sqm/yr lease), power at INR4.36/kWh for 5 years, water at INR25/KL, capex subsidy 17% committed, seeking 35% over 7 years
items.quote: First is the 45 -acres land that has been allocated to us is free of cost. That is at a lease rent of INR1 per square meter per year. Second is the subsidy in the electricity. They would be supplying us electricity at a price of INR4.36 paisa for the next 5 years without any change.

items.statement: Transitioning full 4 GW capacity to TOPCon N-Type by Sep 2025; cell line also TOPCon
items.quote: after nearly September 2025 our complete three units should be transferred and operational with the TOPCon N-type of the capacity, the complete around 4 GW and for MP projects all units should be in the TOPCon, the cell manufacturing also in the TOPCon N-type

items.statement: Key EPC customers: KPI Green, RREC, MAHAGENCO; serving DCR and non-DCR segments
items.quote: Some of our market orders that we have backed recently are under ex ecution including customers like KPI Green, RREC and

items.statement: Preferential issue INR395 crore raised for expansion; funds deployed in Unit 3 (operational in 40 days) and balance for cell/strategic investments
items.quote: Yes, these funds are basically raised for our current ongoing capex which will be operational in next 40 days. A 3-gigawatt capacity of solar module manufacturing with 18,000 metric tons of aluminium framing, so which will be operationalized in next 40 days.

items.statement: Module production volume guidance 2,000-2,100 MW for FY26 from own units, no outsourcing
items.quote: FY26, we are expecting from all our units around 2000 to 2100 megawatts.

items.statement: Cell capacity additions 26 GW by FY27 per MNRE; module capacity ~100 GW; ALCM gap to persist 4-5 years supporting margins
items.quote: The MNRE data shows that 26 -gigawatts of cell capacities will come by next year , right. And module capacity will be close to 100 -gigawatts. So, with ALCM in place, there is again a large gap between what is required and what is present.

items.statement: SME to main board migration process starts 11 Oct 2025; completion expected in 45-60 working days
items.quote: The process will start from 11th of October 2025. We will complete our three-year SME board on 10th October 2025 and after immediately next day we start our migration process and we are hopeful that our migration will be completed within 45 to 60 working days after this 11th October.

items.statement: Quarterly results reporting to begin from Q1 FY26 (Apr-Jun quarter)
items.quote: As per our new guidelines, we are bound to follow the quarterly result declaration process. So , from now onwards from April to June quarter, the results will be published as per requirement.

items.statement: BESS manufacturing awaiting central government policy framework; land available in MP (185,000 sqm)
items.quote: For BESS facility, we are still waiting for the policy framework from the government, especially for the manufacturing. Right now, projects are lots of available in the market.

items.statement: Expects sustainable revenue CAGR of 40-45% going forward
items.quote: think a CAGR of between 40%, 45% going forward is something that we would look to sustainably have.

items.statement: Expects steady EBITDA margin expansion, not exponential jump
items.quote: we don't see an exponential jump in our margin expansion, but a more mathematical progression in the way margins will go forward.

items.statement: H2 FY25 EBITDA margin close to 4.4%, above 4.25% expectation
items.quote: the EBITDA margins for second half are close to 4.4%, which is in some sense even above and beyond our expectations of 4.25.

items.statement: FY25 EBITDA margin well above 4%, up from prior year
items.quote: my EBITDA margins have expanded, right? So, we are well above 4% and hopefully we can sustain this going forward.

items.statement: PAT margin improved from 1.9% to 2.2% in FY25
items.quote: Our PAT margins have gone up from 1.9 to about 2.2.

items.statement: Agrochemical demand recovery confirmed
items.quote: Yes, that would be a very correct assessment, sir.

items.statement: No single sector or product dominates revenue; top product <10% of revenue
items.quote: my number one product may not also contribute close to 10% of my overall revenue.

items.statement: Receivable days increased to 70-75 from 40-43; inventory days decreased; working capital rebalancing
items.quote: Our inventory days have gone down. Consequently, one has to see, inventory days have also come down. And we've had exponential growth in the last few months, whereas debtors reflect what a point of time data is.

items.statement: Expects working capital cycles to remain in current ballpark range
items.quote: As we walk this journey, we feel that the numbers that we are witnessing in FY'24-'25 on our balance sheet are working cap cycles will be ballpark in this range.

items.statement: No plant & machinery capex needed; distribution model is asset-light
items.quote: Since we are in distribution, right, we do not require investments in the form of plant and machinery, right?

items.statement: Fundraise under board discussion; working capital needs grow with revenue
items.quote: we are still internally discussing this with the board and the committees. So, on that one, we'll get back to you as and when we do plan that.

items.statement: Claims unparalleled position; no direct peers in specialized derivative distribution
items.quote: we definitely feel we are unpa ralleled right, that's one of which is what we had mentioned in our offer documents as well in the DRHP

items.statement: Addressable market in niche petrochemicals very large; India imports $20-30B liquid petrochemicals
items.quote: The amount of petrochemicals imported in the country would be well into $20, $30 billion. And I'm just speaking about liquid petrochemicals.

items.statement: No speculation or arbitrage; avoids corrupting organizational DNA
items.quote: we are in the business of distribution, we're not in the business of speculation. So, I mean I would never want to even taste the fruits of speculation because once you do that, you get addicted to it.

items.statement: Management available 24/7 to customers; deep roots over three decades
items.quote: Even as being in the helm of the management, Vikas and I are both available to every consumer 24/7 who can call us at any hour for any support that they need.

items.statement: Management guided for 30-40% revenue growth in FY26 and steady growth for the next 3-4 years, with real momentum expected post-2027.
items.quote: And for this year, we'll grow by 30% to 40%, and then there will be a steady growth for next three to four years.

items.statement: Management targets 8-10% net profit margin for FY26 but may accept lower margins to build semiconductor and data center references.
items.quote: So, going forward, we'll be maintaining the margin that we have shown this year. It will be 8% to 10%.

items.statement: Chairman expects at least 40% growth for the next two years, with a different trajectory beyond that.
items.quote: Next two years, at least 40% growth, and beyond that, this is something, it will be something different.

items.statement: Consolidated order book stands at INR 90 crores, split between pharma (50-60 crores) and semicon/electronics/solar (30 crores).
items.quote: Right now the standing is like if I give you a little rundown, the basically thing is current order book that we have in hand is around INR90 crores consolidated between us and Kelvin.

items.statement: Order pipeline is in excess of INR 300 crores across pharma (INR 137 cr), semicon (INR 118 cr), solar (INR 80 cr), and data centers (INR 15.5 cr).
items.quote: To be very honest with you, we have a very robust pipeline which is in excess of about INR300 crores where we have all the sectors within that.

items.statement: Kelvin subsidiary closed FY25 at 7% PAT margin, in line with Fabtech's margins.
items.quote: Yes, it is almost in line with Fabtech. So now last year we have closed at the 7% PAT.

items.statement: Semiconductor project margins are in line with pharmaceutical industry margins, not significantly higher or lower.
items.quote: As far as margin is concerned, the semiconductor is not a very, very special margin project. It is, you know, in line with the pharmaceutical industry.

items.statement: Working capital cycle improved from 173 days in FY24 to 123 days in FY25, a 50-day reduction; management targets further reduction.
items.quote: We have made significant strides beyond these numbers. Now one of the highlights of the year has been the substantial reduction in our working capital cycle, okay, which improved from 173 days in FY '24 to 123 days in FY '25, a major 50 days reduction.

items.statement: No major capex planned unless a large acquisition opportunity arises; otherwise moderate capex for organic growth.
items.quote: If we get a huge competition to acquire, we might. Otherwise, I don't see so far at this moment.

items.statement: Management plans to increase stake in Kelvin beyond 51.33% soon and is evaluating acquisitions in air handling units, automation, or regional cleanroom contractors.
items.quote: Yes, Ravi is smiling. Yes, we are on the way. We are on the way. We are on the way, you're right.

items.statement: First semiconductor order won from CG Semi worth INR 8.4 crores; data center orders from Nexta Data Center (INR 2.5 cr) and NSE (INR 5.45 cr + INR 4 cr pipeline).
items.quote: Name of the customer is declared, I think CG Electronics, right? Anup Munshi: CG Semi. Management: CG Semi and the order value is INE8.4 crores, yes

items.statement: Cleanroom demand driven by pharma, semiconductors, electronics, data centers, solar, and emerging sectors like food, EV batteries, and medical devices; market estimated at INR 25,000-30,000 crores by 2030.
items.quote: And the market, whatever capex is happening in this industry, 3% to 4% is Cleanrooms. So we see a very huge market explosion happening from till 2030, where 25,000 to 30,000 crores of Cleanrooms are up.

items.statement: Project execution timelines compressing from 7-9 months to 4-5 months; investing in robotic welding and factory-level fabrication to reduce site manpower.
items.quote: Nowadays, as you go along, you have very short delivery periods project coming up. Earlier the project which used to finish in 7 to 9 months, now we are required to finish in 4 to 5 months.

items.statement: Addressing labor shortages via university tie-ups and a learning center at facilities to train workforce.
items.quote: Anup over here is tying up with a lot of universities and we are creating up a learning center in our facilities to keep training people.

items.statement: Raw materials (GPSC coil, rockwool, isocyanate, polyol, aluminum) sourced domestically from long-standing vendor relationships; only capex machinery imported occasionally.
items.quote: So, our raw material, entire raw material is indigenous procurement. Okay, sometimes we procure our capex machine from the overseas market. However, our raw material are Indian.

items.statement: Interim dividend of INR 2 per share declared for FY25 as a gesture of appreciation, not a necessity.
items.quote: We also announced an interim dividend of INR2 per share as a gesture of appreciation to our long-term shareholders.

items.statement: Company is under-leveraged and enjoys strong banking partner confidence.
items.quote: And financially, we are under-leveraged. We continue to enjoy the confidence of our banking partners.

items.statement: Business spans modular partitions, doors, risers, terminal boxes, walkable ceilings, AHUs (via Advantek), and HVAC/ducting/insulation/chillers through Kelvin.
items.quote: We manufacture modular partitions. We manufacture cleanroom doors, return risers, terminal boxes. We do walkable fall ceilings. And we also have investment in Advantek where we manufacture air handling units.

items.statement: Key differentiators: in-house design, manufacturing of critical components, pan-India project management, and domain expertise with pharma professionals and R&D team.
items.quote: We are not just contractors. We are designers ourselves of cleanrooms and pharma projects. We have manufacturing of critical components within the group and we have project management team stationed in Pan-India and internationally also.

items.statement: Return on Capital (ROC) improved to 22.8% in FY25 from 15.76% in FY24.
items.quote: Our ROC improved to about 22.8%, which was up from 15.76% in the previous year, which underlines our focus on disciplined capital allocation and high return projects.

items.statement: Labor shortages identified as a key industry challenge; mitigation via training center and automation.
items.quote: The challenge will come in the entire industry with labor issues happening, with a lot of labor shortages. And that is also what we're trying to mitigate.

items.statement: Regulatory expansion (e.g., diapers, contact lenses, Ayurvedic medicines, blood bags, EV batteries) mandating cleanroom manufacturing, broadening addressable market.
items.quote: Many of, very often earlier, people used to think cleanroom means cleanroom in the normal sense of the word. But cleanroom was a highly technical room. So this is the kind of industry that we are.

items.statement: Project management team stationed internationally; no specific export revenue or FX details disclosed.
items.quote: We have manufacturing of critical components within the group and we have project management team stationed in Pan-India and internationally also.

items.statement: Management emphasizes annualized growth over quarterly results; focuses on long-term value creation, consolidation, and reference building in semicon/data centers.
items.quote: We are not building a company that chases short-term wins. Our philosophy is centered around creating sustainable, compounding value.

items.statement: SOP for assembled camshaft greenfield project expected by Q3 next financial year
items.quote: we are expecting that SOP begins by Q3 of financial -- next financial year.

items.statement: Capex for assembled camshaft project is INR40 crores plus INR40 crores for plant and building
items.quote: The capex for the specific projects that we are talking about is around INR40 crores. In addition to that, there is the plant and the building and so on that is an additional INR40 crores or so.

items.statement: New greenfield plant built for 10 lines; assembled camshaft project will use one line
items.quote: that plant, of course, is built for much more this one project. It is built for 10 lines.

items.statement: New camshaft orders secured up to 2030 and beyond; nominations include resourcing from China to India
items.quote: PCL continues to be profitable at stand-alone level and has new orders for camshafts up to 2030 and beyond.

items.statement: Assembled camshaft EBITDA margins expected similar to machined camshaft at 20-25%
items.quote: Think EBITDA margins would be similar to a machine camshaft, let's say, so around 20%, 25% EBITDA margins.

items.statement: EV demand slower than anticipated in both India and Europe due to supply chain variability, infrastructure, and policy uncertainty
items.quote: However, ramp-up of demand for these e- vehicles has been slower than anticipated and which is also in line with most other OEMs experience in India.

items.statement: MFT diversifying into non-engine components (HVAC, chassis, brake parts); MEMCO automotive concentration reduced from 95% to 65-70%
items.quote: We are doing some components for the heating and ventilation business. Again, machined parts, of course, we continue to do what we know best, but we are div ersifying the industry

items.statement: LOIs from several fleet owners for EV retrofitment; co-developing electrified heavy truck powertrain with customer for specialized application
items.quote: We do have a letter of intent from several customers, and these are larger numbers also.

items.statement: Camshaft business benefiting from OEM resourcing from China to India; participating in all new engine platforms (diesel, petrol, flex fuel, hybrids)
items.quote: some of these nominations that we have got from customers, have been a clear resourcing from China to India. And we have been the beneficiary of that resourcing.

items.statement: No interest cost or significant depreciation in EMOSS; EBITDA flows almost directly to PAT
items.quote: beyond the EBITDA number, there is not much. There is no -- there is really no interest cost or hardly any depreciation. So this EBITDA number almost flows down to the PAT level.

items.statement: Internal cash and deposits (INR300-400 crores) to fund assembled camshaft capex, solar capacity, and potential acquisitions
items.quote: we are using this internal generation as well as deposits that we have on our balance sheet for additional capex that I mentioned before.

items.statement: Impairment provision of INR73 crores on foreign subsidiary investment (mainly EMOSS) as prudent practice; not a write-off, may reverse in 1-2 years
items.quote: The impairment of investment is done purely as a prudent accounting practice and is only taken as a provision and not a write-off.

items.statement: Compensation recovery of INR35.6 crores from customer for underutilized capacity (fixed cost compensation); one-time, not recurring
items.quote: This exceptional item includes a compensation recovery from a customer of INR35.6 crores positive and an impairment of investment in a foreign subsidiary amounting to INR73 crores.

items.statement: Government intervention favoring hybrids over pure EVs adding to demand uncertainty in India
items.quote: Of late, there has been a government intervention regarding more hybrid vehicles rather than pure EVs as well. So there is a lot of question marks, which need to be addressed.

items.statement: EMOSS Europe at EBITDA breakeven after scaling down from two sites to one and reducing manpower; revenue dropped from prior years
items.quote: Slightly, I would say we are just at the breakeven line at an EBITDA level because obviously, the revenue has scaled down compared to, let's say, 2 years ago or 1 year ago.

items.statement: Standalone revenue INR147.5 crores (+3% QoQ), EBITDA margin 18%; consolidated revenue INR200.7 crores (+2.7% QoQ), EBITDA margin 18%, PAT margin 20%
items.quote: total income for this quarter increased by 3% to INR147.47 crores, and EBITDA margin was 18%.

items.statement: EV retrofitment business is working capital intensive due to component sourcing and assembly model
items.quote: Very minimal capex is required with basically a working capital-intensive business because it is sourcing of a variety of components and then building and then selling forward.

items.statement: EMOSS manpower scaled down according to demand; manufacturing sites reduced from two to one
items.quote: manpower, which has been scaled down according to the demand. So yes, of course, we try to stay above the line and stay in the positive.

items.statement: MCA investigation: all required information shared with authorities; no final order yet, process ongoing
items.quote: I think as far as all the information that needed to be shared with the authorities has been shared. So there is no further investment.

items.statement: FY26 segment growth targets: bag making/pouch making and extrusion 10-15%, packaging 30-40%
items.quote: We have always said that if we look at our three revenue streams then ba g making, pouch making as well as our ex trusion is likely to grow at between 10 and 15% going forward, while we have always maintained that packaging will grow much faster. We're looking at between 30 and 40% growth

items.statement: Order book stood at Rs 74 crore as of March 31, including Rs 30 crore deferred sales
items.quote: As on 31st March, our order books stood at about 74 crores that also included deferred sales of 30 crores.

items.statement: Approximately Rs 30 crore of sales deferred from Q4 FY25 to Q1 FY26, mostly packaging machines for US market
items.quote: The quantum of deferred sales is approximately 30 CR of which about 23 CR was for packaging. And balance was for converting.

items.statement: EBITDA margins around 20% are sustainable and may improve with operating leverage
items.quote: Current EBITDA margins of ±20% are sustainable and may possibly improve. In fact, with our scale of operation growing further since operating expenses aren't expected to rise proportionately.

items.statement: Full-year margin expansion of ~2% driven by pricing decisions, design changes, and higher-margin barrier extrusion lines
items.quote: The margins actually expanded by about 2% if we compare the entire year. And it is 2% margin expansion was on account of two things.

items.statement: No in-house manufacturing; capacity expansion limited to adding assembly space on existing campus as needed
items.quote: We do not have a machine shop and we do not manufacture anything in house, so as far as capacity expansion is concerned, basically we might just need more space to assemble machines that we manufacture and we will definitely try and add that space in our existing campus as and when required.

items.statement: Actively seeking inorganic growth in flexible packaging: targeting filling systems, secondary/tertiary packaging, flow wrap machines, especially in Europe
items.quote: We are looking at inorganic growth opportunities, particularly in the ambit of packaging, and that too flexible packaging. So, when you start looking at flexible packaging, there are various aspects to flexible packaging.

items.statement: Will continue equitable dividend distribution; retaining cash as war chest for inorganic growth
items.quote: On dividend front, we will continue with our past track record of equitable dividend distribution. And as I said just now, we are trying to build a war chest that will help us with our in inorganic growth plan

items.statement: No FX hedging; low import content vs export revenue provides natural hedge
items.quote: the question is do we hedge foreign exchange? The answer is no. We do not hedge. Lakshminarayanan: OK. Apurva Kane: Because our import content is very low as compared to our export revenue, we get automatic advantage of hedging and we don't have to do that separately

items.statement: Pricing kept stable; cost controlled through design innovation and procurement rather than pass-through
items.quote: Mamata is known for keeping its pricing very stable. We try not to disturb pricing as far as possible unless we are forced to do it. The cost of the machine, as I mentioned earlier, we believe very strongly that costing is inherent part of design itself and therefore we can by innovation control the pass-through design as well as through purchase.

items.statement: Top 10 customers contribute only 20% of revenue; customer concentration low and changes annually
items.quote: Top 10% of our customers, this is a stated fact, top 10 customers of Ma mata contribute only 20% of our revenue

items.statement: Repeat business accounts for 50-55% of revenue
items.quote: It is around fifty 50-55% is repeat business

items.statement: Packaging machines patented for recyclable films; near-term opportunity of 12-20 machines in 20-24 weeks in India; US/EU machines already running recyclable films
items.quote: Absolutely near-term addressable opportunities that time we are looking at is between 12 and 20 machines in coming 20-24 weeks. It's an opportunity where we are actively pursuing this these opportunities and we are talking to customer.

items.statement: Dispatched 238 machines in FY25 (207 bag/pouch, 10 extrusion, 21 packaging) vs 256 in FY24
items.quote: So, last year we have dispatched 238 machines overall. Lakshminarayanan: OK. 238. Apurva Kane: Yeah, of which 207 were for pack making and pouch making. There were 10 machines for extrusion. These are complete machines, by the way, as I explained earlier. Yeah, these are complete plants. And then packaging machines, we have delivered 21

items.statement: Extrusion revenue 71% export in FY25; packaging sold only in India and US/Canada currently, expanding to Middle East, Africa, Europe
items.quote: For extrusion and bag making and pouch making in terms of revenue, 71% of the revenue was generated from exports in the financial year that we closed, FY25. As far as packaging is concerned, we are either selling machines in India or in USA and Canada, we have not yet tendered the rest of the world and that is the process that we have taken up now and hopefully that is something that will deliver

items.statement: Hired Rajashekar as President for packaging division growth; previously at Kennametal, Mettler-Toledo, Markem-Imaje
items.quote: Mr. Rajashekar has already joined us as our President, with specific emphasis on growth delivery of packaging division, so he has already joined us and he is in process of doing exactly what we want to be done.

items.statement: Main US risk is broader economic slowdown/recession, not tariffs; machines are high-end capital goods bought on technical merit
items.quote: The main risk arising from current situation would be a broader U.S. economic slowdown or a recession which would indirectly impact demand. At present, we do not see any direct adverse impact on our business.

items.statement: Granted patents in India, EU, USA for sealing mechanisms enabling recyclable film use on packaging machines
items.quote: We have given press releases this year earlier where we have been granted certain patents for our sealing mechanisms that we have on our packaging machines, which would allow our customers to use our machines to run recyclable films, so we now have patented technology that is available for the company.

items.statement: Indian machinery perception challenge globally; Mamata rated 6-7/10, Indian industry 5/10
items.quote: I would like to say that if we are talking of Mam ata, just Mamata machinery, we are at 6-7. If we are talking of overall Indian industry, I would put it at 5

items.statement: Packaging growth drivers: Indian snack industry growing ~28%, packaged food necessity post-COVID, double-digit industry growth for 3+ years, leveraging existing 80-country presence for bag/pouch machines
items.quote: For example, snack industry, packaged snack industry in India is growing at rate of about 28% and therefore more machinery is needed to package food. items.quote: Yesterday we checked with all the shipping line. Only it has impact on the Jebel Ali Port where we don't have much exposure. So, till time, we don't see any impact.

items.statement: No shipment disruptions from Iran conflict; shipments smooth and regular as not exporting to Iran
items.quote: No, no. That is stuck up because Iran war and the shippers are not shipping to Iran because of not getting their insurance. So, we are not exporting to Iran. So, our shipments are smooth, regular going.

items.statement: No material financial impact foreseen on cash flow or future earnings of the businesses
items.quote: Further, would like to reiterate that we don't foresee any material financial impact on the cash flow or future earning of the businesses.

items.statement: Two soya meal processing facilities in India and Uganda; utilization depends on competitiveness
items.quote: So, we have two facilities for processing soya meal , one in India and one in Uganda. It depends from where we are competitive. So, we keep using the facility of Uganda and India.

items.statement: FY26 revenue target of INR 60-65 crores with EBITDA margin around 44-45% and PAT margin not less than 30%
items.quote: And revenue, we arc expecting o cross anything between 60 to 65. That is what we are targeting.

items.statement: IPO proceeds of INR 40 crores to be deployed over ~18 months mainly for branch openings, advertising, branding and acquisitions
items.quote: So as mentioned in the DRHP, it will take approximately 18 months for us to deploy the entire funds, because most of these funds would be deployed in opening the branches, as well as advertisements and branding exercises.

items.statement: Plan to open 6-8 more branches in FY26 (3 already opened in Surat, Ahmedabad, Delhi), targeting 18 total branches; also launching video counseling within 60 days
items.quote: Target for this year would be an additional 6 to § more branches. 3 we have alrcady opened, right, 6 to 8 is something we are going to open

items.statement: In advanced discussions to acquire an Indian college (nursing/engineering) and a regional immigration consultant; acquisition is one-time use of IPO funds
items.quote: We are in very advanced stage of basically acquiring acquisition of colleges and one of the broker is one of the immigration consultant as well.

items.statement: EBITDA margin 44.5% in FY25 (up 185 bps YoY); PAT margin 35.9% (up 408 bps); management expects to sustain ~40% EBITDA and not less than 30% PAT margin
items.quote: EBITDA margin stood at 44.5%, an expansion of 185 basis points over FY '24. Net profit stood at INR13.1 crores, up 21.5% year-on-year, with a PAT margin of 35.9%, reflecting a margin improvement of 408 basis points year-on-year.

items.statement: Advertising and marketing spend expected to be ~20% of revenue, the single largest expense line
items.quote: 20%, close to 20%. 20% of the revenue, yes.

items.statement: India outbound student market ~US$30bn in 2023, projected 10%+ CAGR to 2030; over 1.3mn Indian students abroad in 2024
items.quote: As a result, the Indian outbound student market reached an estimated value of US330 billion in 2023, and is projected to grow at a CAGR of over 10% through 2030.

items.statement: Revenue mix: ~60-70% from Canada, 20-30% from UK, Germany, US combined; ~3,000-3,500 students placed annually
items.quote: See, I'l tell you Canada s still 60, 70% of our revermie. So rest all other are 30% of the revemue, 20% to 30% of the revenue.

items.statement: Receivables spike at year-end due to January intake; commission collection cycle 90-180 days; debtors-to-sales ratio rose to 35.9% in FY25 from 14.6% in FY24
items.quote: The commission cycle ranges from like maybe 90 to 180 days.

items.statement: Company is debt-free after repaying all borrowings in FY25
items.quote: Yes, yes, it is a purcly debt-free company.

items.statement: Headcount grew from ~110 (Mar-24) to ~160 (Mar-25) to 175+ currently; employee benefit expense fell in H2 FY25 due to shift from fixed to variable pay and trimming non-performers
items.quote: So majorly, it was related to shifiing from fixed salarics to the variable commissions and all, right. We definitely have reduced or rather taken a call in trimming down those cxpenses.

items.statement: Revenue >90% from university commissions (first-year tuition); adding pathway programs, visa processing, AI-based assessments, loan tie-ups (Credelia, SBI, Axis)
items.quote: So, the major revenue income is the commissions from the universitics and colleges which we get for recruiting students for them. That is the highest, like you can say above 90% would be that only.

items.statement: Major listed competitor is IDP (125 branches, Australian govt-backed); Canam larger than Landmark; Landmark market share ~2-3% of consultant-channel students
items.quote: And so I don't think we are - so as Jasmeet ji has said that our number is we send almost 3,000 to 3,500 students a year, right. And so the number -- so we are not more than 2% to 3%.

items.statement: Three-year CAGR: revenue 27%, EBITDA 47%, PAT 49%
items.quote: Our three-year CAGR for revenue is 27%, EBITDA is 47%, and PAT is 49%.

items.statement: Global expansion planned with upcoming offices in Canada and Dubai; exclusive agreements with 4-6 universities, direct agreements with 150+ universities
items.quote: the company is also looking at broadening its global foofprint with upcoming offices in Canada and Dubai.

items.statement: Canada tightened immigration rules but still targets ~400k-450k students annually; US visa appointments paused ~3 weeks due to fraud concerns; management engaging embassies to verify document authenticity
items.quote: They have stringent laws, definitely. And they want only quality students as all other countries are looking at quality students, but as per the numbers, they're looking still at 400,000, like 4 Iakh students every year.

items.statement: AI disruption risk acknowledged; developing AI portal, app, and AI call center to automate lead qualification and reduce call-center costs
items.quote: So but we are also combining those Al formalities into our website and promoting, we are making an app, which will be helpful to the students. So definitely, so Al will impact our business also in future
